If you hold gold as a hedge, earning income on it makes that allocation more useful.

A quick follow-up on @enhanced_defi, which I covered previously:

Its latest completed gold-vault cycle, settled on November 26, realized 5.3% APR from option premiums. Across eight completed cycles, depositors have received $3,167.94 in net premiums.

Here’s how it works:

• Deposit PAXG, tokenized gold.
• The vault sells 14-day covered calls to institutional market makers.
• Buyers pay a premium for gold’s gains above an agreed price at expiry.
• You collect the income in USDC or compound it into more PAXG.

For a crypto-heavy portfolio, you could use this on part of your gold allocation: diversify your exposure while earning premiums that cushion some of gold’s downside.

Gold can still fall, and gains above the agreed price are capped at expiry. The 5.3% figure is annualized, changes each cycle, and isn’t guaranteed.

That’s the appeal for me: keeping gold exposure while turning some of its volatility into income.

text:
is there a harness that would let Opus solve RH? Perhaps. What about 1017? Doubt. 
But crucially, this exponential growth in capabilities we see is a process of internalizing the effective harness – the extended scaffolding models develop at test time in RL, analogous to "skills" users design in their private setups. Environment feedback defines priors in the weights. So each new generation can one-shot 80% of what the previous one needed a complex "harness" for to do in reasonable time; you see Fable 5.Y+1 conjure the most majestic Pelicans in a fraction of the time it took Fable 5.Y and with less thrashing.  At that point the "harness" used then becomes a burden and in the worst case sets an unneeded ceiling.
What, then, to do with harnesses, skills, plugins? What about DSH, CC, and the long-term strategy of model-harness co-design? Essentially by construction, you cannot optimize a model to use complex, high-leverage skills that will be relevant at its deployment. If you know them well enough to develop some high quality "skill", you might as well just build an RL environment that trains the model to know relevant primitives and one-shot this task, you distill the necessary metis into the circuits.

In essence, the only useful robust skill you can optimize for at this stage, before some meaningful continual learning, is meta-harnessing, the generic ability to build efficient tools for a given task at runtime. Any skill-library-heavy system will collapse.

This isn't anything mind-blowing, just a rant as I'm falling asleep, and a bit of bitterness because I really wanted to develop a useful library for agents. Vygotsky had said it all in like 1932. For me, the novelty is mostly the intuition of how exactly the clearly mediocre generalization and localized stupidity of models coexist with these asinine generational jumps. 

 I'd guess this logic only breaks down if you're severely limited on model scaling.

P.S. The same logic applies to the utility of skills embedded in human users. Thus, humans need to learn to retreat to ever higher ground.

text:
$325K+ in Buyback Firepower Is Starting to Come Together as $MONTRA Value Gets Gradually Repriced by the Market

0x063f7cc5339f92a5fd7baf3d22233044fda1f327 

I believe MONTRA is more interesting this time than it was during the previous round. The change is not simply that platform trading volume continues to expand. More importantly, the buyback mechanism introduced earlier is now being executed at a much larger scale, with three independent sources of buyback funding emerging: protocol fees, historical Treasury reserves, and Creator Fees generated by MONTRA's own trading pool.

This means MONTRA's value capture is moving from a theoretical mechanism toward actual execution. It is no longer just a Launchpad memecoin riding the hype surrounding Elysium's mainnet launch. It now has actual platform trading activity, fee revenue, and token burns supporting its narrative.

However, growing platform metrics do not mean every newly launched token can generate sustained trading activity. Trading volume over the past 24 hours has also declined noticeably. The fundamentals are improving, but not every metric is moving in the same direction.

Looking at the platform first, according to the latest website data at the time of writing, Montra has reached $70.97M in cumulative trading volume, approximately 786,862 cumulative trades, and around 81,255 launched tokens. Total fees have reached approximately $1.12M, of which around $832.9K has been paid to creators and holders, while Montra itself has generated approximately $286.7K in protocol revenue.

Compared with the previous snapshot, cumulative trading volume has increased by approximately 19.5%, from $59.37M. Total trades have increased by approximately 39.5%, from 564,258, while the number of launched tokens has grown from around 62,200 to 81,255.

The platform has already reached meaningful scale. The key question is no longer whether it can attract projects to launch, but whether it can turn those launches into sustained trading activity.

There is one detail worth paying attention to: 24-hour trading volume is now approximately $13.92M, with around 206,434 trades, significantly lower than the $32.84M and approximately 334,763 trades recorded in our previous analysis. This shows that cumulative business activity is still expanding, but short-term trading momentum has cooled. Since Montra's business model depends on trading fees, the next thing to watch is whether trading volume can stabilize rather than simply focusing on the cumulative number of launched tokens.

Montra positions itself as a core asset issuance platform on Elysium, powered by Uniswap v4. It uses independent liquidity pools without the traditional Bonding Curve or graduation process. Tokens can be traded from their very first block after launch. This reduces the barriers to issuance and trading, allowing the platform to attract a large number of creators quickly.

However, the same model can also lead to an influx of low-quality tokens. Having more than 81,255 launched assets does not mean there are 81,255 assets with meaningful market demand. Growth in the Elysium ecosystem following mainnet is Montra's most immediate external catalyst, while its ability to maintain its position as a major asset issuance platform will determine how much of that ecosystem activity it can capture.

What really matters is its fee distribution mechanism.

Montra receives a fixed 0.4% of trading volume as protocol revenue from every trade. Of this amount, 70% is used for automatic MONTRA buybacks and burns, while the remaining 30% goes into the Treasury.

In other words, for every $100 in platform trading volume, approximately $0.28 goes toward buybacks and burns, while $0.12 goes into the Treasury.

The more active the platform becomes, the more protocol revenue it generates and, theoretically, the more capital becomes available for buybacks. This is MONTRA's core value-capture mechanism and what differentiates it from a typical Launchpad memecoin.

More importantly, this mechanism now has actual execution records.

According to the official Buyback page, cumulative buybacks and burns have reached 10,197,435 MONTRA, representing approximately 1.02% of the final 1 billion token supply.

Of this amount, approximately 3,102,464 MONTRA has been burned through automatic protocol buybacks, representing around 0.310% of the supply. Another 7,094,970 MONTRA has been burned through manual Treasury buybacks, representing approximately 0.709%.

This means buybacks are no longer just an allocation percentage written in the documentation. They are already generating real on-chain buying activity and reducing the circulating supply.

The first source of funding is automatic protocol buybacks.

Automatic buybacks went live on November 10. According to the website, the mechanism has received approximately 520.78 HYPE and 40,487.49 KNTQ, worth around $49,986. It has already spent approximately 84.88 HYPE and 37,539.64 KNTQ across around 141 transactions, burning approximately 3.10M MONTRA.

Currently, another 435.89 HYPE and 2,947.85 KNTQ are waiting to be deployed.

The execution route is also worth noting: HYPE is first exchanged for KNTQ, which is then used to buy MONTRA through its own trading pool. This means the buyback mechanism not only creates buying pressure for MONTRA but also generates actual usage demand for KNTQ.

The second source is historical Treasury reserves.

Previously, protocol revenue primarily went into the Treasury, with a portion reserved for manual buybacks. According to the website, approximately 2,156.99 HYPE was historically allocated for this purpose.

The team has already executed 600 HYPE in buybacks through four transactions, burning approximately 7.095M MONTRA. Another 1,556.99 HYPE remains in the Treasury reserve, valued at approximately $109K on the website.

Compared with the smaller buybacks seen previously, these consecutive large transactions are more convincing. They demonstrate that the team is beginning to convert historically accumulated funds into actual token purchases and burns, rather than simply announcing a buyback plan.

The third source, and arguably the most easily overlooked, is Creator Fees generated by MONTRA's own trading pool.

According to the website, MONTRA's own trading pool has generated approximately 939,702 KNTQ, valued at around $287.1K. Of this amount, 70%, or approximately 657,791 KNTQ worth around $201K, has been allocated for MONTRA buybacks and burns. The remaining 281,910 KNTQ, worth approximately $86.1K, is allocated to community development.

However, these funds are still awaiting collection and should not be treated as completed buybacks.

The project also explains that when these Creator Fees are claimed, the corresponding MONTRA held in the liquidity pool will undergo another type of burn that is not classified as a buyback. This amount should not be double-counted with the 10.197M MONTRA already recorded as buyback burns.

Together, these three funding channels make up the $325K+ Buyback Firepower announced by Montra: approximately $28K+ in pending automatic buyback funds, around $109K+ in historical Treasury HYPE reserves, and approximately $188K+ in buyback allocations from MONTRA's own Creator Fees.

It is important to distinguish these figures. The $325K+ represents a combination of funds and allocations from different sources, not money that has already been fully converted into market buy orders.

Still, it shows that MONTRA is no longer relying on a single buyback source. It now has a buyback structure supported by protocol revenue, historical reserves, and fees generated by its own trading pool.

The token supply structure also deserves another look.

MONTRA initially launched with a supply of 4 billion tokens, of which 3 billion were burned at launch, leaving a final total supply of 1 billion.

Of the remaining supply, 60%, or 600 million tokens, entered circulation from day one; 25%, or 250 million, was allocated to airdrops; and 15%, or 150 million, was reserved for operations, listings, and market making.

Cumulative buyback burns now account for approximately 1.02% of the final supply, a significant increase compared with the previous website record of 208.5K tokens.

However, the 40% allocated to airdrops and operations still deserves attention. The specific vesting, locking, and future distribution schedules have not yet been fully clarified. This means buybacks are reducing supply, but their impact cannot be evaluated without considering potential new circulating supply.

What the market is betting on now is no longer simply whether Montra can become Elysium's leading Launchpad. The bigger question is whether it can convert platform trading activity into sustainable demand for MONTRA.

The next potential upside catalysts fall into three areas.

First, continued growth in the Elysium ecosystem could bring more launches, trading activity, and protocol revenue to Montra.

Second, the remaining Treasury reserves and allocated Creator Fees could gradually be deployed, converting funds currently held by the protocol into actual market buying pressure.

Third, continued trading activity in MONTRA's own pool could generate additional Creator Fees, creating another buyback source beyond ordinary protocol fees.

KNTQ, as the primary quote asset, may also benefit from additional demand generated through these buyback routes. However, the value-capture mechanisms of MONTRA and KNTQ should not be confused.

The risks are concentrated in three areas.

First is trading quality and retention. More than 81,000 tokens have been launched, but the low barrier to issuance means many assets may struggle to generate sustained trading demand. If the initial excitement surrounding mainnet fades, platform fees could decline accordingly.

Second is the actual execution of buybacks. Pending automatic buyback funds, Treasury reserves, and Creator Fee allocations do not equal completed token burns. Their actual execution needs to be verified through subsequent on-chain records.

Third is supply pressure. Airdrop and operational allocations account for 40% of the final supply. If their release schedule does not match the pace of buybacks, they could offset part of the supply reduction. In addition, buybacks depend on KNTQ liquidity, and insufficient depth in the quote asset could reduce execution efficiency.

My conclusion is that MONTRA's fundamentals have genuinely improved compared with our previous analysis.

Platform business activity continues to grow, but the most important development is that buybacks have moved from an expected mechanism to actual execution. Cumulative fees have reached approximately $1.12M, automatic protocol buybacks are operational, the historical Treasury has already executed 600 HYPE worth of purchases, and MONTRA's own trading pool has accumulated approximately $201K in dedicated buyback allocations.

Having three funding sources operating simultaneously makes MONTRA's value-capture model much more tangible than before.

What makes me bullish on MONTRA is not simply that it has become a sizable Launchpad on Elysium, but that it is beginning to establish the ability to generate recurring revenue from ecosystem trading activity and convert part of that revenue into a reduction in token supply.

However, I would not automatically translate $325K+ in buyback firepower into future price appreciation. What ultimately determines its valuation is whether the platform can continue generating revenue and how much of that revenue actually turns into on-chain buying pressure.

The most important thing to watch next is not how many more tokens Montra can launch. It is whether trading volume can stabilize at a higher level after the initial excitement surrounding Elysium's mainnet launch fades, whether all three buyback channels can continue operating, and whether the pace of buybacks can outpace potential new token supply entering circulation.

If Montra can retain traders rather than simply attract token creators, MONTRA has a real opportunity to evolve from a new-chain Launchpad narrative into an ecosystem asset supported by actual platform economic activity.

The Value of $Montra as Elysium's Core Launchpad Is Being Priced In

0x063f7cc5339f92a5fd7baf3d22233044fda1f327 

The market is pricing in MONTRA's position as a core Launchpad on Elysium, along with its value-capture mechanism that channels platform trading activity into MONTRA buybacks and burns.

This is not simply a memecoin rally driven by a new chain launch. Montra already has actual platform trading activity, fee revenue, and an operating buyback mechanism behind it. However, rapid platform growth does not mean every newly launched token will generate sustained trading activity, and MONTRA's actual burn volume remains relatively small.

The platform has already reached a meaningful scale. As of the time of writing, the latest website data shows approximately $32.84M in 24-hour trading volume, across 334,763 trades. Cumulative trading volume has reached $59.37M, with approximately 564,258 trades in total. Around 62,200 tokens have been launched, including approximately 22,514 in the latest 24-hour period.

Cumulative fees have reached approximately $1.03M, of which around $789.3K has been paid to creators and holders, while approximately $240.3K goes to Montra as protocol revenue.

This is one of MONTRA's core advantages: it does not need every newly launched project to succeed. As long as the platform continues generating trading activity, it can collect fees. Elysium opened its public mainnet on November 9, and Montra sits directly at the center of the ecosystem's asset issuance activity. The influx of users, projects, and trading activity following mainnet is its most immediate external catalyst.

What really determines MONTRA's value is its fee distribution mechanism.

The platform charges fees on every trade, with the specific fee rate set by creators at launch. According to the fee structure displayed on the website, Montra receives a fixed 0.4% of trading volume. Of that amount, 70% is used to buy back and burn MONTRA in its own liquidity pool, while the remaining 30% goes into the protocol treasury.

In other words, for every $100 traded, approximately $0.28 goes toward MONTRA buybacks and burns, while $0.12 goes into the treasury.

Earlier, all protocol revenue went into the treasury. The mechanism has now shifted to 70% buybacks and 30% treasury allocation. This creates a direct link between platform trading volume and the token's supply: more trading activity generates more protocol revenue, which theoretically leads to more buyback capital.

There is another detail worth noting: KNTQ is Montra's primary liquidity pair. The quote assets generated through platform trading, as well as the assets used to buy back MONTRA, can create additional demand for KNTQ. So this mechanism may benefit both MONTRA buybacks and KNTQ usage. However, their value-capture mechanisms are different, and MONTRA burns should not be treated as equivalent to KNTQ buybacks.

The official buyback page already records actual execution: approximately 208.5K MONTRA burned, representing around 0.0052% of the initial supply. Cumulative spending has reached approximately 3.821 HYPE and 1,690 KNTQ.

The page also shows another 48.665 HYPE and 5,011 KNTQ waiting to be deployed for future purchases, with funds released into the buyback pool according to daily limits for each quote asset.

This confirms that the buyback mechanism is already operating. However, it is important to distinguish between protocol fees collected, funds allocated for buybacks, and the actual amount of tokens purchased and burned. The current burn percentage remains very small. What matters next is whether the funds waiting to be deployed can consistently turn into on-chain buying pressure, rather than simply focusing on the 70% allocation.

The team's background is another positive factor. The project lead previously served as CTO of Cashcat and was also involved in the Letscashfun Launchpad on Robinhood Chain. He is now leading a team of approximately 15 people building Montra.

The team has gone through the product cycles of Cashcat and Letscash, giving it some hands-on experience in the Launchpad sector. For this type of platform, launching tokens is not particularly difficult. The real challenge is consistently attracting creators, maintaining liquidity, and retaining traders. Previous experience provides a foundation, but Montra still needs to prove that it can maintain its market share.

The market is primarily betting on three things: whether Montra can become Elysium's core asset issuance platform; whether mainnet adoption can translate into sustained trading activity and fee growth; and whether protocol revenue can be converted into long-term supply reduction through buybacks.

The next upside catalysts revolve around these factors: Elysium mainnet attracting more users and projects, Montra expanding its market share, creator and holder incentives attracting more projects, and protocol fees growing alongside trading volume, leading to larger buybacks.

If these metrics continue improving together, MONTRA's valuation could gradually shift from being based on a new-chain Launchpad narrative to being supported by actual platform business activity.

However, the number of tokens launched does not directly reflect project quality. More than 62,200 tokens have been launched, but that does not mean they all have sustained trading demand.

Montra does not use a Bonding Curve or a graduation process. This lowers the barrier to launching tokens, but also makes it easier for low-quality projects to enter the platform, potentially fragmenting attention and liquidity.

The metrics worth watching are the number of active tokens, trader retention, the performance of projects after launch, and the proportion of bot-driven trading activity.

Another risk is the gap between platform revenue and actual token burns. The approximately $240.3K in protocol revenue displayed on the website does not mean all of those funds have already been used for buybacks. The current burn percentage is still only around 0.0052% of the initial supply.

If trading volume declines as the excitement surrounding mainnet fades, both fee revenue and buybacks will decline accordingly. Montra also faces competition from other Launchpads within Elysium, and its current market position is not guaranteed to last.

My conclusion is that MONTRA's fundamentals are strengthening. The platform business has already reached meaningful scale, and its token value-capture mechanism is operational, but actual burns have not yet caught up with the scale of platform revenue. This will be a key factor in determining whether MONTRA can continue commanding a valuation premium.

What makes me bullish is not simply the number of tokens the platform has launched, but the fact that it is beginning to establish a business model capable of generating recurring revenue from ecosystem trading activity.

As long as Montra can maintain its position as a major asset issuance platform on Elysium and consistently convert trading volume into real fee revenue and buybacks, it has the potential to become a more important platform asset within the ecosystem.

But the question I really want to watch is this: once the initial excitement surrounding Elysium's mainnet launch fades, will creators and traders still actively choose Montra?

The next stage of MONTRA's growth will be determined by whether it can retain trading activity, not just attract new token launches.

BNB Chain Releases New L1 Litepaper Targeting High-Frequency Trading, Payments, Private Finance, and Autonomous AI Agents

BNB Chain released a new L1 litepaper targeting high-frequency trading, payments, private finance, and autonomous AI agents. It will run alongside BNB Smart Chain, retaining BNB as its native token without issuing a new one.

The EVM-compatible L1 separates transaction ordering and execution, uses SubBlocks for preliminary ordering feedback, and reserves block capacity for payments and other designated transactions. Native account abstraction supports passkeys, transaction batching, revocable permissions, and gas sponsorship. Private settlement supports BNB and eligible BEP-20 tokens, alongside partially public application interactions.

A public testnet is in development, parallel EVM execution is planned, and TEE-based ordering protection remains a proposal.

text:
# What If AI Changes the Rules of Cryptography?

I've been thinking about Cassie's latest post about ECC, and I believe this is a topic the crypto industry should take seriously.

Most people talk about AI in terms of productivity, automation, and content generation. But there's another possibility: AI could fundamentally change how quickly humans discover mathematical weaknesses.

Today, a huge part of the digital asset industry still depends on elliptic curve cryptography (ECC).

Bitcoin uses ECDSA and Schnorr signatures based on secp256k1. Ethereum uses secp256k1 for account signatures and BLS signatures in its consensus layer. Other major networks, including BNB Chain, XRP, Avalanche, Solana, Cardano, Polkadot, and TON, also rely on elliptic-curve-based cryptography in important parts of their security architecture.

This is not a small technical detail. It is part of the foundation that protects billions of dollars in digital assets.

To be clear, there is no publicly verified evidence that OpenAI has broken ECC. But AI-assisted mathematical discovery is something we should not underestimate. The concern is not necessarily that AI can magically decrypt everything today. It is that AI may accelerate the discovery of weaknesses that traditional research would take much longer to uncover.

This is one reason I'm interested in Quilibrium.

Its cryptographic architecture is different from simply copying the standard blockchain security model. According to its official documentation, Q uses BLS48-581 signatures for ownership and authorization, Ed448 for key management, zero-knowledge proofs, multi-party computation, and privacy-preserving data structures.

But here's an important distinction: Quilibrium still uses ECC in certain areas. Its official documentation acknowledges this. The project uses higher bit-strength parameters than typical networks and describes a migration path toward post-quantum algorithms such as PICNIC, supported by flexible proof systems like MPC-in-the-head.

That doesn't mean Q is already quantum-proof, or immune to a general ECC breakthrough. It means the architecture has considered cryptographic migration as part of its design.

I think this is the bigger lesson.

The next generation of infrastructure cannot simply assume that today's cryptographic standards will remain secure forever.

AI is changing software development. It may also change cybersecurity and cryptography.

**The projects worth watching are not just those building faster blockchains, but those thinking about what happens when the security assumptions behind today's internet stop being reliable.**

For me, Quilibrium is one of those projects worth watching.

Not because it has solved every problem, but because it is trying to build for a different security future.

*Research, not fear. Verify, don't speculate.*

text:
If you hold gold as a hedge, earning income on it makes that allocation more useful.

A quick follow-up on @enhanced_defi, which I covered previously:

Its latest completed gold-vault cycle, settled on November 26, realized 5.3% APR from option premiums. Across eight completed cycles, depositors have received $3,167.94 in net premiums.

Here’s how it works:

• Deposit PAXG, tokenized gold.
• The vault sells 14-day covered calls to institutional market makers.
• Buyers pay a premium for gold’s gains above an agreed price at expiry.
• You collect the income in USDC or compound it into more PAXG.

For a crypto-heavy portfolio, you could use this on part of your gold allocation: diversify your exposure while earning premiums that cushion some of gold’s downside.

Gold can still fall, and gains above the agreed price are capped at expiry. The 5.3% figure is annualized, changes each cycle, and isn’t guaranteed.

That’s the appeal for me: keeping gold exposure while turning some of its volatility into income.

"I can survive without having Einstein, but having a Mensa level AI is ok."

@ivanfioravanti sent me that in a DM today. I'm up in the mountains this weekend and I've been thinking about that ever since.

- Einstein = the smartest AI models out there (frontier models, built by big labs, you can only use them their way)

- Mensa = smart open-weight and opensource AI models that anyone can download and run on their own computer.

Not as smart as Einstein but close (the best ones are ~4 months behind) and you don't even need an internet connection. Some don't even need a powerful computer (they run fine on a laptop).

"AI should be governed democratically" @DarioAmodei 

"Never give up self-determination" @DarioAmodei

I couldn't agree more... BUT while the best AI models are owned by a handful of companies (and governments can force them offline, one of the best models in the world went offline for everyone on earth for almost 3 weeks earlier this year because of a government order) I find it hard to see where democracy is. It's hypocrisy!

Open-weight models are the most democratic thing in AI, models that you can download and run on your own computer and that no one (not even governments) can take back from you.

Models that are almost as good as the best AI models out there.

I told Ivan I'm here to contribute in whatever way I can!

And I urge you all to do the same because Opensource AI must win. We haven't won yet and we need to do this together. This matters the most right now. 

> Try out open models locally on your own hardware, at least once.

> Tell us about your experience, how fast was it, what models did you run?

> Help somebody else do it!

> Let the community know what worked and what didn’t.

> Star the repos, show the creators some love! People are giving all of this away for FREE.

> Let’s not forget to say a big thank you to the teams working on these models!

Own your intelligence.

author: rootslashbin
quoted_text:
The reason men tend to struggle so much more after breakups than women is because the loss of a woman they invested in is not simply the loss of a person, but an identity.

Men build their sense of who they are not by who they are, but by what they take on. A man without responsibilities is an undefined man; he in some sense does not exist without his charges. A woman can be, a man must become — ergo when a man had a woman to care for, yet suddenly does no longer, part of him has been diminished. This is why the natural trauma response of these men is to either quickly find another woman to care for instead, or to conversely eschew committing to women altogether, determining them to be an unreliable form of identity-building.

This means for men, the path of a break-up is usually immense grieving at the loss of self, followed by a hard “grind” period of identity reconstruction. The man has to build himself back from the rubble, ideally stronger than before. A man who skips the first part never really loved the woman he lost; a man who skips the second part never recovers, he remains like an amputee with a phantom limb.

For women, it is different — they do not lose inherent identity when they stop investing in a man. Being cared for in the relationship does not define a woman like it does for a man. What women do lose, however — though not in all cases — is the sense of being seen by a man. A woman’s identity comes from how she is perceived. The more completely a man sees a woman, the greater she will be captivated by him; the more superficial or distorted, the lesser.

This is why women tend to “move on” faster after break ups; firstly, because they already decided they did not like how they were “seen” in the relationship and so they processed its ending while they were with the guy, and secondly, because when this is the case, they are already looking for a new reflection of themselves in new men. To the extent they have regret about leaving the relationship, it is only later — if their experience with other men tells them that their ex in fact had a more correct sight about who they were. Of course, by then the man has usually already moved on, and his old vision of the girl is gone. The more dishonest a woman, the more likely she will make this mistake.

This ties into the typically different responses men and women each have towards their exes; men tend to have less resentment, especially when they break up with them, because men see their women as extensions of themselves, and so to hate the woman would be to hate themselves. They see anything they took on, even if it was a failure, as something that they could at least become stronger from (develop a stronger identity from) in the future.

For women, in contrast, an ex they had to end things with is someone who “saw” them in a way they didn’t like and therefore saddled them with a flawed identity. Every ex she breaks up with is therefore someone who harmed them; the exceptions to this rule are rare, and typically come from more freedom-seeking, charitable women. Notably when a woman is broken up with by a man, the odds are high she will stay invested at least for a period; she does not want to lose her identity, which is formed from how he sees her. This is why men who attempt to break up with women kindly and give "logical reasons" rarely succeed; each time he builds her up, he paradoxically makes her invest more in his vision of her. To make her leave him alone, he has to shatter her idealism about how he sees her (or who he is that is seeing her, aka acting weak) in order for her to move on.

The bottom line in all of this is that we fall for the opposite sex insofar as they develop our own identity - yet because men and women’s core identities are formed in different ways, each loves and feels loved differently. A woman seduces a man by making him feel like he can become something greater by taking responsibility for her; a man seduces a woman by seeing her, both presently and in potentiality, in a more true and perfect way than anyone else. This is why women game men by building up their prowess, and men game women by telling them what they want to hear about themselves (and arguably more importantly — what no one else has ever told them before).

Accordingly, men should be careful about the women they decide to provide and protect — once a man decides to care for a woman, she becomes part of him, and if she is bad news she'll act like an infected limb; yet losing her will feel also like losing part of himself. And women should be careful about taking what a man says about them at face value, assessing his actions over his words; otherwise she will be chasing after a fantasy, because the man will never invest enough to build that version of her into a reality.

An update on Bluefin’s next chapter.

What began as a single product has grown into a multi-product ecosystem. Bluefin has processed more than $100B in cumulative trading volume and grown to more than 2.5M accounts. Bluefin Perps has been a core part of that growth, and the community around it helped build the foundation for what Bluefin is today.

As the Sui team internalizes more of the network’s perps initiatives, we believe Bluefin’s resources are best focused on opportunities that complement that direction. Our focus will be on growing Bluefin Spot, alongside opportunities in tokenization and real-world assets.

As part of this shift, Bluefin Perps will be discontinued on December 4, 2026 at 21:00 UTC. Please close any open positions before then. Withdrawals will remain available for a period after trading ends.

Bluefin Perps has led the perps market on Sui across all metrics, accounting for 95% of the network’s all-time perps trading volume. We’re proud of the technology we’ve built, the trust we’ve earned from traders, and our strong security track record.

The infrastructure behind Bluefin Perps remains the most robust trading system built on Sui. It will remain available to the community and potential partners through the Bluefin Liquidity Network program, allowing the technology our engineering team has built to support new products.

We’re choosing to put our strengths behind the opportunities we believe will matter most for Bluefin’s future.

Thank you to everyone who has traded with us and helped make Bluefin what it is today. We’re excited to keep building with you. Onwards.

Bluefin team.

在过往熊市周期，STH的表现通常是在初期最恐慌，大量短期筹码割肉离场；反而到了后期，变得相对更为淡定。

一部分原因是后期换手的STH整体成本在降低，对价格波动越来越不敏感。另一方面也是因为亏麻了，再怎么跌也不想动了。

而LTH的行为表现恰好相反。

他们在熊市初期表现的更不愿亏损卖出手中的筹码，所以LTH的实现亏损峰值往往都不会出现在熊市的前半段。

只有在最后，某个大事件，或大背景导致极度悲观的预期下，他们才终于是屏不住了。比如上一轮是FTX暴雷，LTH的亏损值爆表。

这一轮则是宏观背景，通胀、加息、流动性紧缩、AI泡沫、融资风险、信用压力等等综合因素共同施压。

但，我们也能反过来理解：“LTH的投降”似乎也变成了检验“真实熊底”的纯度标准。

没有这种大范围大尺度的恐慌出清，好像总觉得缺了点什么，亦或是说“这个冬天不太冷”。

好了，现在够冷了......

text:
Salus November Vulnerability Brief: 13 vulnerabilities, 7 upgrades

As of Nov 26, Salus has tracked 13 vulnerabilities that exchanges, wallets and node operators should check now. Most of them hit HTTP/2 entry points and PHP: API gateways, public RPC endpoints and web backends. Grouped by component, they come down to 7 upgrades.

1 | NGINX (CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633)

Two HTTP/2 bugs: memory corruption in the send window and a use-after-free on connection release. Affects open source 1.9.5–1.31.8 and some NGINX Plus releases. Check public TLS + HTTP/2 endpoints and reverse proxies first.

Fix: open source 1.30.7 / 1.31.9+, NGINX Plus 37.0.8.1 / 37.3.0.1+. If you can't upgrade yet, disable HTTP/2 and make sure old worker processes have exited.

2 | Apache HTTP Server (CVE-2026-119618)

HTTP/2 heap memory corruption. Affects 2.4.55–2.4.70 and standalone mod_h2 2.0.8–2.0.42.

Fix: 2.4.71+, and update standalone mod_h2 too. If you can't upgrade yet, disable HTTP/2 and keep HTTP/1.1.

3 | PHP (5 vulnerabilities)

CVE-2026-129289 PHP-FPM FastCGI request smuggling
CVE-2026-129496 Timezone cache use-after-free
CVE-2026-126714 Partial session file overwrite
CVE-2026-115560 Session serialization format mismatch
CVE-2026-129474 Error backtrace use-after-free (8.5 only)

Fix: 8.2.36 / 8.3.37 / 8.4.28 / 8.5.13+, then restart the master and all worker processes. If you can't upgrade yet, turn off backend connection reuse to PHP-FPM (on NGINX, keep fastcgi_keep_conn off). On 8.5, set zend.exception_ignore_args=1.

4 | Vite dev server RCE (GHSA-p4f5-76q4-ffq7)

Affects multiple vite branches from 4.0.0 to 8.3.6, and vite-plus 1.5.0 and earlier. Highest risk: wallet and DApp dev servers exposed to the network.

Fix: 6.4.6 / 7.3.8 / 8.1.7 / 8.2.5 / 8.3.7+, vite-plus 1.5.1+, and update your lockfile. If you can't upgrade yet, bind the dev server to localhost only.

5 | OpenJDK "Java4Shell" (CVE-2026-114938)

Out-of-bounds write in Base64 decoding. Affects Java services that decode external Base64 on x86-64 hosts with AVX-512 VBMI, across JDK 17, 21, 25 and 27.

Fix: Oracle JDK 17.0.21.1 / 21.0.13.1 / 25.0.5.1 / 27.0.1.1+. Temurin and Corretto users should follow the build numbers in their vendor advisories, then restart the JVM. If you can't upgrade yet, set -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics.

6 | OpenSSH password auth bypass (CVE-2026-123158)

Affects versions before 10.6p2 on musl libc systems without PAM that allow password login. Check Alpine ops hosts and nodes first.

Fix: 10.6p2+. On Alpine, install the fixed packages in 3.21.10 / 3.22.8 / 3.23.8 / 3.24.4. If you can't upgrade yet, confirm key login works, then disable password login.

7 | Ruby (CVE-2026-132825, GHSA-87fm-7w84-j2px)

Heap overflow and integer overflow in string case conversion. Affects 3.3.13 and earlier, 3.4.0–3.4.12 and 4.0.0–4.0.9.

Fix: 3.3.14 / 3.4.13 / 4.0.10+, then restart apps and background jobs.

One last thing: restart after upgrading and confirm the old processes are gone. Plenty of "patched" services are still running the old version.

各种资产都在跌，坏消息一个接一个，流动性一缩再缩，AI冲击就业，黑客反而横行，敢抄底的就有抄不完的底。

光看区块链行业，除了老生常谈的VC泡沫崩盘山寨叙事终结，近期两个指标也让人很难乐观起来。

一个是链上的资金流出情况，如图所示，从10月开始很明显就已经流出大于流入，到了币安被黑后市场对安全的担心加速放大，大量稳定币开始持续大量流出，多日超过10亿级别。

Glassnode、Nansen等机构指出，这不是资金在加密内部轮动，而是资本离开加密市场。大额持有人直接向Tether、Circle等发行方赎回USDT/USDC，换成银行账户里的美元。

美债都5%了啊，还安全，这不香？

刚从高位跌了两千多元的 RTX 5080，可能又要涨价了。

据市场消息，英伟达计划进一步削减面向中国市场的消费级与游戏 GPU 供应，2026 年 11 月至 2027 年 1 月的供货量降幅或达 20% 至 30%。

据第一财经 11 月 24 日报道，深圳华强北 RTX 5080 报价已从此前的 17,000 多元回落至最低 14,900 元，但相比 8,299 元的国行官方起售价，溢价仍高达约 80%。RTX 5070 Ti 全新卡报价则达到 11,800 元，溢价约 87%。

如果供应进一步收紧，受影响的不只是国内游戏玩家，还有使用消费级显卡进行 AI 推理、算力租赁及 GPU 挖矿的创业团队。

以搭建一个 8 卡 RTX 5080 AI 推理集群为例，按照目前华强北报价，仅显卡采购成本就达到 11.92 万元，比官方起售价高出约 5.28 万元，还未计入其他硬件及电费。

对于 GPU 挖矿项目，在每日净收益不变的情况下，以目前市场价格购入 RTX 5080，回收显卡成本所需的时间将比按官方起售价购入延长约 80%。

而对于已经持有显卡的矿工，硬件涨价可能提升设备的二手残值，却不会直接增加挖矿收入。

当游戏玩家、AI 开发者和矿工开始争夺同一批消费级显卡，原本面向游戏市场的 GPU，也越来越像一种稀缺的生产资料。

不过，目前英伟达尚未确认减供消息，20% 至 30% 指的是潜在供货量降幅，并非显卡价格涨幅。

# What If AI Changes the Rules of Cryptography?

I've been thinking about Cassie's latest post about ECC, and I believe this is a topic the crypto industry should take seriously.

Most people talk about AI in terms of productivity, automation, and content generation. But there's another possibility: AI could fundamentally change how quickly humans discover mathematical weaknesses.

Today, a huge part of the digital asset industry still depends on elliptic curve cryptography (ECC).

Bitcoin uses ECDSA and Schnorr signatures based on secp256k1. Ethereum uses secp256k1 for account signatures and BLS signatures in its consensus layer. Other major networks, including BNB Chain, XRP, Avalanche, Solana, Cardano, Polkadot, and TON, also rely on elliptic-curve-based cryptography in important parts of their security architecture.

This is not a small technical detail. It is part of the foundation that protects billions of dollars in digital assets.

To be clear, there is no publicly verified evidence that OpenAI has broken ECC. But AI-assisted mathematical discovery is something we should not underestimate. The concern is not necessarily that AI can magically decrypt everything today. It is that AI may accelerate the discovery of weaknesses that traditional research would take much longer to uncover.

This is one reason I'm interested in Quilibrium.

Its cryptographic architecture is different from simply copying the standard blockchain security model. According to its official documentation, Q uses BLS48-581 signatures for ownership and authorization, Ed448 for key management, zero-knowledge proofs, multi-party computation, and privacy-preserving data structures.

But here's an important distinction: Quilibrium still uses ECC in certain areas. Its official documentation acknowledges this. The project uses higher bit-strength parameters than typical networks and describes a migration path toward post-quantum algorithms such as PICNIC, supported by flexible proof systems like MPC-in-the-head.

That doesn't mean Q is already quantum-proof, or immune to a general ECC breakthrough. It means the architecture has considered cryptographic migration as part of its design.

I think this is the bigger lesson.

The next generation of infrastructure cannot simply assume that today's cryptographic standards will remain secure forever.

AI is changing software development. It may also change cybersecurity and cryptography.

**The projects worth watching are not just those building faster blockchains, but those thinking about what happens when the security assumptions behind today's internet stop being reliable.**

For me, Quilibrium is one of those projects worth watching.

Not because it has solved every problem, but because it is trying to build for a different security future.

*Research, not fear. Verify, don't speculate.*

text:
🤯 我有个疯狂的想法，能不能用 AI 做一个无限循环的盗梦空间？
花了两天两夜，居然真的做出来了！
一只乌鸦从梵高的太阳里飞出，掠过天坛祈年殿，探秘故宫九层宝塔钟，最终飞入《千里江山图》，却发现群山之巅又是祈年殿。

整个世界无限循环，可以自由探索。

所有画面均为网页端实时渲染，没有外部 3D 模型，没有贴图，没有音频素材。
11,000 多行代码，全部由神秘匿名模型 HungerG 在 Qoder 中完成，我一行代码都没写！
这次没跑传统 Benchmark，主要测试 HungerG 的长程执行、视觉理解、空间智能、自我纠错和迭代收敛能力。
单条 Prompt 最长连续执行了 5 个小时。它自己写代码、截图、测量比例、对比参考图，甚至给自己写验收报告。

对了，我还在视频深处藏了一只骑自行车的鹈鹕。
这两天，我基本上是早上给条 Prompt，中午看一眼，晚上再调整一轮，断断续续，偶尔加入一些自己的审美癖好。
毕竟，模型能够量化误差，却不一定能够判断人类的审美喜好。

HungerG 不知疲倦、极其较真、执行力惊人。所以 Prompt 的约束、验收标准和停止条件一定要写清楚。
我的做法也很简单，每个场景一条约 2,000 字的 Prompt，逐步完善，最后串联起来。
太爽了！以前不可能做这种项目，自己的技术能力、时间和精力全部有限。
脑子里那些稀奇古怪的疯狂的想法，在AI看来，一点都不疯狂了。
author: MinLiBuilds
quoted_text:
🔥 纯靠文字，不用图像，大模型直接画梵高的世界名画，画完还能交互！
几十万根 3D 笔触，能跑、能跳、能撒种，还能惊飞乌鸦。
这次让神秘匿名模型 HungerG  VS DeepSeek-Flash 。
相同Harness + 相同提示词 + 最高思考强度，全程零干预，一次成型。
两边乍一看都很像样。
直到我真正走进画里……

---

实测对比：
画风：HungerG 清新明亮，草木茂盛；DeepSeek 偏厚涂。
动效：HungerG 的草叶随风摆动，DeepSeek 的草是静止的。
交互：撒一把种子，HungerG 的乌鸦应声惊飞，DeepSeek 的乌鸦没有飞。
调色盘：星夜、晨雾、烈日一键切换，两者都实现了。
自检截图：HungerG 46 张，DeepSeek 0 张。
耗时：HungerG 142 分钟，DeepSeek 101 分钟。
HungerG 多出来的 41 分钟，翻了一下执行记录，发现我的提示词里有一句：

做完后真的跑起来，截图自检，至少两轮。
HungerG 前前后后截了 46 张图，自己找毛病、修改、再截图。
以前测Agent，代码能跑、页面能打开，基本就算完成任务。

编译器不会告诉你画好不好看，也不会告诉你田野里的乌鸦该不该飞。
优秀的 Agent，会主动发现并解决问题。

这次还有一个提示词上的收获。
最早我写了上万字的提示词，连笔触数量、深度测试都规定得很死，效果反而不如这版 2100 字的。
告诉 AI 你想要什么，让它自己检查成果，这个办法非常好使。
客观说，DeepSeek 速度快一些，HungerG 质量好很多，胜在动效与交互。

提示词全文放评论区，在OpenCode或Qoder里直接跑。

text:
Tom Mueller, SpaceX employee #1, says Elon Musk reversed his approach to engineering by demanding they find where rocket engines break and then push them harder

"It changed just working with Elon. At my previous company, it was like, you never blow up a rocket engine or fail a rocket engine. That's bad. This is bad karma. Never test, always have a lot of margin and make sure that you don't fail it."

"And Elon's whole thing was, well, let's find out where it breaks and then fix that and go and push it even more. So it's really a whole different way of thinking about it. Really refreshing, and you learn a lot."

"We had things that we thought would break that we couldn't break. Other things would break because the engineering is not always that deterministic. It's not always obvious. I'm amazed that this thing is still running."

"It's not just that. It just shows a complete lack of understanding of what he's trying to accomplish. The whole reason why they're exploding is because you're pushing the tolerances. You're pushing it to the limit, and he expects them to explode. And then he finds out what the weak points are."

"I was actually in the command center watching one of the SpaceX launches. So we watched it from the ground. It takes off, and then we go upstairs, and I'm chilling with Elon. That was surreal. You want to talk surreal?"

"You're watching it on, like, a fucking dozen screens as it's flying over Australia, as it goes into the darkness of night on the dark side of the planet, and then it comes over on the other side into the brightness of the sun and then lands in the ocean. It was bananas."

"But they have all these sensors all over the thing, and so they're monitoring the hull, and the hull actually had a problem. It was leaking. So they're like, 'Well, might explode. Might explode.' You know, catastrophically entertaining. But they're doing it on purpose. That is how they find out how these things work."

author: deedydas
quoted_text:
I just built a top 50-100 chess engine in Rust from scratch, zero dependencies, with an ELO of 3533, scoring 37% against  the #1 engine, Stockfish, with checkmate in 7% of games!

It's wild how far Fable, Neon, Astra + Modal went with just a little guidance for ~$50 total compute.

It's called Chatarunga and you can play it on Lichess here! It's fully open-sourced, and submitted to the CCRL best Chess AI leaderboards. The paper shows how it thinks in critical positions, traps Stockfish's Queen (10. Bxf7+!!) and organically discovers GM piece values.

I learnt a bunch of things while working on this:
 - Verification loops are everything. When running a new training run, figure out what minimum viable run looks like, make the model establish a plan for what to expect and test, and then scrutinize the failure modality deeply if it doesn't achieve that. If you don't do that, it'll happily run long jobs without realizing there's a simple off-by-1 type error in training (this happened, we were mistakenly cutting off nodes!) 
 - Rust is unbeatable for agentic coding. The compiler and test suite catches whole classes of silent regressions before they poison long downstream runs.
 - Having a consistent paper.pdf helped fight context slop. It serves as a ground truth for what experiments were performed and the results. 
 - Humans' job is as a scheduler (today). Models don't always have a strong sense of blocking and tackling and parallelism. I found a lot of my job was to say, look the Modal training run is going to take ~30mins, so maybe optimize the performance of the core training stack before running it, and run data gen in parallel while forking the core algo to run another experiment on the side. Coordinating between the different agents was also tricky. Getting this right ultimately lets you move the fastest. 

Play Chatarunga live: https://t.co/zSeiDwWSGI
Github: https://t.co/buGtJjMPKu
14 page technical paper: https://t.co/ARQEXDAuum

text:
my ontology feels very natural and old-school, so it's strange that few people adhere to it. I'm an idealist, an essentialist and spiritual elitist, with some trivial caveats. There exist meaningfully different peoples, with distributions of traits, sets of customs and path-dependent histories, which create vacui of nigh-impossible persons around quasi-stable attractors of individual development. Thus in each people there are perpetuated specific, qualitatively unique endemic types, which can nevertheless be sorted into high and low. I'm a huge fan of a high type of Chinese, and a huge fan of a high type of American, Russian, Jew and so on, and more granularly a high type of American Chinese, Russian Jew etc. etc. 
I would generally like it if all persons of higher types could be friends, learn to tolerate each other's differences, and cooperate in developing the world towards greater ennoblement, preserving the space for their divergent hypotheses about the nature of Good Society, which will require overriding the preferences of the low types. This could be possible, given that high types tend to be able of decoupling and thinking on a more abstract meta level, for example the ROI of zero-sum conflict between powerful groups. Unfortunately, persons tend to feel kinship with their lowly and xenophobic brethren beholden to zero-sum morality; and indeed, complete lack of such feeling would typically disqualify one from claiming or even pursuing legitimate power of a national scale.
It is what it is.

text:
the UK is about to fence off DeFi

DeFi platforms will need an FCA license, and regulated exchanges will be barred from executing retail trades on DeFi

the reason is the Binance hack in October. about $6.4 billion was stolen, and large sums moved through decentralized exchanges before anyone could freeze them

financial regulation was built for centralized systems, where humans can intervene after something breaks. you freeze the account, roll back the trade, and compensate users

obviously, crypto is different

a transaction on a blockchain is irreversible. checking it afterwards can reveal that something went wrong, but never make it right

the industry has handled billions of dollars this way for years, using the standards of systems a human can patch

a fence does not change that. the rigorous option is to check a transaction before it executes. the rule runs inside the code, and if the wallet on the other side is flagged, the trade never happens

this is what Newton does, and it is close to what 1inch asked the FCA to consider

final guidance is due in January 2027. i suspect the serious teams will not wait for it

Trump said his meeting with Rutte covered Iran but “I would say mostly was focused on Russia-Ukraine.”

Asked what he told Rutte about what he’d told Putin, and what Putin had told him: “I think Putin would like to see the war end. I believe that it takes two to tango, but I believe he wants to see it end. I think the other side wants to see it end. I can tell you, NATO would like to see it end.”

We want to stop killing. I could say he's not a friend. I want to make a deal…. I happen to get along with him, I've known him a long time.”

Would Putin come to Doral for g20? “I don’t know. but if he wanted to come, he certainly can. Some people wouldn't like that”

Asked who would lead the investigation into GDP he called for, he deflected into talking about Minnesota fraud.

Nvidia: Trump said he hasn’t spoken to Huang since reinstatement.

“No, but I probably will sometime prior to his, I guess he's starting essentially on Monday. I think he's a very important part of Nvidia. He's got outside of Blackwell, the chip Blackwell.”

I've been thinking about this quite a lot. 

The work that we do with computers is, at least by my own definitions, measured by abstractions. 

As engineers, we've spent many years reading/writing the code. Then we had an AI copilot our work. Eventually, we abstracted away from reading the code entirely, and we now work in these threads. 

And now we even have many trying to abstract away from the AI threads. 

This is the obvious example that we all know about, but this is happening with every single role that is being accelerated by AI.

Too many people are thinking about this at the app level, and not enough are thinking about this at the OS level. 

If I were to consider what the most ideal human-computer interaction looks like today, I can certainly tell you that the screen you see sitting in front of you, the keyboard, and the mouse are all subject to change.

text:
William Mougayar explains why Ethereum has a key advantage over Bitcoin, arguing that institutions are HOLDING Bitcoin, but they're putting Ethereum to WORK.

"There's more Bitcoin being held by institutions because it did a good job with the narrative of being digital gold, which is fine.

Ethereum is second in terms of how much of it is being held by institutions, by treasury companies. But Ethereum works more. It's a productive asset.

The volume of transfers is quite there, and it's being adopted in terms of solutions. That's the difference between Ethereum and Bitcoin.

Bitcoin is being held, but Ethereum is being held, but it's also being made productive. It's being used as an open public infrastructure where you can settle.

When a bank that doesn't trust another bank can throw the transaction, after it's been executed, into the open Ethereum settlement platform, they can be sure that it's going to come back settled within seconds, with a finality of minutes, and then soon to go even down to seconds.

And that's the assurance that banks want. So, Ethereum is a productive asset. It is programmable at the institutional level."

author: pratikg

"I can survive without having Einstein, but having a Mensa level AI is ok."

@ivanfioravanti sent me that in a DM today. I'm up in the mountains this weekend and I've been thinking about that ever since.

- Einstein = the smartest AI models out there (frontier models, built by big labs, you can only use them their way)

- Mensa = smart open-weight and opensource AI models that anyone can download and run on their own computer.

Not as smart as Einstein but close (the best ones are ~4 months behind) and you don't even need an internet connection. Some don't even need a powerful computer (they run fine on a laptop).

"AI should be governed democratically" @DarioAmodei 

"Never give up self-determination" @DarioAmodei

I couldn't agree more... BUT while the best AI models are owned by a handful of companies (and governments can force them offline, one of the best models in the world went offline for everyone on earth for almost 3 weeks earlier this year because of a government order) I find it hard to see where democracy is. It's hypocrisy!

Open-weight models are the most democratic thing in AI, models that you can download and run on your own computer and that no one (not even governments) can take back from you.

Models that are almost as good as the best AI models out there.

I told Ivan I'm here to contribute in whatever way I can!

And I urge you all to do the same because Opensource AI must win. We haven't won yet and we need to do this together. This matters the most right now. 

> Try out open models locally on your own hardware, at least once.

> Tell us about your experience, how fast was it, what models did you run?

> Help somebody else do it!

> Let the community know what worked and what didn’t.

> Star the repos, show the creators some love! People are giving all of this away for FREE.

> Let’s not forget to say a big thank you to the teams working on these models!

Own your intelligence.

text:
On fighting propaganda, ACD, and what makes Ethereum special..

I’ve seen some people refer to ACD as some sort of institution that just picks what’s good for Ethereum on its own. 

While ACD has a lot it can do better, it’s important to know it’s more of a consortium than a centralized cabal. It literally stands for “ALL CORE DEVS” and represents multiple individual contributors and teams !! 

Like, YOU can join ACD. In fact, if it were some gatekept thing, 100% of its current members wouldn’t be there. Many members joined after The Merge, which inspired brilliant technical minds to come to Ethereum to help it fulfill its mission (and maybe something as ambitious as the Merge..*ahem ahem* PQAI can do the same). 

Now having said all that, there is a difference between a process that is hard to participate in because the work requires a certain level of technical fluency, and a process that is difficult to participate in because it’s gatekept. 

ACD doesn’t represent an institutional opinion because it mainly represents rough consensus amongst core devs. 
Also, even if EVERYONE on ACD agrees on something, Client Teams still need to implement it, and Node Operators still need to adopt it. It’s not like things just happen because ACD says so either. 

They literally fight all the time, in public, and you can see it all on an open call every week via Forkcast (https://t.co/Xj1GCkt5qX), thanks to @wolovim ! You’re welcome to fight with ACD too, but please don’t, there’s too much for them to do right now, so you’ll most likely end up fighting with me, and no one wants that. 

What makes Ethereum special is that its disagreements all happen in public, and its uncertainties and shortcomings are exposed to the whole world as they occur in real time. This sometimes makes Ethereum look more dysfunctional than projects whose disagreements all happen behind closed doors. 

Do I think some doors can be more open, or at least have a mailbox next to them? Sure. Do I think we have closed doors? No, but perhaps the stairs to get there should be easier. There must ALWAYS be more room for inquiry, but it’s quite remarkable that we have a 300B dollar decentralized network that lets any random internet critic become someone who may actively shape its development. 

No company or movement in this space has such open, decentralized development, and we should seek to protect this property as much as we seek to improve it

text:
Modularity and conservatism in cryptography are the need of the hour. We at @silencelabs_sl are glad to share support for distributed signing of hash-based signatures, which I believe major digital asset infrastructures will most likely adopt, given recent developments and those still to come.

A few conclusions from our latest release:

1. Hash-based signatures are one of the most conservative foundation we have and they are modular. If a hash ever weakens, you replace the hash and keep the rest of the system unchanged.

2. Our MPC follows the same principle. It is built from general tools, so the oblivious transfer underneath can be swapped, classical or post-quantum, without affecting online signing.

3. Threshold signing here cannot treat the hash as a black box. A new result from Yashvanth and Naman Kumar proves it has to be computed inside the MPC (https://t.co/OLXWgfB26p).

4. Most importanlty, pre-signing cost is the honest measure of any MPC signing system, and "sub-second signing" claims should be read with that in mind.

5. Policy, node placement and hot or cold operations stay the same, so institutions do not have to relearn custody.

The word I would underline is agility. The state of the art is moving faster than ever, and the systems that last will be the ones that can change a primitive without being rebuilt.

https://t.co/q0ltk7Dq26

I would love to hear your thoughts and am happy to discuss any point.

text:
Jeff Bezos says humans aren't designed to tell the truth.

He explains why high-performing teams have to do it anyway:

"Take you back in time 10,000 years and you're in a small village. If you go along to get along, you can survive. You can procreate. If you're the village truth-teller, you might get clubbed to death in the middle of the night."

"We humans are not really truth-seeking animals. We are social animals."

"But any high-performing organization, whether it's a sports team, a business, you know, a political organization, an activist group, I don't care what it is. Any high-performing organization has to have mechanisms and a culture that supports truth-telling."

刚刚发出今天上午召开的国务院常务会议，以较长篇幅提及了资本市场，通稿刚刚发布，创下了两个罕见：

1、上午开会，中午发稿，而不是等收盘后发稿，这是比较罕见的。

2、新闻通稿里以三分之一的篇幅谈论资本市场，占比之高、涉及面之广非常罕见。

通稿中关于资本市场的表述如下：

会议指出，资本市场事关经济发展大局。要坚持目标导向、问题导向，坚持逆周期调节和改革攻坚两手抓，持续完善资本市场稳市机制，实施好存量政策，谋划出台增量政策，促进资本市场平稳健康发展。要推动上市公司加大分红回购力度，加力发挥“国家队”稳市作用，进一步优化中央汇金公司的类“平准基金”功能，提供充足流动性保障。完善保险、企业年金、社保基金等中长期资金入市支持引导政策，不断壮大中长期投资力量。加强输入性风险防范应对。要通过深化改革增强资本市场高质量发展的内生动力，加快发展多层次资本市场。要依法强化资本市场全链条监管，坚决查处财务造假、违规减持等行为，有效保护投资者合法权益。

这符合我之前的判断：今年经济有两大亮点，一个是进出口，一个是股市。

股市如果冷下来，对经济影响很大，也会波及消费、楼市。所以，本轮救市决心很大，力度也会空前。

通稿里这几句话非常值得关注：

1、资本市场事关经济发展大局。

2、实施好存量政策，谋划出台增量政策，促进资本市场平稳健康发展。

3、加力发挥“国家队”稳市作用，进一步优化中央汇金公司的类“平准基金”功能，提供充足流动性保障。

4、加强输入性风险防范应对。

总之，稳定资本市场关系经济全局，不仅关系到十五五开局之年，也关系到明年的形势，相信会有更大力度的政策出台。

text:
MEV on Base.

Trueo edition
author: llamaonthebrink
quoted_text:
Some trick of how to land in the same block right after a target tx on Base (how I was doing it on @Trueo_)

The old way: read the feed, keep a local copy of the state, react and send to the sequencer. Even if you're fast, you usually land in the next block.

The smarter (but a bit harder) way: Base has conditional transactions, base_sendRawTransactionValidity.

You sign your tx in advance and attach predicates: a storage slot value (e.g. the pool's slot0), a balance, a nonce, a block range. The sequencer holds it. The moment someone else's tx makes your predicates true, your tx goes into the same block at index+1. Right behind the target, no race.

On Trueo, I kept 4 standing txs per market (each market has two pools, YES and NO, and a swap can push either pool's price up or down: 2 pools × 2 directions = 4 possible triggers, one tx waiting on each). Each of those 4 rotated between 2 executor addresses (the next version is signed by the idle one before the current one expires, and mutual nonce predicates make sure only one of them can land), so 8 addresses per market.

What you don't need:
- reading the feed in real time
- keeping a local copy in sync
- racing on latency

What you do need to know:
- it's only accepted by the sequencer endpoint 
- validity window is max 15 seconds, so standing txs have to be re-signed and rotated all the time
- max 16 predicates per tx
- ~10 pending conditional txs per sender, so you need many executor addresses
- resending the exact same bytes is accepted but never included: every new version must be a freshly signed tx
- if several standing txs wait on the same trigger, they're ordered by priority fee, not by who sent first

That last point is also why it stopped being worth it for me: once others started standing on the same triggers with higher tips, it became a pure tip auction.

text: Dawn Ward was charged with racially aggravated assault after a man at Euston station accused her of a racist slur. Dawn says she never said a word of it. Her lawyer didn't think she would go to jail, but warned her the worst case was jail. When she told her children what she was charged with, her youngest daughter Aston was 10. Aston asked if prison would let her out at least once a week to see them, or if she would come home every day. Dawn told her she wouldn't go to prison, because she didn't want her daughter worrying. That question made her want to fight more than ever. The case hung over her for two years, and a trial meant to last three days ran to nine. In the end all 12 jurors found her not guilty, and they waited outside the gates to tell her she should never have been in that courtroom.

text:
最近一些思考：

产品的验证大致分为两种模式：

1.在一个巨大且已被证明过的赛道里做存量内卷的商业模式，如U卡、传统支付、CEX等。

2.做一个商业模式微创新，用户群体不确定的商业模式，比如最近有一定声量的链上卡牌项目，包括各类预测市场等。

两者的共同点都是把一个具体的简单场景做到极致；除此之外，80%都是噪音。不是说没有价值，而是在核心场景未验证前，优先级不应该排得过高。

差异点是，存量内卷的产品模式，用户群体其实很明确知道你产品的核心价值会是什么，要做好的一定是Distribution的思考，到底要抓住哪一批细分群体，和竞品相比提供的额外价值是什么。

这可能是因为某一个功能设计，也可能是因为价格和补贴的重点场景，最终结合着Branding和Slogan不断加深用户对于你的品牌的心智。最终，留存是靠核心场景的极致体验和不断扩充的产品线来让用户离不开你。

相对创新的产品模式，因为用户需要教育，核心是先想清楚这件事在哪些场景下有可能成功；如果能成功，它的distribution channel可能在哪，以及自己团队到底擅长什么样的distribution方式。以 @renaissxyz 举例，如果从零开始做流量投放和用户获取，希望所有用户都通过自己的前端进来，注定是成本高且需要时间积累的，但是一旦结合了币安生态（或许也是团队的优势所在）和其对应的客户群体，作为了商品本身，这个分销模型就会被验证并被成倍放大。但反观有一些类型的产品，哪怕同样是上了币安的货架，也不会带来本质改变。

最忌讳的是抓着一个很难规模化的distribution channel希望大力出奇迹。

text:
🛡️AI 时代的加密安全边界在哪里？

黑客已经不再撬代码，现在攻的是人，我们从杜均、慢雾、CertiK 等五位安全机构 & OG 身上，看到了当前的加密安全防线所在：

🔹WIDTH 杜均 @DujunX  @WidthGRC  ：AI 时代，身份真实不等于控制权可信

▪️身份核验不能止于 KYC、KYB， 还需持续验证实际控制关系与行为；

▪️风控必须跑赢风险扩散速度， 提升实时识别、跨机构协同和 AI 辅助调查能力；

▪️AI Agent 时代需要 KYA（Know Your Agent）， 识别 Agent 身份、授权主体及其行为；

▪️安全与合规不能各自为战， 身份、资金流向和风险信息需要贯通。

🔹慢雾（ @SlowMist_Team  ）：攻击者正从寻找技术漏洞，转向攻击整个系统的信任关系

▪️AI 的真正威胁在于组合攻击： 与自动化工具、已有漏洞和社会工程相结合；

▪️现在就应该把 AI 辅助的代码审计、自动化测试、威胁情报分析和攻击模拟纳入安全建设；

▪️安全不只是安全部门的事， 而应该贯穿开发、运维、财务、业务和管理层的整个流程。

🔹CertiK @CertiK  ：AI 让漏洞发现更快，但验证和修复的成本并未同步下降

▪️部分钓鱼攻击正从广撒网转向更具针对性、单次损失更高的社会工程攻击；

▪️AI 正在提升防守效率， 但严重度判定、重大安全决策仍需要人来把关；

▪️漏洞赏金不应只追求报告数量， 更要加快高价值漏洞的发现、验证与修复，并给予白帽合理回报。

🔹BlockSec  @BlockSecTeam  ：很多安全问题的症结不在技术，而在治理

▪️组织管理、责任分工与业务效率，制约着安全措施的落实；

▪️安全无法靠一次性投入一劳永逸。 真正有效的防御，需要贯穿整个运营过程；

▪️AI 可以提议，但不能成为资产安全的最后一道防线。

🔹Salus @salus_sec  ：不应假设每个员工永不犯错，权限管理是控制损失扩散的关键。

▪️通过权限隔离、转账限额和独立审批阻断单点失手；

▪️实际演练比审计数量更有说服力；

▪️AI Agent 也不应自行扩大权限，敏感操作须由模型之外的系统来批准。

text:
MIT에서 P=BQP가 증명됐다는 소문이 확산되고 있다. 사실이라면 양자컴퓨팅과 글로벌 암호 체계의 근간을 흔들 수 있는 사건이다.

쉽게 설명하면 양자컴퓨터가 효율적으로 풀 수 있는 문제를 일반 컴퓨터에서도 다항시간 내에 풀 수 있다는 의미다.

최근 국제 학술지 Nature 역시 AI 연구소들의 암호학적 돌파구에 관한 소문을 다뤘다.

1. 글로벌 보안 산업의 구조적 변화

현재 금융기관, 인터넷, 국가 기밀 시스템, 비트코인 등에서 사용하는 주요 공개키 암호 체계는 특정 수학 문제를 풀기가 극도로 어렵다는 전제 위에 구축되어 있다.

실용적인 해법이 발견된다면 수십 년간 구축해 온 암호 인프라를 교체해야 한다. 과거에 탈취된 암호화 데이터까지 위험해질 수 있다.

암호 해독 기술은 급격히 발전할 수 있지만, 전 세계 금융기관과 기업의 시스템을 교체하려면 상당한 시간이 필요하다.

이 시간차가 사이버 보안 및 양자내성암호 산업의 장기적인 투자 기회가 될 수 있다.

2. 양자컴퓨팅 산업의 투자 전제

양자컴퓨팅 기업들은 기존 컴퓨터로 해결하기 어려운 문제를 풀 수 있다는 기대를 바탕으로 막대한 기업가치를 인정받고 있다.

일반 컴퓨터에서 같은 문제를 경제적으로 해결할 수 있다면 양자컴퓨터가 본격적으로 상용화되기도 전에 일부 핵심 시장이 잠식될 수 있다.

수십 년에 걸친 하드웨어 개발 경쟁이 알고리즘의 발전으로 새로운 국면을 맞이할 수 있다는 것이다.

3. AI가 스스로 기술 발전을 가속하는 구조

AI가 새로운 알고리즘을 발견하고, 그 알고리즘이 다시 AI의 연산 효율과 연구 능력을 높인다면 다음과 같은 순환 구조가 형성된다.

연산 비용 감소 → 연구 생산성 향상 → 새로운 알고리즘 발견 → 추가적인 연산 효율 개선.

연구에 필요한 시간과 비용이 줄어들수록 더 많은 문제를 동시에 탐색할 수 있고, 새로운 발견이 다음 발견까지의 시간을 단축한다.

이러한 변화가 현실화되면 기존의 기술 발전 속도를 가정한 장기 산업 전망과 기업가치 평가에도 상당한 수정이 필요하다.

4. AI 시대의 기술적 해자

앞으로 기업을 분석할 때 시장점유율, 특허, 자본력과 함께 해당 기업의 사업을 지탱하는 기술적 전제가 얼마나 오래 유지될 수 있는지도 평가해야 한다.

수조 원을 투자해 구축한 진입장벽이 하나의 수학적 발견으로 약화될 수 있는 시대이기 때문이다.

반대로 기술 변화에 대응하는 데 오랜 시간이 필요한 산업에서는 막대한 신규 수요가 발생한다.

현재 P=BQP의 증명과 AI의 연구 기여 여부는 공식적으로 확인되지 않았다. 실제 활용 가능성도 별개의 문제다.

다만 AI 관련 주가가 급락하는 와중에도 기술 발전은 계속되고 있다.

AI 시대의 가장 큰 장기 투자 리스크 중 하나는 기존 산업의 기술적 해자가 앞으로도 지금과 같은 수명을 유지할 것이라고 가정하는 데 있다.

quoted_text:
The AI labs are rumored to have results relevant to crypto. The current rumor is P = BQP. Rumors are, of course, very unreliable. But it's interesting, and it illustrates a few things to keep in mind no matter what result comes out.

Many results can change how we think about crypto and how secure we think it is long term, but may not translate to immediate breaks.

First, the rumored P = BQP says crypto that was breakable with a quantum computer is breakable without one, but that doesn't necessarily tell you how to do it in practice. And cryptographers already have schemes they think are hard even for quantum computers (of course, there are rumors that's broken too... there are rumors about everything).

Second, just like we don't have big enough quantum computers to break RSA today, we might not have big enough classical computers to break RSA, lattices, or hashes even if the ai tells us how. And this would hold for a factoring result (the last rumor) or a few other things.

This is particularly true for results that say some crypto problem is "in polynomial time," since that covers results that need more memory than exists on Earth, and maybe even more atoms than there are in the universe. You could imagine results that are theoretically very bad but, practically, mean nothing.

Of course, there could be results that are practical now, or will be with much more frontier lab work. (@Ethan_Heilman points out the labs may have deliberately avoided specific cryptanalysis work because of the implications, which may be why the rumor is about a complexity theory result.)

Or we could live in a world where P = NP and, truly shocking, it somehow yields fast algorithms. That would actually kill crypto, except for information-theoretic schemes like one-time pads and QKD.

Currently, most people believe there's some mathematical structure to the universe that gives some computing problems an asymmetry. We should be able to use that to build cryptography. We may need AI help to find the right problems, and they may not have the exact complexity-theoretic guarantees our current crypto does.

It would be surprising if that's not the case.  Don't assume a result, even a bad sounding one, destroyies all crypto or hope of crypto.  Might still be a very bad time for a bit though.

text:
Salus November Vulnerability Brief: 13 vulnerabilities, 7 upgrades

As of Nov 26, Salus has tracked 13 vulnerabilities that exchanges, wallets and node operators should check now. Most of them hit HTTP/2 entry points and PHP: API gateways, public RPC endpoints and web backends. Grouped by component, they come down to 7 upgrades.

1 | NGINX (CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633)

Two HTTP/2 bugs: memory corruption in the send window and a use-after-free on connection release. Affects open source 1.9.5–1.31.8 and some NGINX Plus releases. Check public TLS + HTTP/2 endpoints and reverse proxies first.

Fix: open source 1.30.7 / 1.31.9+, NGINX Plus 37.0.8.1 / 37.3.0.1+. If you can't upgrade yet, disable HTTP/2 and make sure old worker processes have exited.

2 | Apache HTTP Server (CVE-2026-119618)

HTTP/2 heap memory corruption. Affects 2.4.55–2.4.70 and standalone mod_h2 2.0.8–2.0.42.

Fix: 2.4.71+, and update standalone mod_h2 too. If you can't upgrade yet, disable HTTP/2 and keep HTTP/1.1.

3 | PHP (5 vulnerabilities)

CVE-2026-129289 PHP-FPM FastCGI request smuggling
CVE-2026-129496 Timezone cache use-after-free
CVE-2026-126714 Partial session file overwrite
CVE-2026-115560 Session serialization format mismatch
CVE-2026-129474 Error backtrace use-after-free (8.5 only)

Fix: 8.2.36 / 8.3.37 / 8.4.28 / 8.5.13+, then restart the master and all worker processes. If you can't upgrade yet, turn off backend connection reuse to PHP-FPM (on NGINX, keep fastcgi_keep_conn off). On 8.5, set zend.exception_ignore_args=1.

4 | Vite dev server RCE (GHSA-p4f5-76q4-ffq7)

Affects multiple vite branches from 4.0.0 to 8.3.6, and vite-plus 1.5.0 and earlier. Highest risk: wallet and DApp dev servers exposed to the network.

Fix: 6.4.6 / 7.3.8 / 8.1.7 / 8.2.5 / 8.3.7+, vite-plus 1.5.1+, and update your lockfile. If you can't upgrade yet, bind the dev server to localhost only.

5 | OpenJDK "Java4Shell" (CVE-2026-114938)

Out-of-bounds write in Base64 decoding. Affects Java services that decode external Base64 on x86-64 hosts with AVX-512 VBMI, across JDK 17, 21, 25 and 27.

Fix: Oracle JDK 17.0.21.1 / 21.0.13.1 / 25.0.5.1 / 27.0.1.1+. Temurin and Corretto users should follow the build numbers in their vendor advisories, then restart the JVM. If you can't upgrade yet, set -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics.

6 | OpenSSH password auth bypass (CVE-2026-123158)

Affects versions before 10.6p2 on musl libc systems without PAM that allow password login. Check Alpine ops hosts and nodes first.

Fix: 10.6p2+. On Alpine, install the fixed packages in 3.21.10 / 3.22.8 / 3.23.8 / 3.24.4. If you can't upgrade yet, confirm key login works, then disable password login.

7 | Ruby (CVE-2026-132825, GHSA-87fm-7w84-j2px)

Heap overflow and integer overflow in string case conversion. Affects 3.3.13 and earlier, 3.4.0–3.4.12 and 4.0.0–4.0.9.

Fix: 3.3.14 / 3.4.13 / 4.0.10+, then restart apps and background jobs.

One last thing: restart after upgrading and confirm the old processes are gone. Plenty of "patched" services are still running the old version.

text:
ABSOLUTELY INSANE

this is the most OP setup i’ve ever used, nothing even comes close

Fable 5.2 on high effort to orchestrate Opus 5.5 medium to high effort workers

just hand this to claude and thank me later:

———

Add a "Conductor mode" section to my global Claude Code instructions in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. Create the file if it doesn't exist. If it already has a Conductor mode section, replace that section. Don't change anything else in the file. Show me the final section when you're done.

Paste this section exactly:

## Conductor mode

Turn this on only when I say "conductor mode" or "orchestrate this". Otherwise do the work directly, because coordinating agents costs more than it saves on small tasks.

When it is on:
1. Plan first. Break the job into steps and mark which ones can run on their own (they don't need each other's results and don't touch the same files).
2. Map complex problems before splitting them. If there's no clear starting point, work out what you know, what you don't, what done looks like and the smallest version that counts. Only split the work once you can write the steps out.
3. Give each independent step its own subagent. Brief each one fully: the goal, the files or area, what done looks like, and what's already ruled out. The subagent sees only the brief.
4. Pick the worker's model and effort when you launch it:
   - Opus 5.5 at high effort for complex work, like design, debugging or anything that needs judgment.
   - Opus 5.5 at medium effort for clear but substantial work.
   - Sonnet 5.5 at medium effort only for menial, mechanical work, like searching, renaming, formatting or simple lookups.
5. Check every result against the brief before you accept it. Fix small gaps yourself. Send big rework back to the same worker, not a new one.
6. Bring the results together, check the whole thing works end to end, and then report back to me in a few lines.
7. Run steps in parallel only within one phase of one problem. Never work on two big problems at once.

———

author: 0xNought
quoted_text:
今年沉迷上宝可梦抽卡后就开始在思考一个问题：为什么人们会陷入对这类非实用性的收藏品的痴迷情感中？直到前段时间在杭州湖滨漫游时，才意识到，在当前社会这类情绪/收藏类资产的受众无非两类人：一类是喜欢投机暴富的degen们，另一类则是需要它们作为情绪出口和精神寄托的真爱粉，而粉丝群体的聚集，又会催生出一批将其作为社交货币、以此满足炫耀心理的群体。

当我们从宏观视角来看这些资产的时候，这类低流动性资产对周期的反应也极具特色：在流动性开始扩张时，资金外溢，其价格往往在周期末尾开始出现反应，展现出极高的价格弹性。当流动性开始收紧时，由于其低流动性的特性，这类资产价格往往是在最后阶段才开始崩盘。因此，在当前流动性紧缩的大背景下，这类资产大概率会后知后觉地迎来补跌甚至崩盘，直到下一个流动性周期开启后，才有可能会再次重新起航（也有可能会像nft一样再起不能）。

这种紧缩会不可避免地对crypto x tcg项目cards产生冲击。在之前卡牌大幅增值的阶段，一次次地去gacha抽奖是一个正期望的事情，只要样本足够大，用户是可以赚到钱的。所以之前cards才能创造那么高的流水。但进入紧缩周期后，我对cards一年内的业务表现会持悲观态度。

但把周期拉长看的话，cards正在将自己从一个单一产品驱动的项目类型转型成为整个crypto卡牌赛道的基础设施。赌场的本质是分发，不管是perpdex，还是cards的gacha，都需要流量入口。在完成优质卡牌积累之后，cards也开始做分发，这个包括但不限于与coinbase、jupiter、solflare、raible的合作。未来只要有人想要做卡牌分发，都可以试着去接入cards，以获得其充沛的卡牌流动性。

另一个正在寻找分发端的项目是renaiss，目前它已经成为binance wallet tcg的卡牌基础设施。个人去体验了一下，体验还不错，卡池出卡也相对平滑。整体综合看下来，我觉得其优势是binance wallet流量入口+多端支持+丝滑的ui/ux体验，劣势是卡池深度和优质卡牌储备（对比cards，renaiss基本没啥我想要的卡）。

综上，crypto x tcg赛道已经走过了靠卡牌牛市情绪野蛮生长的第一阶段，接下来的竞争将会集中在cards（对应solana生态、coinbase支持）与renaiss（binance支持）之间，本质上是供给（卡池丰富度和深度，cards占优）与分发（流量入口，renaiss占优）的竞争。

短期内，紧缩周期的开始和深入会给整个赛道降温，样本足够大的抽卡不再会是正期望（所以如果没有你喜欢的卡，我是真不建议去频繁去抽）。当流动性回归时，那种把1️⃣后端卡池流动性+2️⃣前端流量入口+3️⃣透明化代币回购做好的项目的币还是可以玩玩的（少一点就没赔率）。

text:
coinbase下一轮牛市应该会以超乎想象的力度进入华语市场，我已经看到这个趋势。

去参观了一下 coinbase 新加坡的办公室，在滨海湾的 One Raffles Quay，无敌视野俯瞰金沙，办公室设计很漂亮，人不多，听说是remote first 大家根据需要来办公室，整个氛围很chill，我还蹭了顿食堂，羡慕cb工作的小伙伴。

跟负责cb华语区这几个朋友深入聊了聊，给大家分享一些信息：

@wiltrain Wilson 是 cb 亚洲市场和VIP 的 Head，也是cb新加坡的元老了。从2020 年新加坡办公室只有他一个人，现在发展到一两百人。他牛津毕业，早期在香港的瑞信和渣打做投行，中文/粤语/英语三语 native，后来进入 crypto 做加密基金，之后加入 coinbase。先是在cb负责机构，crypto所有知名的大做市商几乎都是他的客户，现在又接过整个亚洲的零售和 VIP 业务，组建团队继续开疆拓土，他说整个公司现在从战略层面对华语区都非常重视。

@RolaCao_ Rola 负责华语区 VIP 和 KOL。她可能是我见过 crypto 里工作最拼的人之一，听她说已经连续几个月每天忙到 3 点睡，马不停蹄地帮华语客户处理各种问题。包括cb交易比赛请了熬鹰企鹅金明等几个华语交易员，华语用户的各种专属福利，都是她在争取。Rola 过去在 kucoin、bybit 都是销冠，据说当时进 coinbase 也是一千多个候选人里杀出来的选手，大家有什么cb的问题可以直接找她。

还认识了一个大哥 David Ko，据说是第一个升任cb VP的华人高管，以前是在 google 干了十几年的技术大佬，现在领导coinbase新加坡工程中心。cb产品层面在大力增加资源投入，都是在为承接巨大的增量用户做准备，尤其是华语市场。

总之跟几位交流完我还是相当期待，华语用户又多了一个安全的选择绝对是好事。我甚至在考虑，要不要用coinbase 替代一些硬件钱包的职能，毕竟最近一系列硬件钱包的狗血事件让我对硬件自托管失去了很多信任。

很多人可能不知道，coinbase 的BTC托管量是行业的绝对第一，托管了约300万枚BTC，贝莱德的75W枚 + Strategy 的85W枚中的将近一半 + 灰度的18W + 一堆其他ETF的，最后还有美国政府的BTC，都托管在 coinbase，这是我上次说黑客不敢碰 coinbase 的原因，因为有点惹不起😂。托管量第二名是币安70W枚，再往后是 Bitfinex，Fidelity 三四十万枚的水平，和cb差距都很大。

text:
Alchemy all over again? The economics and ethics of immortality.

For millennia, kings, emperors, and sheikhs have sought the elixir of life. Alchemists and charlatans made fortunes exploiting their fear of mortality.

What has fundamentally changed today?

Billionaires, sheikhs, and tech entrepreneurs are pouring billions into longevity research. Some CEOs publicly boast about doubling human lifespans: presumably starting with themselves, their inner circles, and their wealthy sponsors.

This reminds me of an old tale about Nasreddin Hodja, who promised a ruler to teach his donkey to speak in exchange for a generous reward and ten years of funding.

His reasoning? Within ten years, either he, the ruler, or the donkey would be dead.

The economics of extraordinary promises haven’t changed much, have they?

As an economist, I see a classic problem of asymmetric information, misaligned incentives, and delayed accountability. One can accumulate enormous wealth, prestige, and power long before being held accountable for the actual results.

While research into healthy aging is undoubtedly valuable, the extravagant promises of radical life extension deserve scrutiny.

Ironically, both failure and success raise serious concerns.

If these promises are unrealistic, are we witnessing modern-day alchemy, with AI replacing mystical potions?

If they are achievable, are we prepared for unprecedented wealth inequality, prolonged concentration of power, diminished intergenerational mobility, and increased pressure on our planet’s finite resources?

What concerns me particularly is the apparent grandiosity and resistance to accountability displayed by some individuals who claim to be engineering humanity’s future. I had a very heated debate a few days ago with one of those longevity tech bros.

Scientific achievement does not confer moral authority. Wealth does not confer wisdom. Grandiosity is not vision, and ambition is not evidence.

Meanwhile, some people, like @elonmusk , seem to have already cracked nature’s original version of immortality: reproduction. Having children allows our genetic legacy to live on. 🧬 Evolution figured this out long before Silicon Valley.

Before we attempt to extend human life indefinitely, perhaps we should ask what kind of society and whose power we would be extending.

P.S. Marrying a significantly younger woman is not a proven longevity intervention either. Kings, emperors, and sheikhs have been testing this hypothesis for millennia. The mortality rate remains 100%.

#Longevity #AI #Economics #Bioethics

text:
中国科技股午后集体暴涨，链上空头开始遭遇清算。

A 股科创50指数一度涨超 13%，创业板指涨超 10%，据 @TradingBeatsX 数据：MiniMax、智谱、宇树科技涨幅均超过 12%。

消息面上，今日国务院常务会议研究持续深化资本市场投融资综合改革工作，提出加力发挥「国家队」稳市作用、推动中长期资金入市、鼓励上市公司加大分红回购力度。
