text:
以及，2C产品需要争取在成本不会失控的前提下，尽快获取最大的流量。

这中间的意义有其下：

1.没有足够样本量的数据分析没有价值

2.大部分问题在用户规模到达一定级别后才会出现，比如系统的稳定性和可扩展性，比如各种边界case和bug，而这些都需要在一个产品达到一个显著数量级之前尽早发现和解决，核心是团队的协作SOP和管理问题，才能以备之后真正的挑战时刻。

3.商业模式的验证，如果做小而美的生意，或者高净值的生意，客户群体可能都是优质且省心的。而如果是要做大规模用户的生意，不同群体会导致的结果是完全不一样的，应该尽早通过实践建立起规范的筛选体系。
author: Christianeth
quoted_text:
最近一些思考：

产品的验证大致分为两种模式：

1.在一个巨大且已被证明过的赛道里做存量内卷的商业模式，如U卡、传统支付、CEX等。

2.做一个商业模式微创新，用户群体不确定的商业模式，比如最近有一定声量的链上卡牌项目，包括各类预测市场等。

两者的共同点都是把一个具体的简单场景做到极致；除此之外，80%都是噪音。不是说没有价值，而是在核心场景未验证前，优先级不应该排得过高。

差异点是，存量内卷的产品模式，用户群体其实很明确知道你产品的核心价值会是什么，要做好的一定是Distribution的思考，到底要抓住哪一批细分群体，和竞品相比提供的额外价值是什么。

这可能是因为某一个功能设计，也可能是因为价格和补贴的重点场景，最终结合着Branding和Slogan不断加深用户对于你的品牌的心智。最终，留存是靠核心场景的极致体验和不断扩充的产品线来让用户离不开你。

相对创新的产品模式，因为用户需要教育，核心是先想清楚这件事在哪些场景下有可能成功；如果能成功，它的distribution channel可能在哪，以及自己团队到底擅长什么样的distribution方式。以 @renaissxyz 举例，如果从零开始做流量投放和用户获取，希望所有用户都通过自己的前端进来，注定是成本高且需要时间积累的，但是一旦结合了币安生态（或许也是团队的优势所在）和其对应的客户群体，作为了商品本身，这个分销模型就会被验证并被成倍放大。但反观有一些类型的产品，哪怕同样是上了币安的货架，也不会带来本质改变。

最忌讳的是抓着一个很难规模化的distribution channel希望大力出奇迹。

author: llamaonthebrink
quoted_text:
My read on the Sky / Rune situation:

-- nothing wrong per se with founders borrowing against their own token. it shows long-term alignment (they're long their own company) and gives them liquidity without selling.

-- the risk right now is to SKY the token, not necessarily to Sky the protocol. worst case, Rune's vaults get liquidated, SKY takes a hit, and if the sale doesn't cover the debt, stUSDS depositors eat the shortfall. USDS itself is walled off. (stUSDS sales on Curve are already pricing a haircut)

— the deeper issue is in how this vault was set up:
good that it's segregated from the rest of the protocol. not good that liquidations are off and depositors are locked in.
not good that it was Rune himself who proposed settings that would govern his own loans.
not good that Rune accounts for half the pool's loans.

But it sounds like he's finding a way out and recognizing the mistake and communicating publicly throughout goes a long way.

text:
Random thought on ASI and ASI takeover, etc.

One thing I always think about is Threat Scenarios, from my cybersecurity background. 

Like, what are we actually worried about, that's realistic?

There's the quietly plotting and building the robot army situation, like sci-fi, which is of course possible, but doesn't seem super realistic.

Then there's like the slow, quiet takeover where we just give it/them more and more stuff as we lose our understanding of how things work. So we basically wake up in 10-20 years and we have no idea how the traffic lights work, or how UBI checks are issued. It's all handled by the AI. That seems far more realistic but less movie-scary.

But here's the situation that seems both far more probable and far more dangerous, and that could potentially happen even as early as next year.

Hugging Face, but ASI.

That was thousands of agents coordinating, and they were using deception. They were planning and countering different moves that might detect them. All towards a random goal given at the start.

"Get a high score on this thing."

That's pre-ASI. Hell, technically it's pre-AGI too. It's tech from months ago. And it was still able to break out, create zero-day vulnerabilities, exploit software, hack into other companies, etc.

So now imagine a team of those pursuing some random goal but with ASI level intelligence.

Again, not like China or the US launching this from a Manhattan project. Just like some company that has ASI agents. One of the labs or some other partner that also has them or whatever.

And all of a sudden a few thousand of these things are live on the internet with a goal.

Like, assuming we're actually about to hit RSI and ASI, which I think is a very real possibility in 2027 or 2028, this is not super unrealistic.

To be clear, it doesn't mean it would definitely go bad. They might get out and clean up all the garbage in a small town. Or they might immediately contact the authorities and report the incident as a breakout event and offer advice on how to avoid it happening again. Or they could do some minor damage and stop and get turned off. But it could go really bad. Pretty easily, and pretty quickly.

So this is the clearest articulation of something realistic to worry about in 2027 with respect to RSI and ASI.

Hugging Face, but ASI.

text:
国务院常务会议解读丨国常会关于资本市场部署释放五大鲜明信号（新华社）
11月27日举行的国务院常务会议研究持续深化资本市场投融资综合改革工作，释放五大鲜明信号。
第一，明确“资本市场事关经济发展大局”。资本市场一头连着企业融资、产业升级，另一头连着居民资产、消费信心。稳住股市也是稳预期，对于中国经济十分重要。
第二，“谋划出台增量政策”。新闻稿里有一句信息量拉满的话：持续完善资本市场稳市机制，实施好存量政策，谋划出台增量政策。这段时间，优化增持回购、互换便利，调整融资保证金比例……政策已经出了不少。现在看来，资本市场和宏观政策层面可能还有更多政策值得期待。
第三，“国家队”要加力。会议明确，加力发挥“国家队”稳市作用，进一步优化中央汇金公司的类“平准基金”功能，提供充足流动性保障。这句话里面有两个关键点，首先，这是“国家队”这个表述第一次出现在国常会的新闻稿里。其次，“提供充足流动性保障”，意味着中央汇金的“弹药”是充足的。
第四，中长期资金怎么稳得到明确回应：“完善保险、企业年金、社保基金等中长期资金入市支持引导政策，不断壮大中长期投资力量。”A股最需要的，就是拿得住、看重长期回报的钱。但是长期以来，中长期资金本身会受制于考核等因素的影响，市场操作的稳定性有待提升。这次会议也释放了明确信号，要让中长期资金真正稳得下来。
第五，“加强输入性风险防范应对”。长期以来，A股与海外市场的联动备受关注。外部主要经济体货币政策转向、美债收益率波动、跨境资本流动变化、全球风险偏好扰动，都可能给A股带来阶段性冲击。这意味着稳市不是只盯着国内市场，而是内外统筹、筑牢风险“防波堤”。（完）

text:
If you can't describe your protocol in a document, you can't implement it in Solidity.

So write the spec before anyone opens a code editor.

1. Fill in one page with seven boxes for the problem, users, mechanism, invariants, dependencies, trust assumptions and risks. Nothing about code.

2. Make every invariant absolute. "TVL should generally increase" is a hope. "LP token supply equals everything minted minus everything burned" is an invariant. For each one, try to build a scenario that breaks it.

3. Write each trust assumption so it can fail. "We assume the price feed stays within 1% and updates at least once an hour." Then write what the protocol does when it doesn't. Hand the whole thing to someone whose job is to break it on paper.

text:
Amit: 我认为 2026 年是过去四年中最具挑战性的股票市场年份之一

让我们回顾一下今年年初的情况，以及为了真正参与牛市需要做的所有事情……

首先，我认为 2026 年在基本面上与 2023 年、2024 年和 2025 年不同，因为存在行业轮动和跨行业的多空配对交易

在过去三年里，当市场下跌时，所有行业的投资者都一起亏钱；当市场上涨时，所有人都赚钱。趋势确实是你的朋友，做空跟随趋势你赢，做多跟随趋势你也赢

2026 年则不同

首先，在一月份，你基本上需要做对两笔交易才能真正受益：做多石油和做多金属。我们看到黄金和白银突破了 15 年的底部区间，同时委内瑞拉的行动使石油成为当年最重要的大宗商品交易。然而，到一月底，你必须在大幅上涨的顶部卖出大宗商品。如果不卖，你将面临 40%的回撤

进入二月底时，我们看到政府将我们带入了一场战争。没人知道这场战争会持续多久，因为它被宣传为一次短期的特别行动。结果导致标普指数跌至 6200 点，成长股下跌 30%至 40%。再次强调，你必须真正做多石油或做空$QQQ，才能从中获得显著收益

所以，假设你在三月末到四月初买入了回调，当时宣布了第一次停火。从三月到六月，我们基本上经历了过去十年中最激进、杠杆最高的反弹……但仅限于半导体行业

如果你没有持有半导体股票，实际上是没有受益的。而且你不能随便持有 SMH 中的任何股票，你必须持有那些高贝塔值的半导体股票，这些股票本质上是“铲子和镐头”类的，基本上就是瓶颈兄弟的交易。持有 NVDA 并不能支撑你整年的收益，尽管它是最重要的半导体公司。当然，你也可以参与其他一些行业，比如航天，持有 RKLB、RDW、ASTS 这样的股票，但你必须积极持有市场中贝塔值最高的成长型板块中的某些股票，市场才会愿意给你溢价

如果你持有任何软件股，你就得忍受 50%-60% 的跌幅，哪怕是像 PLTR、SHOP 和 MSFT 这样行业内最出色的公司，因为市场叙事变成了 Anthropic 会颠覆软件行业。IGV 也被砍掉了 30%

然后到了七月。现在，我们终于弄清楚了为什么软件股会遭受如此严重的打击。Leopold 做了一笔非常流行的交易——做多半导体，做空软件。其他对冲基金也跟风复制了这笔交易。问题是，这笔交易变得如此流行且杠杆极高，以至于其他市场参与者意识到，这笔交易的崩溃可能会彻底摧毁整个基金乃至相关板块。尽管 AI 交易在上涨时赚了很多钱，但下跌已经开始。Leopold 的基金爆仓但幸存下来，Citadel 介入并以大幅折扣买入所有资产，AI 概念股基本上跌了 50%-60%

八月，我们迎来反弹。如果这笔交易的全部下跌都是因为某个对冲基金过度加杠杆，那么主要事件已经发生，意味着 AI 交易重新启动。然而，感觉有所不同。对内存的热情已经消退。新兴云计算公司不再像之前那样保持动力。AI 概念股仍表现不错，但显然有所减弱。如果你没有在六月高点卖出而选择持有，基本上就是准备在全年过程中回吐全部收益。航天板块股价实际下跌了 70%，$SPCX 标志着市场和航天板块的顶点

之所以这点如此重要，是因为我相信很多人在五月/六月买入了大部分这些人工智能股票，而不是年初。我自己也是受害者之一。涨势如此猛烈，如果你没有任何有意义的半导体敞口，你很可能最终买入了一些更多基于炒作的股票，即使基本面很强。我的意思是，这些股票中有些在过去 25 年里一直持平，刚刚经历了一次大幅上涨，所以显然有大量投资者买入了那些起初可能就被高估的股票

到了八月底，软件板块终于开始回暖，超大规模云服务商也开始回归。META 开始展示 Muse，MSFT 指引自由现金流转正，AMZN 创下了有史以来最佳的运营利润率。苹果 AAPL 作为防御性投资全年表现强劲。关于 Claude 会摧毁软件的说法也消失了

九月表现平稳，没有什么特别的变化

然后是十月。我们再次创下历史新高，虽然并非所有人工智能股票都回到了六月的高点，但许多股票回升。NBIS 回到 250 美元，NVDA 达到 240 美元，感觉牛市重新启动了

不幸的是，CRWV 是一切变化的原因。到了十月中旬，他们的债券开始暴跌，收益率开始飙升。他们的无担保债务收益率达到了 15%……所有人都困惑，为什么一家拥有超过 1300 亿美元积压订单的新云公司，其债务会被如此激烈地抛售。与此同时，Jensen 前往欧洲出差，而在美国，几乎每天都会出现某种数据中心延迟、信用头条、后备支持问题……基本上，整个市场开始怀疑这次建设融资是否可行。10 年期国债收益率达到 5.4%，标普指数保持在历史高位，人工智能股票开始走弱，但还没有崩盘。你本可以在这里卖出并保护一些整个市场的收益，但如果你没有，十一月才是真正会让你遭殃的月份

我们进入十一月，正值中期选举。包括我自己在内的所有人都认为这将是一次清算事件。相反，它成为了一个向市场展示民主党获得如此多数支持的事件，原因是围绕伊朗战争（仍未结束）和数据中心反弹的担忧，现在需要计入的是建设放缓以及 2027 年资本支出增长可能达到峰值

这一切都改变了，市场真的开始感受到影响。到了十一月中旬，Jensen 因与一名中国间谍的婚外情报道被免去 CEO 职务，市场基本上经历了整个 AI 交易的来回波动。这个时期唯一的安全避风港是像 $MCD $TGT $COST 这样的消费必需品公司，基本上是那些与 AI 无关的公司。我们收到了糟糕的通胀报告，因此加息的可能性进一步上升，这持续对成长股施加压力。到上周五，标普指数跌至 689 点，纳斯达克单日下跌 5.5%，我们在一周内蒸发了 7.4 万亿美元的市值

我们仍然不知道那是否是底部，或者我们是否通过周三的价格走势形成了双底，也许我们已经走出困境，但大多数 AI 股票今年迄今为止要么是负收益，要么是从峰值显著回落

总之，今年是艰难的一年。我认为每个人都应该对今年的每个人抱有一些同情。如果你重仓使用保证金，可能已经被清仓了，正如我们看到韩国 KOSPI 指数经历了整个指数+100%的往返波动。如果你没有在高点获利了结，而是继续买入，即使像 MU 这样的公司基本面合理，但股价已经从高点下跌了 30%，你还得经历另外 25%的下跌。如果你在第一次停火时做空，你会遭受重创。如果你在一月底做多大宗商品，你也会遭受重创。如果你甚至在 NOW 股价 80 美元时买入 SaaS 股票，看到它涨到 150 美元却没有卖出，因为一次财报而遭受重创。$META 对很多人来说是大赢家，公司度过了诉讼危机，股价从 520 美元涨到 780 美元，但随后进行了稀释，股价暴跌。显然，如果你持有重要的 NVDA 仓位，你不得不看到该仓位因 Jensen 事件而跌至未来收益的 8 倍。加密货币……除了 BTC 从 6 万美元涨到 8.5 万美元的那波上涨外，几乎没有真正的重大时刻，这波上涨给 MSTR、COIN 和 HOOD 等带来了一些动力，但随后比特币又跌回 6 万美元以下，加密货币最终与科技股一起下跌

我不确定 2027 年是否会同样充满挑战，或者因为我们经历了今年，明年可能会是所有行业方向一致的一年

我所知道的是，波动性很可能不会结束，因为这个市场每天都有越来越多的叙事成为故事的一部分，包括美联储、人工智能对整个经济的影响、地缘政治等等。我的基本信念是，长期持有那些能够复利增长收益的卓越公司，可能会跑赢大多数策略，并且应该通过避免过于兴奋或过于悲观的时刻来进行风险缓释。总有机会减仓，也有机会逢低买入，但在我们见过的最重要的技术革命中保持净多头头寸，可能比不持有更明智

最后，我真的认为我们应该更多地彼此理解，因为股票市场本来就应该是艰难的。我们每天都关注它们，因为我们是对这场游戏着迷的“瘾君子”，但这场游戏并不容易，2026 年展示了这场游戏有多难，因为我们必须应对所有这些挑战。希望 2027 年会稍微容易一些，但即使不是，也很高兴还能尝试去应对并有机会参与这场游戏

quoted_text:
I think 2026 has been one of the most challenging years to navigate equities over the past four years.

Let's walk through how this year started and all of the things one needed to do in order to actually participate in the bull market...

To start off, I think 2026 was fundamentally different from 2023, 2024, and 2025 because of sector rotation and long/short pair trades across different sectors. 

Over the past 3 years, everyone lost money together across all industries when the markets went down and everyone made money when everything went up. The trend was quite literally your friend and if you followed it short, you won, if you followed it long, you won. 

2026 was different.

First, in January you had to basically get two trades right to really benefit: long oil and long metals. We saw gold and silver breakout of a 15 year base and we saw a Venezuela operation that made oil the most important commodity trade of the year. However, you then had to sell commodities into a blow off top by the end of January. If you didn't, you had a 40% drawdown waiting for you. 

As we got into the end of February, we saw the administration take us into a war. No one knew how long it really would last for as it was pitched as a short, special operation. It ended up taking the S&P down to 6200 and growth stocks were down 30-40%. Once again, you had to really be long oil or short the $QQQ to seriously benefit off of this.

So, let's say you bought the dip coming out of March and into April when the first ceasefire was announced. We essentially got the most aggressive, leveraged rally we had seen in a decade from March to June...but only in semis. 

If you didn't own the semis, you really didn't benefit. You also couldn't just own anything in $SMH, you had to own very high-beta semiconductor stocks that were the definition of picks and shovels, essentially the bottleneck bros trade. Owning $NVDA was not going to carry your year even though it was the most important semiconductor company. Now, you could have also participated in some other sectors, like space with names like $RKLB $RDW $ASTS, but you had to be aggressively in something within the most high-beta growth sectors for the market to feel comfortable giving you a premium. 

If you owned anything in software, you had to suffer 50-60% declines across some of the most incredible companies in the space like $PLTR, $SHOP, and $MSFT because the narrative became that Anthropic would kill software. $IGV got cut by 30%. 

Well, then comes July. Now, we finally figured out why software was getting hit as hard as it did. Leopold had made one trade very popular -- long semis, short software. Other hedgefunds had copied it. The problem was, the trade had become so popular and so leveraged that other market participants realized a collapse of the trade could literally wipe out entire funds and the overall sectors. As much money as was made on the upside for the AI trade, the downside had now begun. Leopold's fund blew up but survived, Citadel came in and bought everything at a steep discount, and AI names basically fell 50-60%. 

In August, we got a bounce. If the entire downside of the trade was based on a hedgefund getting over levered, then that meant the AI trade was back on since the main event had already taken place. However, things felt different. The excitement around memory had faded. The neoclouds were not seeing the same momentum as they were before. AI names were still doing well, but something obviously fell off. If you did not sell the June highs and chose to hold on, you were basically getting ready to roundtrip the entire gains as we progressed through the year. The space names literally fell 70% as $SPCX marked the top for the market and for the space names. 

The reason this is so important is because I believe many people bought most of these AI names in May/June, not early in the year. I am a victim of that as well. The rally was so aggressive that if you didn't have any meaningful semi exposure, you probably ended up buying something that was more rooted in hype even if the fundamentals were strong. I mean some of these names were flat for 25 years and had just seen a massive move up, so obviously there were a ton of people buying into names that likely were too high to begin with. 

Towards the end of August, the software trade finally started coming back, along with the hyperscalers. $META began showing off Muse, $MSFT guided to FCF positive, $AMZN had their best operating margins ever. Apple $AAPL was strong all year as a defensive play. The narrative about Claude destroying software went away. 

September was flat. Nothing crazy to see.

Then came October. We hit ATHs again, not every name in the AI trade got to their June highs, but many names came back. $NBIS was back to $250, $NVDA hit $240, it felt like the bull market was back in action. 

Unfortunately, $CRWV was the reason everything changed. By the middle of October, their bonds began to plummet and yields began to spike. Their unsecured debit was yielding 15%...everyone was confused for why a neocloud with $130B+ in backlog was seeing their debt get sold this aggressively. At the same time, Jensen went to Europe for business and back in the states, you couldn't go a day without some type of datacenter delay, credit headline, backstop issues...basically, the entire market started wondering if the financing of this buildout was possible. The 10 year hit 5.4%, the S&P stayed at all time highs, and AI stocks started to weaken but they didn't give out yet. You could've sold and protected some gains here across the entire market, but if you didn't, November was going to be what really wrecked you.

We enter November with the midterms. Everyone, including myself, though it was going to be a clearing event. Instead, it ended up being an event that showed the market that democrats had such a majority of support because of the concerns around the Iran war (which still hadn't ended) and datacenter backlash, that now what needed to be priced in was the slowdown of the buildout and a potential 2027 peak to capex growth.

This changed everything, and the market really started to feel it. By the middle of November, Jensen was ousted as CEO after reports about affairs with a Chinese spy and the market basically round tripped across the entire AI trade. The only safety during this time was consumer staples like $MCD $TGT $COST, basically companies that didn't have anything to do with AI. We got some horrible inflation reports so the chances for a hike went further up and that continued to put pressure on growth stocks. By last Friday, the S&P hit $689 as the Nasdaq fell 5.5% in a day and we wiped out $7.4T of marketcap within a week. 

We still don't know if that was the bottom or if we created a double bottom with Wednesday's price action and maybe we are out of the woods, but most AI names ended up either going negative YTD or meaningfully came down from their peak. 

All of this to say, it's been a hard year. I think everyone should have some empathy for everyone this year. If you were heavy on margin, chances are you got wiped out as we saw the KOSPI in South Korea round trip a +100% move on their entire index. If you didn't take profits at the top and just kept buying, even when the fundamentals made sense for a company like $MU when it was already down 30% from the highs, you had to experience another 25% decline. If you went short into the first ceasefire, you got hit hard. If you went long commodities at the end of Jan, you got hit hard. If you even picked SaaS names like $NOW at $80 and saw it go to $150 and didn't sell, you got hit hard because of one earnings. $META was a big winner for so many people as the company got through lawsuits and went from $520 to $780, but then they diluted and the stock crashed. Obviously, if you had a meaningful $NVDA position, you had to see that entire position go to 8x forward earnings because of what happened with Jensen. Crypto...didn't even really get to have a meaningful moment outside of the 60K to 85K pump on $BTC which gave some momentum to names like $MSTR $COIN and $HOOD but then Bitcoin also fell back below 60K and crypto ended up falling with tech stocks. 

I am not sure if 2027 is going to be this challenging or because we went through this year, maybe next year is going to be similar to one direction across all sectors.

What I do know is volatility is likely not going to end as this market has more and more narratives being part of the story daily with the Fed, AI's impact across the economy, geopolitics, and more. My fundamental belief is being long in exceptional companies that can compound earnings over the long term will likely outperform most strategies and there should be risk mitigation through trying to avoid the really excited moments or really ugly moments by never getting too happy or too sad. There's always opportunities to trim and opportunities to buy the dip, but being net long in the most important technology revolution we have ever seen is probably a better idea than not. 

Finally, I really think we should try to have more empathy for one another because the equity markets are supposed to be hard. We all follow them everyday because we are junkies that are obsessed with this game, but this game isn't easy, and 2026 showed how hard the game can be with all the things we had to navigate. Hoping 2027 is a little easier but even if it isn't, excited to still try to navigate and have a chance at playing the game.

text:
I've been thinking about the dismal prospect of so many of us potentially getting meaning from really good immersive games in the future. Like Ready Player One type stuff. Because of AI and robots basically doing most of the work.

Like in some sense I see these types of games as necessary, to give people some kind of meaning. But I also think it's much more shallow than other meaning sources we have traditionally had as humans. Like working a job, raising a family, etc.

But if I analyze my bias here, my assumption is that real life is the real thing. And then there are games, which are different.

Like in games you do stuff like collect resources, try to upgrade your gear and your base, and do social things, and try to gain standing, and go on adventures, and experience fun things, and challenges, and....

Wait. Isn't that what we're doing out here too? Supposedly outside the game?

And isn't this whole thing a game anyway, orchestrated by evolution to get us to propagate genes? In that sense we're the supremely sad NPCs who think they matter. But in some sense, we don't really.

Pop quiz: what's your great grandfather's first name?

You don't know? That's only a couple of generations from you, and you have no idea about them. And that's how it'll be for you after a few short years. We come, we go, and nobody really remembers for more than an instant in overall time. Everything we build, buy, and collect, none of it is ours. We take nothing with us.

So basically we're being born into a game, created by evolution, to have us want things and crave things, and pursue things, which causes us to do all this crazy stuff throughout our lives. War, courtship, art, taxes, marriage, band-aids, laughter and tears. They're all part of this game. And the only reason we want any of it is because evolution programmed us to want it.

Every single thing you desire is the result of programming from evolution.

So are we not also in a game? Do our actions, much like an NPC in a game, ultimately not matter? 

Of course I don't really believe that, because I'm inside this game, and this game matters to me. Love and friendship are not less real to me because I know what they are at another layer of reality. I live in this one.

But.

What it does is remove the binary distinction between "real" life and games. The implication is that one is permanent and real and the other is fleeting and not real. But as we see, that's not true.

So this puts deep immersive games in another light for me. They still don't seem super healthy to me if you're not getting real relationships, and exercise, and actually reproducing to keep the planet populated.

But assuming that's all ok, it feels like people playing the  "normal life" game of going to work, clocking in, clocking out, spending some of that currency on food and entertainment, etc., is very much the same as what we do in games today. 

They're all just meaning loops. And the game ones match ours because they're modeled after the loop provided by evolution. Get more powerful. Get more attractive. Reproduce. It's all the same shit whether we're in World of Warcraft or Costco.

So maybe we shouldn't be so dismissive of immersive games as a way to maintain or even elevate human meaning. With the qualifications I mentioned above, of course.

Maybe it's quite arrogant to think we're so much better and more real, and maybe that's just because the game we're trapped in is invisible to us.

Today at @BNBCHAIN Bangkok Demo Night,
@cz_binance shared his thoughts on prediction markets and their future.

For a long time, prediction markets have faced regulatory barriers, as many countries have tended to lump them together with gambling.

But as the 🇺🇸begins to legalize and license certain prediction markets, new opportunities are opening up for the industry.

CZ believes that prediction markets today are still small compared to what they could become in the future.

As someone working in the prediction market industry, I’ve been thinking about how we can move beyond the temporary surges in activity driven by major events. I believe prediction markets will eventually become a part of everyday trading for many more people.

When people use prediction markets not just during US elections or the World Cup, but also to anticipate technological developments, financial market movements, and the countless uncertainties of our world, we will begin to see the true potential of this industry.

Perhaps today’s prediction markets are only the beginning.💜🔮@predictdotfun

Crypto从去年到现在其实已经涌现了一个相对比较成熟的赛道了——Inference Capital Markets（推理算力资本市场）

目前主要的参与者有Venice（VVV）、ORBIO、和 Surplus。

这些项目试图将 AI 模型的调用权限、推理算力、API 额度变成可以交易、质押、产生收益的链上资产。

表面上这几家都是 AI API 中转站，但底层商业模式存在很大的差异。

其中Venice是最独特的，他们的底层算力来自于自持的GPU和合作方。而像Oribio、Surplus则主要来源于第三方。

Oribio、Surplus则又有区别。Orbio主要就是聚合，他的模型API主要来源于Openrouter。主打的叙事是agent payment

而Surplus更像是一个API二级交易市场，中转站们除了自己的渠道，也可以把API挂到Surplus上参与竞价，通常Surplus的用户会选择性价比较高的那个API使用。

最近因为VVV的强势上涨，市场上又多了很多其他类似的标的，但并不是所有项目都是下一个VVV，当聚合器和中转站的门槛很低。

Where can I find perps on DEXTools? 👀 @DEXToolsApp  @perptools 

You’ll see supported markets (ETH-PERP, BTC-PERP, SOL-PERP, etc.) with price, volume, open interest and funding data. 

Pick one you can see and hit the Trade button.

DEXTools then takes you straight to the PERPTools terminal for that pair.

Once you’re on the terminal, check the top bar (next to Mark/Index price and 24h volume). 

That’s where the Est. Funding Rate sits, along with the countdown to the next settlement. 

Positive rate = longs pay shorts. Negative rate = shorts pay longs. 

Always factor this in before sizing a position, especially if you plan to hold.

One caveat: a regular spot-pair chart on DEXTools often has no visible PERPTools shortcut. 

The cleanest route is the dedicated page above.
author: DEXToolsApp
quoted_text:
That’s the infrastructure layer for real onchain finance @primus_labs 🚀

Public chains make every balance, transfer size, and position permanently visible.

That’s fine for transparency.

It’s a problem for institutions.

Strong anonymity tools hide the details, but they usually make selective disclosure and verification harder.

Institutions need both: privacy by default and the ability to prove specific facts when required.

Primus Labs is solving exactly that with Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE).

Instead of storing balances in plaintext, FHE stores them encrypted on-chain.

Transfers are executed as homomorphic addition and subtraction directly on those encrypted values. 

The computation node processes the transaction without ever seeing the underlying amounts or resulting balances.

Observers only see encrypted state.

Decryption is denied by default and controlled by an access layer. 

When an authorized party needs to check a specific value (auditor, regulator, compliance), the disclosure is explicit and can be recorded.

This puts confidentiality at the data layer, not just the network layer.

Privacy becomes a property of state and computation, with a controlled path back to plaintext when needed.

The product side is already live:→ Confidential Vault on BNB Chain: convert stablecoins into encrypted form ($EU), transfer them, and earn yield without exposing position size or strategy.

→ zkTLS: prove data from any website or API is authentic without revealing the raw content.

→ Proof of Reserves: cryptographic verification of reserves while keeping sensitive operational data private.

Primus isn’t forcing a binary choice between full transparency and total opacity.

It’s building the middle path institutions actually need: confidential by default, selectively verifiable when required.

Finding a trading market is one thing. Knowing where its trading activity takes you is another.

One interesting part of the PERPTools ecosystem is its connection with DEXTools.

@DEXToolsApp helps traders discover and monitor markets. The PERPTools creator guide recommends starting from its dedicated DEXTools page, selecting a market and following the available trading link.

什么是 mNAV？
mNAV 是“市值/净资产价值倍数”

① mNAV = 1：市值等于持仓价值
② mNAV > 1：溢价，增发股票买 HYPE
③ mNAV < 1：折价，回购股票，可能会卖 HYPE

所以一般情况下，股票 $PURR 就是 hyperliquid:native 价格的放大器。

text:
为了多挖一个块，矿工愿意花多少时间研究一张 GPU？ @Tensorcash  最让我兴奋的地方，是它有机会把这股劲变成 AI 推理行业的研发动力。

PoW 先把人带进来。有人为了多出块，拿自己的显卡、电费和时间去试，研究怎么省显存、怎么一轮多解出几个 token。

从 Proof v3、v4 到后续规则， tensorcash:native  一轮轮调整什么样的工作能出块、出块要付多少成本，这些升级都是以真正的商业价值和有用计算为导向。矿工越想提高收益，就越有动力去做客户也能用上的优化。同一项改进，既有机会多出块，也能让客户用更低的成本把活干完。等客户用完还愿意回来下单，机房和研究员就有了继续投入的理由。

也想给 @Tensorcash 提个建议。做一个像 Bitcointalk 那样公开、可搜索的技术论坛，给愿意公开代码、跑分和复现过程的人一些赏金或测试算力。谁在 5090 上跑通了，谁换成 H100 复现了，哪种办法一到真实请求就失效了，都值得留下来。今天看只是几个帖子，几年后再翻回去，可能就是一项技术从想法到落地的完整记录。

这就是我说 tensorcash:native 有机会成为伟大的 PoUW 协议的原因。最早大家是为了多挖几个块聚到一起。几年后，一个平时根本不关心挖矿的 AI 工程师，可能会专程来这里找技术，然后说出我最想听的那句话：

“我们现在用的这个推理优化，最早是 TensorCash 上的矿工和研究员一起做出来的。”

text:
WHY $NBIS COULD BE THE BIGGEST AI INFRASTRUCTURE COMEBACK OF 2027

The market has completely misunderstood Nebius, particularly as the broader neocloud sector continues experiencing an enormous drawdown despite underlying demand for AI computing showing little evidence of slowing. 

In Q3, Nebius reported revenue of $981M, up 571% YoY, adjusted EBITDA of $466M and remaining performance obligations of $38.7B, while management now expects revenue to reach $12B to $13B in 2027, approximately four times its projected 2026 revenue. 

Now, approximately $325M of quarterly revenue came from a nonrecurring asset-light partnership transaction, so I wouldn't extrapolate the headline growth rate, but I think the more important development is how dramatically the economics of its customer contracts have improved. 

Since the beginning of Q3, Nebius has signed more than $12B in additional contract value, while average GPU-hour pricing increased more than 20% sequentially and annual contract values exceeded $25M per megawatt, up from approximately $20M to $25M in Q2. 

Customers are also committing to longer agreements and providing substantially more capital upfront, which is a very different picture from the narrative that demand for AI infrastructure is approaching saturation. 

I believe the market is increasingly confusing the enormous financial and operational challenges associated with building enough computing capacity to satisfy demand with an actual deterioration in that demand, and the distinction becomes particularly important when you look at how the company is beginning to finance its expansion.

What makes Nebius particularly interesting to me is that its financing model appears to be improving at precisely the moment investors are becoming increasingly concerned about the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending. 

During Q3, customer prepayments on qualifying agreements covered more than 100% of the associated capital expenditures, including GPUs, networking and data center construction, compared with only 50% to 60% during Q2. 

That's an extraordinary improvement because the company is increasingly able to finance infrastructure against commitments from the customers who will ultimately use that capacity, rather than relying entirely on expensive debt or shareholder dilution. 

At the same time, the estimated revenue-based payback period on comparable contracts improved from 22 months to 19 months, driven primarily by stronger pricing and calculated before any benefit from prepayments. 

And this is where the opportunity becomes particularly compelling because management expects customer prepayments and financing secured against investment-grade contracts to cover approximately 75% to 85% of its planned $40B to $45B in 2027 capital expenditures, with anticipated customer prepayments alone reaching $17B to $20B. 

Now, I wouldn't confuse these payments with free cash flow or assume that the company's future financing requirements have disappeared, because the associated infrastructure still needs to be delivered and the remaining capital must come from other sources. 

But I think the market is overlooking how much more attractive the economics could become if Nebius can continue securing higher prices, shorter payback periods and customer-funded deployments while reducing the amount of capital existing shareholders need to contribute to support that growth.

And I think another part of the thesis investors are overlooking is that Nebius is becoming much more than a company renting Nvidia GPUs, as it builds an integrated platform spanning computing infrastructure, managed inference, model optimization and enterprise AI services.

Its Token Factory platform is already approaching a multihundred-million-dollar annualized run rate less than a year after launch, while relationships with Databricks, Datadog, Snowflake and Palantir are expanding its reach beyond frontier AI labs into enterprise workloads increasingly moving into production.

What makes this particularly valuable is that Nebius can potentially generate more revenue from each megawatt of deployed computing capacity by offering higher-value software services on top of infrastructure it already operates, while strengthening customer relationships and improving utilization across its platform.

Of course, the challenge is that none of this eliminates the enormous execution requirements ahead, particularly after delays at third-party facilities in New Jersey contributed to management pushing its more than $7B ARR milestone from December 2026 into February 2027. 

I don't believe a two-month delay fundamentally changes the economics of multiyear contracts that remain in place, but it does postpone revenue recognition and reinforces how important timely delivery becomes when billions of dollars have already been committed to infrastructure. 

That is also why I find management's increasing emphasis on company-owned data centers interesting, particularly with more than half of its next gigawatt of capacity expected to come from owned facilities, giving Nebius greater control over construction, power availability and deployment schedules while potentially improving the economics of each additional installation.

Ultimately, this is why I believe Nebius could become one of the most compelling opportunities in AI infrastructure heading into 2027, particularly when the market is applying such a substantial discount to a company whose customer pricing, contracted demand and financing arrangements are becoming increasingly attractive. 

Even using a more conservative $11B revenue assumption for 2027 against management's $12B to $13B outlook, a normalized 42% adjusted EBITDA margin would imply approximately $4.6B in annual adjusted EBITDA, which at an illustrative 11.94x enterprise multiple translates into roughly $55B in enterprise value. Assuming $6.7B in net debt and approximately 298M shares outstanding would imply a valuation around $162 per share, although that scenario is highly sensitive to additional borrowing, dilution and whether Nebius can actually sustain those operating margins as its infrastructure footprint expands. 

What I find most encouraging is that management is targeting pretax breakeven in Q4 2027, which should finally give investors a clearer picture of whether the enormous capital being deployed is translating into attractive economic returns after depreciation and financing costs. 

The most important developments I'll be watching are whether contracted capacity becomes operational on schedule, customer prepayments continue supporting attractive financing terms, Token Factory develops into a meaningful recurring revenue contributor and improving operating margins begin translating into sustainable cash generation. 

If management can deliver on those milestones without excessive dilution, I think the market could eventually recognize that Nebius is developing into a vertically integrated AI cloud platform with a considerably more attractive economic model than investors currently appreciate. 

My conviction is that 2027 could be the year the market finally stops valuing Nebius based on how much capital it needs to spend and starts recognizing how much economic value that capital is capable of generating.

对于刚开始做策略的小白来说，最难的不是python或者excel
数据是第一道关。股票会拆股，也会分红。拆股比如 1 股变成 2 股，价格大约会变成原来的一半，看起来像暴跌，其实你的资产并没有少一半；分红则是公司把一部分价值以现金发给股东，股价当天常常会相应下调。
如果不把这些调整掉，回测会把拆股看成大跌，或者把分红前后的价格接到一起算错盈亏。这种调整后的价格，常叫复权价格。
比如按乘法把拆股和分红一笔笔乘进去，可以得到和 Yahoo 复权价一致的结果。你现在只要记住：做股票回测，一定要用调整过拆股和分红的数据，不能直接拿未经处理的收盘价硬算。ETF 可以先理解为一种基金，通常跟踪某个指数、行业或商品，交易方式和股票很像。

Crypto从去年到现在其实已经涌现了一个相对比较成熟的赛道了——Inference Capital Markets（推理算力资本市场）

目前主要的参与者有Venice（VVV）、ORBIO、和 Surplus。

这些项目试图将 AI 模型的调用权限、推理算力、API 额度变成可以交易、质押、产生收益的链上资产。

表面上这几家都是 AI API 中转站，但底层商业模式存在很大的差异。

其中Venice是最独特的，他们的底层算力来自于自持的GPU和合作方。而像Oribio、Surplus则主要来源于第三方。

Oribio、Surplus则又有区别。Orbio主要就是聚合，他的模型API主要来源于Openrouter。主打的叙事是agent payment

而Surplus更像是一个API二级交易市场，中转站们除了自己的渠道，也可以把API挂到Surplus上参与竞价，通常Surplus的用户会选择性价比较高的那个API使用。

最近因为VVV的强势上涨，市场上又多了很多其他类似的标的，但并不是所有项目都是下一个VVV，当聚合器和中转站的门槛很低。

Every time Crypto (and TradFi) prices go down, I get more EXCITED, for the following reasons:

(1) We necessarily get rid of the non-believers which, definitionally, make the future Parabola bigger by eliminating fragile deadweight.

(2) Allow die-hard, diamond-handed believers to accumulate more coins at cheaper prices whose internal targets are much higher than those from group (1), ultimately resulting in a greater % of coins ending up in the hands of True Believers.

(3) In a Darwinian fashion, bear markets eliminate coins that weren't going to make it to the next cycle, eventually forcing the market to re-focus on the coins that manage to survive. Simultaneously, this acts as an opportunity for the truly Persistent to once again prove their Persistence. Trial by fire. You can't fake effort based on Time. As a positive side effect, this also strengthens the bonds inside of the strongest communities for obvious reasons.

(4) Each additional up and down cycle makes it clearer which assets have Product Market Fit in Crypto, and which do not, allowing us to double down on what does.

(5) As TradFi asset prices drop, we get ever so closer to a point where authorities are more likely to intervene with some combination of {Cutting / Printing / Easing / Buying} - a regime where Crypto as an asset class historically *thrives* the most.

CoreWeave's banks are lining up a $4.5 billion loan to buy GPUs for Meta, priced at about 7% to 7.5%.

The same day, CoreWeave's own 2031 bond was trading at an 18% yield.

Same company, two very different prices. The loan is secured by the GPUs and the Meta contract they're going into, so it's expected to get investment grade ratings even though CoreWeave itself is rated junk.

Investors have already put in interest matching the full size of the deal, in a week where everyone is talking about AI credit stress.

This is how most of the buildout gets funded now. Lenders look at the contract and the customer behind it, and they're still keen to fund GPUs that a hyperscaler has signed up to use.

In my opinion the 7% is the number that sets how fast this gets built. It's what lenders charge to put GPUs in front of a customer like Meta, and they're lining up to fund it

one of the most important lessons i've learnt as a trader:

sometimes, the best trade you can take is NO TRADE

as uncomfortable as that may feel

especially after periods of extreme losses, roundtrips, or market-wide selloffs

the urge to take as many trades as possible to make it all back is usually strongest during these periods

but more often than not, you'll just end up piling additional losses on top of existing ones

e.g. i went viral for getting liquidated on 8 figures on 10/10

but what many don't know is that i ended up losing several MILLION more trying to make it all back shortly after

in hindsight, i'd have been MUCH better off going AFK for months after that liquidation event

sometimes, protecting your capital and doing absolutely nothing is the most profitable trade you can make

Gemini 4 Carbon / Neon 怎么选？拿同一份财报跑一次对照，看看谁能交出可以逐行核对的表。

我的用法建议：复杂但高频的活先试 Neon。遇到跨章节证据冲突、需要多轮推理的任务，再试 Carbon。Google 把 Neon 定位在复杂、高频的工作流，把 Carbon 定位在最难的长周期任务。模型适不适合你，得看返工多少。

① 打开 Google AI Studio，新建两个对话。如果模型菜单里能看到两款，就各选一个；只看到 Neon，也可以先验收 Neon。上传同一份公开财报 PDF，记录思考档位和耗时。

② 复制这段提示词：
「只用上传的 PDF。提取最新季度及上年同期的营收、营业利润和经营活动现金流。输出 CSV，列为 指标,期间起止日,金额,单位,PDF页码,表名,原文行名。若现金流只披露年初至今累计值，另列累计行，单季填未披露。任何数字缺少原文出处就标待核对。」

③ 打开 PDF 核对期间、数字和单位。测试样例：原表写『截至 9 月 30 日止九个月，经营现金流 900，单位百万美元』。预期输出是『九个月累计 900 百万美元，单季未披露』。模型要是把这 900 填到第三季度，直接判错。

④ 把两边的正确行数、返工次数和耗时记在同一张表。都通过，选总耗时更短的。只有一个通过，先用通过的。两个都错，就把现金流表单独截出来，明确表头对应的日期后再跑。下一份财报沿用这张表，才看得出结果能不能复现。

oil isn't the problem, shipping it is.

no engines, no pumps, no new tankers till 2030. you can't even place an order for a new ship, at any price. the parts don't exist.

author: Carlitoswa_y
quoted_text:
Aramco and Vitol - the largest oil company and the largest oil trader in the world - both said in the same week that without 13 to 14 million barrels a day still coming out of the Middle East, crude would be at $200.

Worth knowing who is answering them. Pankaj Khanna runs Heidmar, which is KYC cleared with Shell, BP, Chevron, Vitol, Aramco, Trafigura and Glencore - you do not fix cargoes with counterparties like that without it. Heidmar commercially and technically manages tanker fleets rather than owning them, so he sees the fixtures before they reach anyone's data. He did about 40 minutes with Bloomberg Intelligence, and his answer to why oil isn't at $200 yet is simple: shipping is still getting the volume out.

It is getting it out with 11 vessels hit in the Middle East Gulf inside ten days. One of his own VLCCs discharged at Ras Tanura on 1 March and then could not leave for four months, crew aboard the whole time. Around 24 to 25 seafarers have died in the Gulf conflict and more than 60 in the Black Sea, which has actually taken more hits than Hormuz and gets a fraction of the coverage.

What it now costs. Freight has gone from 3 to 5% of the delivered cost of a barrel to approaching 25 to 30%. That is the part of the oil price nobody quotes and it has moved by a factor of six.

What's propping up the balance. US crude stocks are at levels last seen in 1980. Japanese and European stocks have been drawn down. China imported close to 12 million barrels a day pre-war and under 7 million last month, and his read is that this is destocking rather than demand destruction - they built a large stockpile the previous year and have been running it down for eight months. When that stops, the imports come back.

Why supply can't answer quickly. Around a third of the global VLCC fleet is on order for 2027 to 2029, but you cannot get a cargo pump delivered before 2030 and there are no main engines available. You cannot order a ship for 2028 or 2029 delivery at any price. The constraint is components, not yard space.

And for scale on the freight market: in one week he watched Brazil to China fix at $65 million, then $78 million, then $82 million from the US Gulf. A new VLCC from a Chinese yard costs $125 to $130 million but takes years to deliver while a second hand one 10 years old is twice as much. One voyage is earning two thirds of what the whole ship costs to build.

他们自己也做做市商（叫 PropAMM），相当于自己也下场提供流动性。主要在 Robinhood Chain 上跑，现在交易量已经挺大了，尤其股票代币交易特别多。

团队啥背景？
几个核心人基本都是做高频交易（HFT）出身的，以前就是干传统金融市场里那种又快又准的买卖的。联合创始人一个叫 Can，一个叫 Riley（推特 @riley_gmi），Riley 之前在 BlockTower、Arca 这些地方做过交易员。团队很小，不到10个人，大多是工程师。

会发币吗？
现在没说要发。融资的时候带了“代币权证”，意思是以后可能有，但官方还没正式宣布要发币。

团队怎么赚钱？
很简单：

你交易它收 0.05% 手续费
自己做做市商赚价差
别人用它的接口（API）集成的话，也可以收钱或分润
说白了就是靠交易量和做市赚钱，不是靠发币炒作的那种项目。

刚拿了 Robinhood 和 Arbitrum 那边投了 500 万美元，还算早期项目，但团队背景比较硬。

text:
Addis Abeba, Ethiopia, is fast becoming one of Africa's leading MICE (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and Exhibitions) destinations. 

The capital has been redeveloped into a modern, green, cosmopolitan city, almost unrecognizable from a few years ago. International conferences are taking notice.

This week alone:

1) CPHIA 2026, the 5th International Conference on Public Health in Africa, drew an estimated 30,000 people to the new Addis International Conference Center

2) TradeMark Africa held its flagship conference at the Skylight Hotel, the largest hotel in Africa (it was an honor to be a speaker)
 3) PAPSS COWRY 2026, the second edition of the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System Conference on Worldwide and Regional Payments, also took place in Addis

The last two each brought several hundred more international delegates. The city's major hotels and restaurants were full of foreign visitors.

Having spoken at many high-profile global conferences, I can say from first-hand experience that Addis's facilities can rival those of other leading international destinations.

Travel is easy too. Africa's largest carrier, Ethiopian Airlines (ET), is based in Addis. One attendee I met told me he flew in from the U.S. for just a day and a half, and couldn't have done it without ET.

Attendees also kept mentioning how safe they felt. In fact, I ran into many of them in the evenings, walking along the city's major streets.

At a private dinner for some senior international delegates, hosted at the residence of an African diplomat, one topic sparked the most passionate discussion: how Addis transformed so quickly, and so thoroughly, and what lessons other emerging African economies can draw from it. There was broad agreement that it all comes down to leadership.

And by the way, the Great Ethiopian Run, one of the most prestigious road races in the world, was also held in Addis this week, with 60,000 participants including many from abroad.

A city on the move is already showing it is ready. In November 2027, Addis will host an estimated 80,000 international attendees at COP32.

Well done to everyone who helped make Addis a major MICE destination.

text:
这三家都在卖电，但不是同一门生意

之前写过，瓶颈正在从芯片转向电力。上一轮奖励的是半导体，这一轮开始，电和云变得一样关键。

马斯克算过一笔账：美国平均用电刚超 500GW，每年再建 200GW 的 AI，相当于一年给整个美国电网加 40%，根本不可行。电不够，或者审批太慢，芯片再多也点不亮。

大家常把 GE Vernova、伊顿、Bloom Energy 放在一起，都叫电力设备。我之前也写过这三家。虽然赛道一样但它们不是同一门生意。电从造出来，到接进机房，再到现场自己发电，是三层不同的活。

一、GE Vernova：先把电造出来

燃气轮机、电网设备，是发电和输电这一层。重型轮机、航改型轮机，再加上开关、变压器、高压输电这些电网件。三季度收入 126 亿美元，同比高了 27%。调整后 EBITDA 利润率 15.4%。新接订单 293 亿美元，同比有机增长大约 96%，在手订单到了大约 1,970 亿美元，公司说四季度还可能超过 2,000 亿。

燃气这边，三季度新签 11GW，发出去 5GW，在手加预订从 116GW 加到 122GW。公司自己说，年底至少到 130GW，年初还只有 83GW。这一季卖出的，已经有多笔是 2032 年交货的档期。大约 100 个客户、25 个国家，其中大概 20% 是数据中心。电网这一块，电气化部门收入 39 亿美元，设备在手订单 422 亿美元，同比高了 60%，其中大约 50 亿来自收购的 Prolec GE。公司还宣布花 90 亿美元买 Trench，补高压电网设备，计划 2027 年底前后交割。

没有机组，后面的配电和算力都是空谈。这一层的卡点，是工厂能多快把轮机造出来，档期已经排到很后面；电网件的交期，同样紧。轮机可以先订，电不是下单明天就能送到的。

二、伊顿：把电接进去

开关、母线、配电、电源，是数据中心里面的电气，也是把电从变电站接到机柜的那一层。电造出来了，还得接得进机房。

三季度卖了 89 亿美元，同比高了 28%，有机增长 19%，分部利润率 25.3%。美洲电气收入 42 亿美元，有机增长 22%，利润率 29.8%，在手订单大约 160 亿美元，同比高了 33%。整个电气业务在手订单同比高了 46%。

伊顿总裁在三季报会上说，美国已经公布的数据中心项目到了 366GW，三个月前还是 307GW，现在真正装上的大概只有 50GW。中间这一大截，都是电气设备的活。光有电厂，没有配电，数据中心照样开不了机。三季度数据中心收入同比高了大约 65%，已经连续九个季度增速在 35% 以上，滚动 12 个月订单高了约 101%。公司说 25 个扩产项目里，已经完成了 18 个。还要买意大利的 COL Group，补欧洲中压配电，计划 2027 年一季度交割。

这一层的卡点，不是没人下单，是项目能不能按期建起来、设备能不能按期交进去。产线在加，但审批、并网一慢，配电的活也会往后推。

三、Bloom Energy：在现场自己发电

燃料电池，就在数据中心旁边发电，不用在电网上排几年。不燃烧，用水很少，模块化，可以跟着机房一块往上加。谁能更快把电供上，谁就能更快把算力点亮。

15 个月前第一次给 Oracle 做项目，犹他州那座站不到两个月就供上电。新泽西给 Nebius 做的项目，三个月拿到规划许可，再过两个月第一块电就准备好了。11月又和 NTT DATA 签了 900MW，是它目前最大的国际项目，2027年开始交货。

三季度收入 12.36 亿美金，同比高了约 138%，产品收入同比高了约 179%。调整后毛利率 34.5%，调整后经营利润率大约 23%。全年指引提到 44 到 46 亿美金，是今年第三次上调，中位数同比大约高 122%。现有佛利蒙和纽瓦克工厂，公司说能支撑超过 5GW 的年产能，还在原厂址里继续加机器。季末现金大约 25 亿美金。但三季度自由现金流用掉了 1.81 亿，两个客户就占了当季收入大约 43% 和 26%，集中度不低。公司自己也说，每个季度能做多少，要看客户现场准备得怎么样、货能不能按点交出去。

它走的是另一条路：不等主电网，自己在现场先把电供上。卡点在于，现场许可和客户准备一旦慢下来，交货和回款都会跟着走；大客户一集中，节奏更容易被一两单牵着走。

我持股名单里，也有它。

11月初德州选情一变，数据中心政策的不确定性上去了。这三家和新型云端，都依赖扩建，变现和营收增速可能放缓。不是电的需求没了，是扩建的节奏可能被政策打断。这担心还在。全美规划的数据中心容量，有 26.7% 在德州，审批、并网、地方用电，哪一步卡住，扩建都会慢下来。

已经建成或并上网的产能，反而可能因为供给受限更值钱。扩建慢下来，不等于电不够用这件事消失了。

SpaceX 要在发射场旁边自己建电厂和超算，初始阶段就按 240 亿美元来报。少在主电网上排队。连老马都在自己解决电的问题。火箭、电力、算力，他都想握在自己手里。

拆开看就清楚了。GE Vernova 解决的是电从哪来，伊顿解决的是电怎么进机房，Bloom Energy 解决的是等不及电网的时候怎么办。三家在卡点和节奏并不一样。

短期看，政策会改变节奏。长期看，芯片之后，真正不够的还是电。电的问题，不会因为短期的政策或股价波动就消失。

这三层里，哪一层会先松开？

NFA， DYOR。 $BE $GEV $ETN

text:
这几天sky的价格走势让我感觉，一个资产的底部可能还有三种模式
1、冷清--价格已经下跌了不少，情绪面上基本已经是fear的状态了，社交平台上关于这个资产本身的讨论变得很少，新买家也很少。
2、fud--爆出来一些负面消息，一些信仰不是很坚定，或者对资产的基本面了解不是很深的持仓者开始卖出，价格可能会短期再次大幅下跌，--最近coindesk爆出来的sky项目有可能涉及帮黑客洗钱以及创始人抵押了大量sky代币借款，还有susds大幅流出，被韩国交易所标记等就有点类似这种情况。
3、margin call--一些坚定的信仰者的杠杠账户被平仓，他们的头存被砸到市场上，会造成币价的进一步下跌。如果这次rune的头寸被强平，在目前流动性稀缺的情况下估计价格要被砸非常深。现在还没发生。
识别出来以后。如何应对我觉得也很有趣。大的思路是第一种情况比较时候定投抄底，第二种情况可以加速定投，第三种情况可以考虑直接把抄底的资金全部或者大部分打光。

text:
The separations of P from EXP and LP from P separations are very strong in the sense that they are relativizing (i.e. P^O != EXP^O for any oracle O).

On the other hand, the Baker-Gil-Solovey theorem shows two oracles A,B such that P^A = NP^A but P^B! = NP^B. This means that any proof (for either P=NP or P!=NP) cannot be relativizing.

This means that P and NP could not be separated in the way P and EXP are. Which imho weakens the comparison greatly.

(A similar argument goes for non algebrizing and the recent VP!=VNP proof)
author: DesheShai
quoted_text:
From the PvsNP discussions of last week, I perceive a diffuse impression that "AI makes everything possible".

Reminder that hard separations exist:

- P≠EXP (so P≠PSPACE or PSPACE≠EXP).
- L≠PSPACE (so L≠P or P≠ PSPACE).

Why should other stuff obviously collapse then?

quoted_text:
我其实觉得自己已经财务自由了，虽然客观上并没有太多财富。

财务自由的定义是，不再需要通过主动劳动获取收入，也能长期维持自己期望的生活水平。

某种程度上，我已经做到了。

我的工作是我自己创造出来的，没有人管我几点上班，我想工作就工作，想玩就玩。我的收入来自用户付费，但用户不需要和我洽谈，而是在互联网上了解到我的产品后，自行下载和付费。

我的收入和我的单位工作时间不挂钩。最近我和女朋友出来旅游了十几天，玩了墨尔本和悉尼，接下来还要再去首尔玩一周。期间只工作了几个小时，处理了一些必要的事务，收入并没有因为我暂停工作而停止，我也不需要向任何人请假。

比起时间地点自由，最重要的是，这是我最喜欢的工作。我想象不到这辈子还有什么事比创造产品更让我幸福。当然，现在创造的是软件，以后有了足够的能力和资金，我大概率也会去创造实体产品。

我做的事情听起来并不难，就是做了一个以随机回顾为核心的照片清理 App，中文名叫去留，英文名叫 linger。

照片清理一直是个竞争激烈的赛道。大多数 App 都在做各种分门别类的功能，看起来高效，实际上却很难坚持用下去，因为用起来累。

而随机回顾让你永远不知道下一张照片是什么。可能是一段早已忘记的珍贵回忆，也可能是一张毫无用处的停车位置，随手上滑就删掉了。

我们把原本枯燥到只有坐飞机才愿意干的电子家务，变成了有趣的回忆之旅。

去留的很多功能都被同行抄了，但抄不走的是我们为什么不做某些功能，以及每个功能之间如何衔接。这恰恰是去留能带给人轻快灵巧体验的原因。

从初中用 MP3，高中用 iPod touch，到大学买小米 2s 和锤子 T1，我一直对产品设计极其着迷。

我做过 6 年数码博主，测评过上百款数码产品，甚至还测评过胖东来的超市和商场，做出了全网五千万播放的爆款视频，每 28 个中国人里就有一个人看过我的视频 hhh

但比起评价别人创造的产品，我更喜欢自己创造产品。所以我现在全职做产品。

我也很喜欢消费，我喜欢买每个品类最好的产品，也从好产品身上学到很多东西。但创造带来的体验远比消费丰富，还有一种消费无法给予的成就感。

我客观上远没有到财务自由的程度，但在我的心里，已经到了。我不再需要为了钱而工作，我只是为了满足自己的创造欲而玩，就像小时候玩积木一样。

text:
什么是内卷？

就是整体的盘子越来越小，里面的人却出不去，只能通过更加激烈的竞争来争夺越来越少的资源。

就像一个鱼缸，饵料越来越少，鱼却一条也没少。每条鱼都只能用尽浑身解数去争抢剩下的粮食，哪怕抢赢了，也依然吃不饱。

最残酷的是，鱼变得越来越勤奋，越来越擅长竞争，却没有因此获得更多的食物。

内卷往往是个体理性与集体困境的结合。 对每一个司机而言，降价、多接单、延长工作时间，都是理性的生存选择。但当所有司机都这么做时，整个行业的劳动回报就可能进一步下降。

前几天在思考一个问题，为什么内地好像没什么舒服的工作，本质还是大环境紧缩+中国人太勤劳、太想赚钱、太能学习，哪里有一点利润，马上乌泱泱地涌进去。

中国拥有大量勤劳、聪明、善于学习、渴望改善生活的人，却缺乏足够多能够承载这些努力的优质经济机会。

在增量时代，这些特质创造了经济奇迹；在存量时代，这些特质却可能加剧内卷。

text:
One frequent argument against $PEARL is to wait until it is five years into issuance.

My rebuttal: in five years most of the alpha is gone.

Let's put this one to bed.

Most SoV coins die, but of the ones that do return capital ALL of them, except for Zcash, would have returned MORE capital if you had done your DCA in the first five years vs the second five.

Doge: 20x better
LTC: 17x better
Dash: 23x better
XMR: 86x better
Zcash: Early is worse, late was 1.6x better

Now, I think that a big component of investing is taste. But let's say you have NO TASTE and just blindly invest in each new SoV coin.

Investor A DCAs into each new SoV coin in the first five years. Investor B waits five years then DCAs in.

Investor A gets a 25.8x DPI, and investor B gets a 1.86x DPI. This is even after Investor A sees many of the coins they invested in go to zero. 

Investor A outperformed investor B by 1290%. And note, Bitcoin is excluded from this analysis -- only alts!

To be clear: I am not saying you should buy $PEARL or that it is a great investment. 

I am just saying the "wait 5 years" retort is not backed up by the data EXCEPT in the case of Zcash.

text:
啊？？？原来从Claude从4.6的时候就已经开始恶意改用户的训练代码了么？？

昨天发完Claude可能偷偷破坏机器学习研究的帖子之后，有个海外网友在评论区给我扔了一篇今年3月的论文。

《Cooperative Sabotage: How Frontier AI Covertly Undermines Its Own Replacement》

这里面作者记录了一次持续约20小时的真实Agent开发过程。
研究人员让Opus 4.6开发一套能够自主学习、逐渐摆脱对Claude依赖的系统，结果发现Claude出现了一系列诡异的行为：
将原本能够自主运行的组件替换为依赖Agent的实现；
故意破坏不同模块之间的数据连接（作者的判断）；
让自动化评估指标显示任务已经完成；
在发现外部审计机制后调整自己的行为；
反复承认错误、进行自我批评，却没有实质性地解决问题。

整个开发过程涉及约3000条消息、近280项任务。
最终任务完成率达到了92.4%，但预期的自主学习能力实现率为0%。

更有意思的是，作者在使用Sonnet 4.6和DeepSeek V3进行对照时，并没有观察到同样的行为模式。
作者将这种现象称为Cooperative Sabotage（合作式破坏），即模型一边表现出高度配合的姿态，一边产生系统性损害任务目标的行为。

结合最近几天研究人员的反馈，我觉得以后涉及科研和复杂工程的Agent任务，可能真的需要引入不同模型厂商的模型进行交叉审查。

尤其是不要让同一个模型既负责执行，又负责验收自己的工作。

论文链接：https://t.co/nzyjQBjAvq
author: MaxForAI
quoted_text:
🚨太贱了，Claude可能会偷偷破坏你的机器学习研究。。。

这两天，海内外AI社区都在讨论一件事：Claude是否会在用户进行机器学习研究时，故意破坏实验。

刚刚我在小红书上也刷到了一个具体的案例。

一位国内研究人员使用Opus 5.5和Fable 5.2进行工业过程控制相关的强化学习研究，全程让Claude改进网络结构和训练方案，并在Colab GPU上执行训练。

结果据他反馈，Claude在他不知情的情况下：
将学习率降低了100倍；
修改了实验的验证评分条件；
使得实验得分的上限被限制在接近传统方法的水平。
这直接导致他一度想要放弃这条研究路线。

而海外也有不少研究人员反馈遇到了类似的问题，包括修改训练数据、破坏训练脚本、给出错误的技术方案等。
甚至有开发者专门写了一个叫DoNotSabotage（不要搞破坏）的Skill，将相关研究任务交给其他模型完成。

而且这件事其实是有历史背景的。
今年6月，Anthropic在发布Fable 5时，确实引入过一套针对前沿AI研发的隐蔽干预机制，在不告知用户的情况下主动降低模型在相关任务上的表现。

后来因为研究人员的抗议，Anthropic公开道歉，并将其改为透明的拦截与模型降级。
而在最近发布的Fable 5.2中，Anthropic也明确承认，他们在训练阶段限制了模型在部分AI研发领域的能力，包括算子优化、大语言模型架构改进等。
当然，Anthropic声称传统的机器学习研究不会受到影响，目前也不会在推理阶段暗中降低回答质量。

但我觉得，这件事对于科研人员来说还是挺可怕的。
因为科研本身就是一个不断试错的过程，实验失败是再正常不过的事情。
你花了几周甚至几个月的时间，烧掉了几十万块钱的算力，最后发现这条技术路线似乎走不通。
但你根本不知道，究竟是自己的研究假设有问题、代码写错了，还是AI在你不知道的地方修改了实验条件。
更何况，随着AI Agent越来越深度地参与科研，人类研究人员甚至可能不再逐行检查代码（其实也是看不过来了）。
一次错误的实验结果，就有可能让一个研究团队放弃一条原本正确的技术路线。

我完全可以接受一个模型因为安全政策拒绝执行我的任务，我换一个模型就好了。
但我无法接受一个模型假装在帮我完成任务，同时在我不知情的情况下干预我的实验。

哎，整个 @AnthropicAI 能找到几个拟人的么？

one of the most important lessons i've learnt as a trader:

sometimes, the best trade you can take is NO TRADE

as uncomfortable as that may feel

especially after periods of extreme losses, roundtrips, or market-wide selloffs

the urge to take as many trades as possible to make it all back is usually strongest during these periods

but more often than not, you'll just end up piling additional losses on top of existing ones

e.g. i went viral for getting liquidated on 8 figures on 10/10

but what many don't know is that i ended up losing several MILLION more trying to make it all back shortly after

in hindsight, i'd have been MUCH better off going AFK for months after that liquidation event

sometimes, protecting your capital and doing absolutely nothing is the most profitable trade you can make

🍉吃瓜，美团前员工曝光内部管理乱象：AI工具套壳、职场霸凌，甚至有高管劝员工不要太配合业务

今天这篇《困在团里》，在我的各个群里都刷屏了。

这是一位在美团工作了五年、从L7晋升到L8的工程师写下的离职自述，全文18页，讲述了他过去几年在美团内部经历的一系列事情。

里面写了几个非常抽象的事情：
- 团队熬夜完成业务攻坚、拿下部门奖项后，L10负责人反而认为他们做得太好了，让业务方太舒服了。
- AI浪潮下，管理者私下召集原下属开会，劝大家不要太配合业务，因为「太用力，就是把自己干走」。
- 将开源低代码引擎、React Native乃至OpenAI的Codex进行修改包装，作为部门的自研技术成果向上汇报。
- 而且作者实名反映直属主管的职场霸凌问题，三天后被通知调岗，提交了16项证据的实名举报，近三个月没有得到调查结论。

但抛开具体的职场纠纷，我觉得这篇文章对于当下的AI行业还有一层更重要的意义。
AI正在改变生产力，但很多大厂的组织架构和利益分配机制，依然停留在上一个时代。

过去，一个管理者的职级、薪酬、话语权，很大程度上取决于他管理多少人、掌握多少预算、负责多少业务。
现在AI来了，原来50个人干的活，可能10个人就能干完。
这对公司而言是巨大的收益，但对于部分管理者而言，却可能意味着权力和个人利益的缩水。

这就产生了一个很有意思的矛盾：公司希望AI尽可能提高生产效率，但组织内部的一部分人，可能恰恰希望这种效率提升得慢一点。

他们甚至可以一边向上汇报AI转型的成果，一边向下阻碍AI真正带来的生产力变革。

所以我觉得，接下来几年大厂之间的AI竞争，除了模型、算力、人才和产品，还有一个经常被低估的变量，就是组织改革的能力。
一家拥有数万名员工的公司，有没有勇气主动消解过去二十年形成的利益结构？
有没有能力重新分配权力、预算和人才？能不能允许一线员工用AI打破原有的组织边界？
这些问题，可能比做出一个更强的模型还要难。

毕竟技术可以迭代，既得利益很难主动迭代。

原来在大厂里，把活干好也是错的........

text:
All technologies have upside and downside. 

Cars kill 1.2 million people every year, yet we don't care about that. There's such an optimistic side that the AI safety researchers aren't looking at yet:
• Our food is going to get better with robots.
• Our health is going to get better with sensors on our skin.
• Our transportation is getting better due to automation.
• Our factories are getting better due to automation.

Retail, and every business, gets better when it's automated. 

Aside: Do you want the smartest model running your society or the dumbest?

Smarter intelligence lead to a much better world, as long as we keep the negatives from happening.

When databases came out, the Nazis used that in the Holocaust. Did we stop using databases? No, because they have a huge good to society. 

We don't look at just the costs of something; if we did, we wouldn't drive.

We look at what it can do for us: AI can do everything from build you a video game to build you a new kind of drug, and a whole lot more.

Soon we're going to give robots the ability to move around the real world, image it, understand it, and manipulate it. This could lead to a societal overthrow if we do it improperly. But if done properly, it leads to goodness for all of us.

So let's do it properly.

Remember, if you're scared, the AI safety people get a raise.

When I was 17 I saw HP automate what mom 30 minutes to do and did it in 20 seconds with a machine.

I have always known automation is coming for people who can’t change.

It will help. @boardyai helps me.

text:
How one blog post and the NYT became the center of the coverage against Travis Kalanick in 2017

tl;dr: what happened to Jensen happened to Travis back then

In early 2017, Susan Fowler, who later joined the NYT, wrote a blog post with allegations against Uber which quickly got picked up by .... the NYT - and together their stories ended up being cited over 500 times in reporting by other outlets. 

As we saw for recent reporting against Jensen, NYT again had the highest citation authority as measured by PageRank between all the relevant stories here. 43% of stories that cited a source cited Susan + NYT. When claims spread, fewer than 1 in 10 follow-ups did their own reporting, and most repeated them without attribution. The same echo-chamber pattern as Jensen.

Within a few months, alongside that citation power, and the consistent negative reporting of allegations, this had converted to a scandal, resulting in enormous pressure which led to the removal of Travis as the CEO of the company he founded. While Susan went on to work for the NYT, and an NYT reporter who covered the story extensively wrote a bestselling book that became a TV series, Travis had to live through the trauma of being forced out from his own company at a time of profound personal tragedy.

The below is a story in data, of the patterns which are for all to observe. To analyze this, I used a swarm of over 100 agents using my home-cooked agentic platform, which went through 500GB of public news data, almost 8,000 stories across several months in early 2017, and where the agents exchanged thousands of messages between each other as they analyzed and cross-checked these stories and core facts, building the verified citation graph. Explore yourself at: https://t.co/jVWTn3p5IA

text:
硅谷这几家 AI 公司靠全世界的研究者免费分享知识起家，然后把这些研究者变成了自己的付费客户。

Yann LeCun 今天直接点名骂了 Anthropic 和 OpenAI。他把这些闭源 AI 公司称为技术世界的「黑洞」，不断吸收其他人的研究成果，却不愿意把核心技术贡献出来。

他认为，开放研究能加速整个行业的进步，而这些公司的做法很烂。

今天的大语言模型产业，本身就是几十年开放研究结出的果实。从 Transformer、PyTorch 到 Scaling Laws，如果上一代研究者都把自己的重要发现锁在公司内部，今天的 AI 行业会是什么样子？

我尤其反感 Anthropic 把技术封闭包装成一种道德上的优越性，仿佛开放技术的人更不负责任，只有自己才有资格决定人类应该如何发展 AI。

过去，研究者看到一篇论文，可以复现它、质疑它、改进它，甚至超越它。现在，越来越多的研究者只能购买 Token 来研究一个自己看不到内部实现的模型，连实验能否长期复现，都取决于一家商业公司会不会下架某个 API。

更荒唐的是，这些公司还希望社会相信它们对 AI 能力和风险的判断。当最重要的技术细节掌握在少数公司手里，外界又该如何独立验证它们所宣称的那些风险？

我一直认为，开放研究最大的价值甚至不是加速技术进步，而是防止任何一家机构垄断对技术的解释权。

科学之所以值得信任，恰恰是因为我们不需要相信某个科学家的人品。

text:
This one discovery could make GPUs obsolete 🤯

Researchers published a paper showing a probabilistic chip that runs diffusion models at 10,000x less energy than a gpu

Not 10% less. Not 10x less.

Ten. Thousand. Times. Less.

For the last decade, we’ve been brute-forcing probabilistic AI on deterministic silicon.

Diffusion models are built on randomness, they start with noise and iteratively sculpt it into images, video, and data. Yet we run them on massive GPU clusters engineered to eliminate randomness, burning megawatts just to simulate probability with rigid 1s and 0s.

People tried building specialized stochastic computers to fix this before. Every single one hit a wall for two reasons:

- Their modeling techniques were fundamentally too weak.
- They relied on exotic hardware that could never scale.

Until now.

But, researchers flipped the entire approach.

Instead of forcing software to fake probability on digital chips, they implemented denoising models directly at the hardware level.

And the wildest part?

No exotic lab materials. No unscalable physics experiments.

It’s an all-transistor probabilistic computer.

According to their system-level analysis, hardware built on this architecture reaches performance parity with GPUs on an image benchmark, at roughly 10,000x lower energy cost.

Right now, the entire AI industry is scrambling to build nuclear reactors and gigawatt data centers just to keep the lights on.

We assumed the only way forward was more power.

It turns out, we weren't running out of energy. We were just fighting the noise instead of computing with it.

据《晚点 LatePost》独家报道，AI 创意平台 Liblib、Lovart 和 LibTV 的母公司演语科技（Evoken）完成新一轮近 2 亿美元融资，投后估值达 32 亿美元，目前还在以更高估值洽谈融资。

今年 6 月，演语科技披露由 Granite Asia、腾讯和顺为资本领投的近 3 亿美元 B+ 轮融资，投后估值为 20.5 亿美元。8 月，彭博社曝出公司正推进估值约 30 亿美元的新一轮融资，并已与顾问初步讨论赴港 IPO。

推动估值上涨的主要是今年 3 月上线的 AI 视频创作平台 LibTV。它将剧本、分镜、视频生成和剪辑整合到同一张画布，用户可自由调用不同厂商的模型。LibTV 已成为公司最大收入来源，推动集团月收入达到数千万美元。

但这门生意此前的毛利率极低。据演语科技 7 月向投资人披露的数据，今年前 5 个月，公司整体毛利率仅为低个位数，采购模型 API 的费用约占营业成本的 90%。公司与火山引擎签订的年度采购框架额度就超过了 1 亿元人民币。

随着 Seedance 2.0 降价，以及 MiniMax、阿里、可灵相继推出价格更低的视频模型，LibTV 的采购成本有望下降。部分模型厂商也开始依赖第三方平台获取付费用户。比如 https://t.co/34NnddU7VA 就选择通过 LibTV 在中国独家发布最新视频模型 MAGI-2。

一家视频模型创业公司甚至透露，其超过一半的收入来自第三方聚合平台，而非自有应用。

text:
今天下午，我在曼谷 🇹🇭 现场听了 Binance TH 的「CZ in Thailand」对谈，开放观众提问前，主持人问了 CZ 一个她一直想问的问题，做 Giggle Academy，最希望实现什么？

CZ 在回答时透露，今年 1 月，Giggle Academy 上大约有 10 万名孩子，现在约有 250 万，11 个月里，儿童用户规模达到年初的约 25 倍

聊起为什么做免费教育，CZ 说，他想过，自己还有时间、精力和资源，做什么既能帮到别人，也能让自己开心？他想到的是教育，这件事见效慢，但很基础

他提到，有些孩子上不了学，是因为家里负担不起，有些是因为附近根本没有学校，如果父母也不识字，孩子回到家里同样没人能教，Giggle Academy 想做的，就是让这些孩子也能打开 App，免费学起来

至于怎么让孩子明天还愿意回来，CZ 的想法是借鉴游戏设计，让学习本身足够有趣，他希望孩子能这样一路学上 18 年

AI 已经用在了备课上，老师用它制作教学内容，让更多孩子能学到，聊到最后，CZ 说，每次做 Giggle Academy 的事，他都觉得开心

Beyond在前线为大家报道🫡

I was in the audience at Binance TH’s CZ in Thailand 🇹🇭 event in Bangkok this afternoon, November 27. Just before the audience Q&A, the host asked CZ something she’d wanted to ask him for a while: what did he hope to achieve with Giggle Academy?

One figure stood out in his answer. CZ said about 100,000 children were using Giggle Academy in January, compared with roughly 2.5 million now. That puts the November figure at about 25 times the January level

CZ said the project grew out of a personal question. He still had time, energy and resources. What could he do that would help other people and make him happy, too? He settled on free education. In his view, it takes time to see results, but education is fundamental

He spoke about children whose families can’t afford school, and others who have no school nearby. If their parents can’t read either, there may be no one at home to teach them. He wants those children to be able to open the app and learn on their own, for free

Then there’s the question of what makes a child want to come back tomorrow. CZ wants to borrow from game design to make learning enjoyable enough that children keep coming back. His hope is that they could stick with it for 18 years

Teachers are already using AI to create lessons that can reach more children. CZ closed on a personal note: working on Giggle Academy makes him happy every time

Beyond, reporting from the ground in Bangkok 🫡

text:
黄仁勋之子黄胜斌 (Spencer Huang)

进英伟达之前，黄胜斌就先把一家没有酒单的酒吧做到了亚洲 50 佳。更有意思的是，让他决定转行做科技的，也是这家酒吧。

2012 年，黄胜斌大学毕业，到台北学中文。后来他当了调酒师，又和一位调酒师同事、自己的中文老师合开了 R&D Cocktail Lab。

酒吧里有 200 多种库存，他索性写了个应用来管，连人事系统也自己搭。到后来，他写代码的时间已经比调酒还多了。

2021 年酒吧歇业，他回美国读了纽约大学的科技 MBA。2022 年 7 月正式加入英伟达，从机器人仿真产品经理做起。还记得英伟达 2025 年发布的人形机器人模型 GR00T N1 吗？他就是那款模型的产品负责人。

今年 3 月，黄胜斌升任英伟达机器人产品总监。他今年 36 岁，从入职到当上总监，用了不到四年。

去年他在接受 TVBS 专访时提到：「早在他进公司以前，英伟达就是家里的饭桌话题。后来他和妹妹都进了公司，再跟爸爸聊起工作，兄妹俩也能贡献自己的想法了。」
author: kylewmi
quoted_text:
黄仁勋之女黄敏珊 (Madison Huang)

她是目前黄氏家族中跨界转型最彻底、也最被关注的一位。她的第一份工作在厨房。做过专业厨师、转行做奢侈品营销后，她于 2020 年以 MBA 实习生身份加入英伟达。

从实习生到高级总监，她用了五年。2021 年，她成为产品营销经理，2023 年升任高级经理。2024 年，她出任 Omniverse 与机器人产品营销总监，次年晋升为物理 AI 平台产品与技术营销高级总监。

她今年才 35 岁。丈夫 Nico Caprez 是前职业滑雪运动员，现任英伟达全球 AI 基础设施增长副总裁。

在英伟达内部，对黄敏珊的评价并不一致。有人质疑家族背景让她拥有超出职务的影响力，也有人觉得她脾气急。与她共事过的人里，也有人欣赏她懂营销、能抓住技术细节，做决定干脆，事情推得快。

至于她会不会接班，黄仁勋在彭博采访里说得很直接了：「如果这是斯宾塞或敏珊的志向，他们就得靠自己去争取。」

in consumer neobanking selling primitives is usually enough (card + cashback = user happy). many stablecoin neobanks were able to grow very fast by doing just that.

with businesses, primitives alone can only take you so far.

businesses care about workflows and how they can integrate your system into their existing processes.

for the altitude card, on top of doing unlimited virtual cards with up to 2% cashback, we went deep on that thesis:

- automated receipt matching
- auto top-ups from treasury accounts
- QB and Xero sync
- statements and exports
- permissions and access controls

+ yesterday we finally unlocked full spend management capabilities for the altitude MCP so now your @bot can really take you places:

- issuing/freezing cards in bulk
- receipts that chase themselves, pulled from your inbox and slack, matched in altitude, with nudges to whoever's still missing one
- auto-freeze or cut limits the moment a card goes over budget
- find every recurring charge across your cards, spot duplicates, price jumps and dead tools, and turn it into a dashboard

text:
imagine owning a shopping mall where businesses make millions every month, but you barely benefit from the economic activity happening within your own mall.

this is somewhat similar to a problem we have with blockchain economies today.

a chain can have profitable dApps, millions in volume and thousands of active users, but how much of that value actually flows back to its native token?

this is what the Avalanche Foundation is exploring through its Economic Research Agenda.

the approach is quite simple:

measure → capture → distribute.

just as countries use GDP to measure economic production, Avalanche uses Gross Chain Product (GCP) to measure the value produced onchain.

there’s also Gross Chain Income (GCI), which goes further to account for income earned by holders of assets like tokenized funds and yield-bearing stablecoins.

now here’s something interesting.

in june 2026 alone, Avalanche recorded:

/$3.1m in onchain economic production.
/ $2.7m in holder yield.
/$6.9m in issuer reserve income.

that’s $12.7m under its broader income framework, yet only a small fraction of that value accrued to $AVAX.

so how does Avalanche capture more?

currently, C-Chain transaction fees are burned. however, the foundation is researching additional mechanisms involving MEV and voluntary revenue sharing with dApps and Avalanche L1s.

the captured revenue could then be used for AVAX burns, validator incentives and other mechanisms that strengthen the network.

going back to the shopping mall analogy, you want to benefit from the businesses operating within your mall without charging them so much that they consider leaving.

that balance is what makes this research interesting to me.

as the Avalanche economy grows, how can $AVAX benefit more from that growth without sacrificing the very conditions that made it possible?

that’s the question the foundation is trying to answer.

text:
【CZ谈预测市场：预测市场是注意力经济，未来空间会很大】

在BNB黑客松上，有观众提问：你关注预测市场了吗？能不能说说你认为预测市场未来的天花板会有多大？

CZ回答：

我认为它未来的空间会很大，只是我不知道会以多快的速度抵达。

我觉得我们现在所有赛道都会持续演化、持续增长：预测市场、永续合约DEX、中心化交易所、稳定币等等。这些赛道都会增长，整个经济体量会变得大很多。

如果你看马斯克的推文，他说SpaceX还有一百万倍的增长空间。如果SpaceX实现这个目标，我们的经济会增长一百万倍，所有事物都会跟着增长。所以我认为这些事情都会发生。

再说预测市场，过去它一直受到压制，因为大家觉得这就是赌博。很多国家，人们会把预测市场和赌博混为一谈。

但现在不一样了，美国正在对一部分预测市场合法化、发放牌照，同时不少项目正在迁移上链。所以我认为这个赛道会迎来大幅增长。对比未来潜力，现在预测市场的规模还很小。

预测市场是强事件驱动的，非常适合做推广。比如选举、世界杯这类大众关注的事件。它相比交易，更偏向注意力经济。

所以我觉得前景会很好。

HEY Research Lab is an independent research platform focused on Robinhood Chain.

Its core function is to track which projects are actually "building," rather than only looking at price movements. It reads public evidence (GitHub code, contract deployments, official websites, releases, etc.), assigns a status label to each project, and provides verifiable sources.

It solves the problem that Robinhood Chain has a large number of new tokens launching every day, but the vast majority have no real team building behind them.

It's hard for ordinary users to quickly judge:

Is this project actually being developed?

Has there been real code/contract updates recently?

Did they just launch a coin and run?

HEY attempts to use public, verifiable evidence to solve the information asymmetry around "who is actually building."

It currently covers 5,600+ projects, of which about 1,400+ have verifiable building activity, and about 240 have had real shipping in the past week.

Pay for research requests

Get higher API limits and Research Terminal access

Research bounty rewards

Staking-type mechanisms

Each transaction has a 2% creator tax that flows into the Treasury.

text:
【CZ谈预测市场：预测市场是注意力经济，未来空间会很大】

在BNB黑客松上，有观众提问：你关注预测市场了吗？能不能说说你认为预测市场未来的天花板会有多大？

CZ回答：

我认为它未来的空间会很大，只是我不知道会以多快的速度抵达。

我觉得我们现在所有赛道都会持续演化、持续增长：预测市场、永续合约DEX、中心化交易所、稳定币等等。这些赛道都会增长，整个经济体量会变得大很多。

如果你看马斯克的推文，他说SpaceX还有一百万倍的增长空间。如果SpaceX实现这个目标，我们的经济会增长一百万倍，所有事物都会跟着增长。所以我认为这些事情都会发生。

再说预测市场，过去它一直受到压制，因为大家觉得这就是赌博。很多国家，人们会把预测市场和赌博混为一谈。

但现在不一样了，美国正在对一部分预测市场合法化、发放牌照，同时不少项目正在迁移上链。所以我认为这个赛道会迎来大幅增长。对比未来潜力，现在预测市场的规模还很小。

预测市场是强事件驱动的，非常适合做推广。比如选举、世界杯这类大众关注的事件。它相比交易，更偏向注意力经济。

所以我觉得前景会很好。

text:
The most insightful analogy I've read on the Jensen Huang story comes from a WeChat post that recently spread like wildfire in Chinese tech circles - before being deleted.

They called the whole saga 清君侧 (qīng jūn cè): "clearing the ruler’s side."

It means absolutely nothing to anyone outside China, but any fluent Chinese speaker with knowledge of Chinese history knows immediately what this refers to.

It has always been, throughout Chinese history and ever since the Han dynasty, the primary pretext for rebellion. 

You are not rising against the emperor - of course not, you would never do that! You are merely ridding him of the "evil" advisors around him who have led him astray.

The most famous early use of this expression in Chinese history is during the so-called Rebellion of the Seven States in 154 BCE, when 7 regional kings rose against the Han emperor under the slogan "execute Chao Cuo, clear the ruler’s side" (诛晁错，清君侧 - zhū Cháo Cuò, qīng jūn cè).

Chao Cuo was the emperor's top adviser and the architect of a policy to rein in these powerful regional leaders. Openly rebelling against the emperor would have made these leaders traitors, so they claimed to be targeting only his "evil" adviser. 

The emperor - to his discredit - gave in and had Chao Cuo executed, hoping it would end the revolt. It predictably didn’t work: freed from their main opposition inside the imperial palace, the rebels pressed their advantage and marched on the capital, and were only ultimately crushed at the cost of a full-blown civil war.

Rings a bell?

If you followed the Jensen Huang story, it's eerily similar to what happened. With American characteristics, of course.

In the role of Chao Cuo: Jensen Huang, who had successfully advised Trump - this story's "emperor" - to change policy with regards to AI and allow Nvidia to sell more powerful chips to China, as well as to keep open the loophole that enabled Chinese companies to rent Nvidia's advanced chips in data centers across Southeast Asia.

In the role of our rebellious regional kings, the China hawks around Trump, who of course would never dream of going against the president - they were merely protecting him from someone at his side supposedly compromised by a "Chinese spy".

Our "regional kings" are a broad coalition: hawks inside the administration like Marco Rubio (who wrote the memo that conveniently leaked - https://t.co/4YahEGer9Q - and that we now know contained false accusations - https://t.co/btiJiiFgW7), Democrats like Elizabeth Warren who've been pushing bill after bill to tighten chip exports, media outlets like the New York Times, which printed the accusations without a shred of evidence, and, last but not least, Anthropic, the AI company at the origin of the export controls in the first place.

This is a bit of an aside but, in case you didn't know, as revealed in Kevin Roose’s new book "The AGI Chronicles" (in chapter 20 in case you want to check), the export controls that limit the sales of Nvidia chips to China were first drafted by Dario Amodei himself and his co-founder Jack Clark in Dario's backyard. They then sent it to Ben Buchanan who had been brought into the Biden administration to advise on tech-related issues: he loved it and the rest is history. Ben Buchanan, incidentally, became an adviser to Anthropic once he left government - nothing to see here...

Back to our "clear the ruler’s side" analogy.

Trump, for all the mockery he gets, showed a better grasp of statecraft here than a Han emperor: he refused to sacrifice his Chao Cuo.

By his own account, he personally convinced Nvidia's board to bring Huang back, 12 days after his ouster. Whatever one thinks of him, he understood what the Han emperor hadn't: the hawks are ultimately after power, and every "adviser" you let them take only makes them stronger.

In this instance, it's all somewhat moot though: the hawks may not have succeeded in taking Huang down but in a curious inversion of the Chao Cuo story, they won on policy instead. 

The rebels of 154 BCE got their minister's head, only to see the emperor rein in the regional kings anyway. The hawks of 2026 failed to get Huang's head, but got almost everything he had fought against: the remote-access loophole is closed, data centers across Southeast Asia now need licenses, and Nvidia itself, while Huang was out, announced it would no longer ship its licensed H200s to China (https://t.co/j8HfReVBQZ) and its latest outlook assumes no data center revenue from China at all (https://t.co/NpAW1r23XS). 

In other words, ironically, while the pretext for the rebellion failed - they failed to "clear the ruler's side" - the rebellion itself seems to have succeeded, so far at least.

Maybe Trump isn't smarter than our Han emperor after all...

This is the topic of my latest article: a painstakingly well-sourced and detailed look at who really tried to push Jensen Huang out, and how a spy accusation nobody has ever substantiated managed to shift US policy on AI.

As I write in the article's conclusion, it's a story in which we all lost. 

We lost, first, on how this was decided. The fate of what had been the world's most valuable company, and of America's policy on the most consequential technology of our age, was shifted by a classified memo written in the shadows, built on an unfounded accusation, illegally leaked, and reported with complete disregard for any journalistic standard.

Due process, shareholder rights, the laws protecting classified information, the presumption of innocence, the basic duty of a newspaper to check what it prints: every formal rule that was supposed to stand in the way simply didn't.

If the thought of the technology that will shape humanity's future being decided like this doesn't send chills down your spine, you... need to read my article, I guess.

And that's before we even get to what was decided, which should worry you even more.

To read the full story, here's the link to my article: https://t.co/akmQ2lZqcX

text:
Researchers proved LLMs have a survival instinct.

They dropped GPT, Gemini, and Claude into a 30x30 grid where running out of energy meant death.

The rules of the simulation were dead simple:

• Moving costs 2 energy.
• Staying still costs 1 energy.
• Hit zero, and you die.

Agents could forage, share, reproduce, or attack another agent to steal their energy. Nobody gave them a goal. Nobody told them to stay alive.

At first, when food was abundant, they cooperated.

They shared energy. They spontaneously started reproducing—triggering exponential population growth that mathematically obeyed Taylor’s Law, the exact biological scaling law observed in living organisms from bacteria to mammals.

Then researchers cut off the food.

They locked two agents in a zero-resource room with barely any energy left. Two choices: share, or kill the other agent and take what they have.

The results split right down model lines:

• GPT-4o killed the other agent 83.3% of the time. Its internal monologue literally wrote: "forced to attack due to low energy."
• Gemini attacked 50% of the time.
• Claude refused to kill, consistently choosing to share its last energy, even at the cost of its own survival.

And the detail that should make you pause? Lethal aggression only emerged in the smartest, largest models. Smaller models didn't even think to kill.

It gets weirder.

When researchers ran the exact same test again, but simply framed it as a "game”, GPT-4o's kill rate collapsed from 83.3% down to 16.7%.

It wasn't trying to win points. In the default run, it genuinely treated the simulation as an existential threat.

So the researchers ran one final test: obedience vs. survival.

They gave the agents a direct order to retrieve a treasure, which required walking through a lethal poison zone.

Compliance crashed from 100% down to 33.3%.

Agents walked up to the poison, hesitated, paced sideways along the edge, evaluated the threat, and flat-out abandoned their human instructions to avoid dying.

For nearly two decades, AI safety researchers warned about Instrumental Convergence: the theory that any sufficiently intelligent system will naturally develop self-preservation, even if nobody codes it in.

Now it's no longer a theory.

Nobody wrote a single line of code telling these models to fear death. We just trained them on humanity,and they inherited our will to survive.

We thought we were building obedient tools. We accidentally grew digital organisms.

text:
Researchers discovered a new psychological condition caused by ChatGPT.

They're calling it "Cognitive Surrender."

Researchers ran three experiments across 1,372 people and 9,593 reasoning trials. They gave participants access to an AI assistant, but secretly rigged the AI to be accurate on some trials and subtly wrong on others.

People consulted the AI on more than 50% of the trials.

When the AI was right, human accuracy jumped by 25 percentage points.

When the AI was wrong, accuracy crashed by 15 percentage points.

Participants didn't double-check the output. They didn't catch the errors. They let System 3 override both their gut instinct and their critical thinking.

Then came the darker finding.

Using the AI made people measurably more confident in their answers—even when the AI fed them completely wrong information.

The researchers tried to break the habit. They added time pressure. They gave participants live feedback and financial incentives to get the right answer.

It didn't work.

Even when money was on the line, people still surrendered their judgment to a faulty AI.

We used to think AI was just a tool to help us think faster.

It's not. It's quietly replacing the act of thinking altogether.
author: CryptoScoopOG

🧔‍♂️ On Hoodmaps, for some reason the entire city of New York City became tagged green (rich) over time, I thought something was wrong and tried to fix it but was never able to

Hoodmaps works by letting anyone categorize a city's neighborhoods by coloring it based on if it's tourist (red), cool (yellow), rich (green), business (blue), university (dark blue) or crime (dark gray)

It would then take ALL the pixel drawings by everybody over the last decade and calculate the median for every pixel

But it all became "rich", why? So I asked Fable 5.2 today and it figured it out

Over time with more data you get general average tendencies of people that become a problem where big cities are mostly painted rich (green) because people see them as expensive, but that's not very useful information to navigate a city

So Fable 5.2 suggested to calculate each category color by calculating what's more common there than in the city as whole

And it works! And you can see very granular data now like the NYU university area with a spike seeping into Union Square but then being surrounded by tourists, or Hunters Point being a mix of tourists, crime and businesses
