text:
现在大家对于“量子计算”，有一种薛定谔的恐慌：

平时觉得遥不可及，但只要顶级圈子里稍微漏点风声，大家又会瞬间草木皆兵，生怕一觉醒来所有私钥和密码一夜归零。

这两天，前 OpenAI 研究员、量子计算权威 Scott Aaronson 就在 X 上掀起了这样一场风波。

起因是他在自己博客评论区随口提了一句，说听到不少传闻称 OpenAI 或 Anthropic 已经找到了用普通电脑快速分解大质数的算法，这意味着支撑现代互联网安全的 RSA 加密可能要被攻破了。

消息在圈内疯传后，他赶紧回去把那行字划掉，强调“谣言就是谣言”，但紧接着又补了一句：
他依然“几乎确定”这两家实验室手里确实握着某些密码学上的重磅突破。

持币者一看到“AI 破解加密学”，往往第一反应就是比特币和以太坊钱包要危险了。

但这其实是个误区。

网页证书、银行系统和日常电子签名靠的是 RSA 加密，传闻里 AI 突破的正是它依赖的大数分解难题；

而比特币和以太坊用的是另一套基于椭圆曲线（ECDSA）的密码学底层，哪怕这个谣言成真，也不会直接威胁到链上私钥的安全。

至于中本聪那些已经暴露的公钥...确实已经成了未来所有算力最现成的超级赏金池。

这股抛压威慑力会一直在，且看社区如何应对吧。
author: TechFlowPost
quoted_text:
it went viral on X: ex-OpenAI researcher Scott Aaronson hinted that AI labs may have found a way to break RSA encryption.

Now he has crossed out the blog comment that started it.

"A rumor is a rumor is a rumor," he wrote.

He still says "I didn't say anything false." 
He still says he heard those rumors, and he's still "virtually certain" the labs hold some cryptography results.

On Nov-24 he had told a reader he'd heard "many, many rumors" that OpenAI or Anthropic had a fast way to factor huge numbers, the math problem RSA relies on being hard.

RSA secures web certificates and signatures because ordinary computers can't split a large number into its 2 prime factors in reasonable time.

A practical polynomial-time method would void that protection without quantum hardware, though Bitcoin and Ethereum use ECDSA instead.

A lot of people posting these charts don’t even understand how equity and credit markets interact.

Quant hedge funds use CDS for hedging, pair trading and cross-asset strategies. When stocks sell off and volatility increases, demand for credit protection can increase, pushing CDS spreads higher.

And then you create a vicious cycle:

• Stocks go down.
• Funds buy credit protection.
• CDS spreads widen.
• Accounts like ZeroHedge post scary CDS charts.
• Retail investors panic and sell.
• Demand for credit protection increases again.

And somehow people are treating this feedback loop as independent confirmation that the entire AI industry is collapsing. 😂

Now look at the actual numbers:

• Microsoft: 51 bps.
• Google: 87 bps.
• Amazon: 98 bps.
• Meta: 123 bps.
• Nvidia: 145 bps.

Screaming “ALL-TIME HIGHS” without contextualizing the absolute spreads is ridiculous.

Oracle and especially CoreWeave deserve more attention, but let’s look at what these companies are actually doing.

CoreWeave:

• $9B in customer prepayments and deposits expected within three months alone.
• Approximately 80% of eligible project financing can typically be covered through contract-backed debt, with the remainder supported by customer prepayments and internal cash.
• Morgan Stanley and MUFG are preparing a $4.5B Meta-backed loan expected to receive investment-grade ratings, with an indicative yield of 7–7.5%.
• Management expects to raise less than $5B in additional capital through 2027.

Even Goldman Sachs acknowledged that CoreWeave’s CDS is being used as a proxy to hedge broader AI infrastructure exposure.

And Oracle? Oracle literally announced on November 20 that it had secured all the funding necessary to fulfill its OpenAI contract, following its final capital raise for this investment cycle.

But apparently, we’re just going to ignore all of this and keep posting scary CDS charts?

CDS spreads reflect default risk, hedging demand, liquidity, market positioning and risk premiums. They are not a pure measure of bankruptcy probability.

I’m not saying credit risk doesn’t exist. I’m saying that blindly posting CDS charts without understanding the underlying financing structures or trading dynamics is not financial analysis.

It’s fearmongering.

text:
Taking over someone else's unfinished work in 2022:

Open GitHub, there's a PR there.
+673 -241 diff.

Checkout the branch, run tests.
They pass.

Spend 2 hours reading the code to understand it.

There's a weird if statement that you don't understand why it's there.
You ask the coworker who opened the PR.

He says it's because some obscure payload field can be null and now it all makes sense, you understand all the code.

Read the ticket again to see what's missing and write rest of code.

+871 -308 final diff.
Merge PR.

✅ Done.

Taking over someone else's work in 2026:

Open GitHub. There's a PR there.
+87341 -32651 diff.

Tell Claude to read the ticket and see what's left.
Claude comes up with 5 bullet points of what's left to do. You understand none of them.

There are 15 markdown files in the PR your coworker's agent dumped for future context.
You open them. 3000 lines each. You understand none of it.

Ask Claude to explain it like you're 5.
Claude outputs words that are coherent but you still understand none of it.

You tell Claude to make diagrams to explain the architecture.
A tiny bit of it starts making sense.

There's some weird service "Transactional Reconciliation Service" you don't understand why it's there. Claude says it shouldn't be there and the markdown files don't specify why it's there.

You ask the coworker about that service.
He has no idea what you're talking about, he needs to ask his agent.

His Claude makes an artifact that explains why that service is slop that was written by the subagent who implemented it and shouldn't be there at all.

The coworker hands that artifact to you. He hasn't read it.

You hand the artifact to your Claude. Your Claude advices to remove the service and proposes 4 different solutions to replace it.

You understand none of the solutions but there is one which seems to make more sense. You ask the coworker if that's a good call.

He has no idea what any of that means, he asks his agent. His agent says it's a good solution but it's missing an important edge case. He copy pastes the agent output in Slack.

You copy paste the Slack message into your Claude. Your Claude says that you're absolutely right, that this is an important edge case that was not handled in the initial solution. Claude proposes a small fix to cover it and asks if it should implement it along with the other 5 bullet points.

You say ok, Claude starts writing code. PR diff grows to +97564 -41698.

You ask Claude if everything in the ticket is implemented. Claude starts reviewing the code.

Claude says that most of it is implemented, but comes up with 5 bullet points of things that are missing.

You are confused, it already came up with 5 bullet points the first time you asked. These seem different bullet points that only came up after reviewing the code though, so you say ok, implement it.

Claude writes code.
PR +102467 -45790 diff.

You ask if now it's all done.
Claude reviews the code. Says it's mostly done but there 3 low priority items that are not yet implemented.

You don't understand any of the items but since they're low priority you figure out they don't matter much, so you click merge.

PR spends 3 hours in the merge queue for CI to go green, then it merges.

Next Monday your coworker asks his agent to deploy to AWS.
Your agent's code now runs in production.

2 hours later the whole backend is down. No one knows why.

Your coworker asks his agent to investigate. After 20 minutes it finds the code that threw an unhandled error when some payload came up with an obscure null field.

Your coworker doesn't recognize any of that code and his agent says it should not be there but you wrote it so your coworker should check with you first.

He asks you about that code.

You've never seen that code in your entire life.
You ask your agent about it.

Your Claude says the error was thrown because the code never expected that obscure field to be null.

The code was in "Transactional Reconciliation Service".

text:
THE BANKS WILL BE HACKED LONG BEFORE BITCOIN IS.

They keep telling you Bitcoin is the risky one. So look at who actually got hacked this week.

The US Treasury. FinCEN, the office that collects every report your bank files about you, admitted hackers got into its systems. Systems are offline. They still won't say who got in or what they saw.

The CIA. Hackers got into one of its unclassified networks too.

And the week before, one software bug at Chase held up payments for people at other banks across the country. One bank broke and everyone felt it.

None of this is new.

In 2016 hackers used the banks' own payment network to take $101 million from Bangladesh's central bank account at the New York Fed. They tried for $850 million more.

The Fed found more than 50 breaches of its own computers in five years.

The regulator that watches America's banks had hackers reading its emails for over a year. Microsoft had to tell them.

Now compare what protects each one.

Your bank: a password. A code by text. A call centre that can reset both. Thousands of staff and outside companies with access. And one big database holding everyone's money and details. Get in once and you get it all.

Bitcoin: no head office to break into. No password to reset. No staff to trick. It runs on tens of thousands of computers around the world, and every one of them checks every transaction. There's no middle to attack.

To take your coins, someone has to guess your private key. There are almost as many possible keys as there are atoms in the universe.

Bitcoin hasn't gone down once since 2013. Your bank's app went down this month.

Here's what they don't tell you. The maths that protects Bitcoin is the same kind of maths that protects your bank's website and the chip in your card. If anyone ever breaks it, they won't start with Bitcoin. They'll go for the banks. That's where the money is, and the doors are already open.

Every "Bitcoin hacked" headline you've ever read was an exchange, or someone who lost their keys. Never Bitcoin itself. Leave your coins on an exchange and you've chosen bank security again.

I've held Bitcoin since 2012. In that time I've watched banks get hacked over and over. Bitcoin just kept running.

They call Bitcoin the risky one while the Treasury can't keep hackers out of its own systems.

So who do you really trust with your savings?

text:
There are rumors that one of the frontier labs cracked 2048-bit RSA, the powerful asymmetric encryption algorithm that secures bank accounts, wallets, password vaults, and pretty much all of modern life.

Some believe the rumors are false because the labs haven't published anything. Of course they haven't, because such a thing would be kept secret.

When a US lab (or anyone else in the US) makes a discovery which would be classified as impacting national security, they are subject to the Invention Secrecy Act and Espionage Act. Germany has its own version of it, called the Geheimpatent ("Secret Patent") with extremely strict prohibitions around "Treason and Endangering External Security". Many other countries have similar laws.

In other words, if someone comes up with a technology that is a threat to national security, and they don't cooperate with the government before publishing anything, they're risking lifelong time in jail.

Given that RSI has been achieved, it seems very plausible that AI has in fact cracked RSA, because RSA rests on inefficiency, exploiting decades old computational asymmetry. It's super easy to multiply two large numbers, but good luck trying to factor their product back into those primes!! RSA relies on this being practically impossible, for the lack of an algorithm that would be capable of reversing this operation in a reasonable amount of time.

Now we saw AI solved the Riemann hypothesis, which was claiming for something like 165+ years or so that there is a pattern behind the distribution of prime numbers, while it seemed they were random. AI also solved a mountain of other such conjectures, and it seems it's going to get us to warp drives quite soon. Great.

But what this also shows is that it is not that far fetched to assume those rumors are, in fact, true.

Reason to panic? Yes.

No reason to panic? Also yes.

Why? Because if AI really cracked RSA, it means it's going to be quite easy for it to come up with a new kind of cryptography that is so ridiculously insane that it's actually unbreakable. And because the fall of RSA would cause western civilization to collapse, we'd see patches getting rolled out quite rapidly. Therefore I'm not worried at all. In fact, I'm excited, because if AI really got that powerful, I can sleep peacefully knowing that in a few years from now we'll get technologies we can't even imagine today. And we urgently need them.

text:
A very simplified explanation: P vs. NP -- What does it practically mean?

I did a lot of research on this topic -- theoretical computer science -- and want to ELI5 what its about.

Let's look at a classic problem related to optimization and efficiency:
You have a bunch of boxes of different sizes.
You need to pack as many of them into a container.
There are many different ways of doing it, can you find the most efficient one?

Here's another example:
A sales person needs to visit 50 cities and wants to pay the minimal airfare for this long trip. There are many different ways to do this, each one has a different total airfare cost.
Can you find the cheapest one?

I hope you already see how natural and convenient such problems are. This type of problems arise in chip design, in manufacturing, in chemistry and economics, all over the place. They all have the same flavor: You have a set of options and set of constraints, and you want to choose the setting that satisfies all constraints and has minimal cost (or, sometimes, maximal benefit).

There is a simple method to solve each such problem:
You try every single possibility and remember only the one with the lowest cost. This works but it's inefficient 🙂

For the traveling salesperson with just 50 cities there are 50! (50 factorial) different options. That's a huge number.
If you have your laptop just counting from 1 to 50 factorial, it'll take it longer than the age of the universe to do it!

The question we computer scientists obsess with is this:
Is there an efficient algorithm that solves such problems, *and* takes time that is closer to 50 than to 50 factorial?
*This is exactly the meaning of the P vs NP problem.*

If P = NP, it means there *is* an efficient solution to such problems.
And if P doesn't equal NP, there is no efficient solution.

Here's what you need to know about P vs. NP:
There are thousands of problems that lie in this family of problems. I mentioned two of them. The amazing thing is that if there's an efficient solution to any one of these problems, it immediately means there's an efficient solution to *each and every* of these problems.

This would mean that if you can pack things efficiently in a container, then you can solve the optimal route for the traveling salesperson, and you can solve every Soduko puzzle, and you can find proofs of any mathematical theorem quickly, and you can do thousands of other tasks very efficiently.

Which is why most of the experts don't think that P = NP.
But so far we, humans, haven't been able to prove this.
How long till AI does it for us?

text:
I see a lot of people arguing that $ETH will continue to underperform for years. What I find interesting is how much of that conviction is based on historical price action rather than the economic infrastructure being built today.

Take STRATO as an example.

Some people interpret us building our own chain as moving away from Ethereum. In reality, our technology has been in development for over a decade, and our architecture allows us to specifically address a multi-trillion-dollar hard asset economy.

If we succeed in bringing even a few percent of that capital onchain over the coming years, think about what that could mean for ETH.

Through STRATO, ETH can be used as collateral, deployed into liquidity pools, held as a reserve asset, generate yield and unlock liquidity through USDST. A significant portion of our own network token will also reside on Ethereum, benefiting from its security, which is economically backed by ETH itself.

One of the biggest opportunities for ETH is not simply attracting more of the capital already circulating within crypto. It’s expanding the total amount of capital available onchain and creating economic reasons for that capital to flow into ETH.

Now apply that same principle across thousands of projects, financial institutions and global organizations building their own economies.

That is where I believe people fundamentally underestimate Ethereum’s long-term economic potential.

Sentiment, narratives and speculation can dominate price action for extended periods. But what ultimately matters is how much economic value an asset can capture as the infrastructure around it matures.

I’m bullish on $ETH not because of where the chart has been, but because of where the economy around it is heading.

Believe in somETHing…

text:
为什么我认为美联储加息将进一步导致AI产业的风险？
昨天我讲了AI技术发展过快可能导致就业市场恶化和消费下降的宏观经济风险，今天想进一步讲讲美联储的货币政策。
我认为，相比美联储是否会加息，更值得关注的是市场是否充分定价了持续加息所带来的连锁影响。
美联储的长期通胀目标为2%，而目前AI产业大规模的资本开支，正在增加市场对电力，芯片以及基础设施的需求，可能进一步加剧通胀压力。
我认为，依靠资本开支推动的经济增长才是真正值得警惕的，因为这些资本投入能否在未来产生足够的回报，仍未得到充分验证。
与此同时，越来越多的科技企业通过发行债券为AI基础设施建设融资。一旦美联储持续加息，企业融资的成本将进一步上升，对资本回报率的要求也会越来越高。
如果AI带来的收入增长无法覆盖资本成本，企业就可能被迫削减资本开支，进而影响英伟达等AI基础设施企业的订单及盈利预期。
更值得警惕的是，一边是AI资本开支可能造成的通胀压力，另一边却是AI替代就业可能造成的消费下降。
如果这两种情况同时发生，美联储可能面临经济增长放缓，通胀却高于目标的困境，甚至无法通过降息及时刺激经济。
因此，我依然维持昨天的预测：至少在2027年Q1财报公布之前，美股大概率仍将处于熊市。
我认为，目前市场最大的风险在于，AI产业的高估值建立在未来高增长，高资本回报率的预期之上，而持续加息可能同时打击企业的实际盈利能力与估值。
市场可以提前定价加息，却未必充分定价加息所带来的经济后果。

text:
Why do new roads, universities, and industrial parks so often fail to transform an economy?
Often, the problem isn’t that the right pieces are missing; it’s that they don’t fit together.
In The Missing Pieces of Development: What Asia Reveals About Coherence, Capabilities, and Africa’s Economic Transformation, Jean-Claude Maswana offers a clear, eye-opening look at why well-intentioned development efforts frequently fall short; and what it actually takes to build lasting prosperity.
Drawing on the real-world experiences of Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Singapore, Malaysia, China, and Vietnam, the book shows that Asia’s economic rise did not come from a single magic formula. Economies took off when roads, skills, local businesses, finance, and government policies began reinforcing one another instead of operating in isolation:
Roads without maintenance quickly deteriorate.
Degrees without real jobs produce diplomas rather than practical capabilities.
Foreign factories without local learning leave domestic companies on the sidelines.
New technologies, including AI, cannot lift an economy that lacks the everyday skills and infrastructure needed to put them to work.
Rather than asking the usual question “What is Africa missing?”, this book invites readers to ask a far more practical one: “How can African economies make the pieces they already have, and the ones they are building, work together?”
Written for everyday readers, students, entrepreneurs, and policymakers alike, it is an accessible guide to rethinking growth, industrialization, and a shared future between Africa and Asia.

quoted_text:
赚钱核心：散户如何快速的判断行情

加密市场的行情都是有逻辑可以寻的，虽无法做到精确制导，但大体方向，区间是可以完全判定的

条件论逻辑是我觉得最适合大家的！

所有的上涨和下跌的行情，都是条件汇聚形成的结果，大条件累积成大行情，阶段性条件累积成阶段性行情。

牛市OR熊市

判断结合核心：
宏观条件+叙事条件+情绪条件+技术条件+链上条件+名人条件

以上六大条件是判断大行情的逻辑核心，条件汇聚的越多，确定性越强，反之如此

一、宏观条件 ：

资金流动性面（加息、降息、ETF等）政策面（对项目方、对交易所、对资金政策等）、美债、美元指数、美股指标

二、叙事条件：

1、外部叙事：AI、元宇宙、物联网、WEB3、RWA等
2、行业叙事：如以太坊叙（技术和生态）、比特币叙事（减半事件、铭文概念推动等），能促进行业发展的核心路径（技术+用户）。

三、情绪条件：

市场散户情绪：通过恐慌和贪婪指数，各个社群情绪、KOL情绪、热点币情绪（交易所疯狂上热点币OR很久不会上新）

外部媒体和散户情绪：外部媒体如果频繁报道比特币和币圈的财富效应一般都是阶段性，或者牛市顶部阶段。

四、技术条件

1、小周期、大周期K线趋势、结合几个核心的指标（MACD、BOLL等）

五、链上条件

1、比特币的中期、长期筹码链上状态，如中长期持有者是否持续增加或者减少等等一些核心的链上指标

2、熊市中进入的中大鲸鱼持有者，如果到牛市中批量减持，散户地址批量增长，也是阶段性或者牛顶的信号之一

六、名人条件

1、名人言论：海内外行业OG，比如木头姐、李启威李启元兄弟、CZ、区块链大机构核心分析师、

2、名人指标：九神、江卓尔60日、彩虹图、山寨指数、还有一些外国朋友的指标等等

*熊市底部参考重要条件一：比特币矿机关机价
主流矿机陆续出现矿机关机，币价接近主流矿机关机价，目前关机价18000到20000U

*熊市底部参考重要条件二：交易所状态
交易所的利空消息（政策、黑客、技术等）

总结如下：

结合六大条件：

1、利好的条件，或预期条件积累的越来越对，那么大牛市就越来越确定，
2、利好的条件越来越少，预期条件逐渐兑现，一般就是在牛市末期阶段。
3、利空的条件逐渐增加，预期利空条件出现，一般就是进入熊市周期。
阶段性的行情也是如此，需要结合近期的利好或者利空条件，再去综合判断。

举例子：说说这轮牛市行情，目前的市场状态

技术条件：月线已经自2023年1月到现在呈上升趋势，并且最近5个月连续阳线

宏观条件：ETF利好条件逐渐落地中，最晚3月
叙事条件：坎昆升级2月左右结束，比特币4月减半
情绪条件：场内一直是呈贪婪指标高区间，并且持续了一段时间，场外情绪热的不明显
链上条件：数据没有太大变化，
名人条件：有些区块链机构OG判断回调

总结：短期阶段性利好都在逐一落地，4月减半是最后一个，猴哥个人觉得4月之前，3月左右，2月中下旬，市场可能就会有一波回调，但既然是牛市周期，我们就要保持长线思维，只买不卖的思路，耐心等最后的补仓机会出现，记住真正的行情来了，都不是一两天就结束的，无论是回调还是上涨，保持耐心最重要。

quoted_text:
The most insightful analogy I've read on the Jensen Huang story comes from a WeChat post that recently spread like wildfire in Chinese tech circles - before being deleted.

They called the whole saga 清君侧 (qīng jūn cè): "clearing the ruler’s side."

It means absolutely nothing to anyone outside China, but any fluent Chinese speaker with knowledge of Chinese history knows immediately what this refers to.

It has always been, throughout Chinese history and ever since the Han dynasty, the primary pretext for rebellion. 

You are not rising against the emperor - of course not, you would never do that! You are merely ridding him of the "evil" advisors around him who have led him astray.

The most famous early use of this expression in Chinese history is during the so-called Rebellion of the Seven States in 154 BCE, when 7 regional kings rose against the Han emperor under the slogan "execute Chao Cuo, clear the ruler’s side" (诛晁错，清君侧 - zhū Cháo Cuò, qīng jūn cè).

Chao Cuo was the emperor's top adviser and the architect of a policy to rein in these powerful regional leaders. Openly rebelling against the emperor would have made these leaders traitors, so they claimed to be targeting only his "evil" adviser. 

The emperor - to his discredit - gave in and had Chao Cuo executed, hoping it would end the revolt. It predictably didn’t work: freed from their main opposition inside the imperial palace, the rebels pressed their advantage and marched on the capital, and were only ultimately crushed at the cost of a full-blown civil war.

Rings a bell?

If you followed the Jensen Huang story, it's eerily similar to what happened. With American characteristics, of course.

In the role of Chao Cuo: Jensen Huang, who had successfully advised Trump - this story's "emperor" - to change policy with regards to AI and allow Nvidia to sell more powerful chips to China, as well as to keep open the loophole that enabled Chinese companies to rent Nvidia's advanced chips in data centers across Southeast Asia.

In the role of our rebellious regional kings, the China hawks around Trump, who of course would never dream of going against the president - they were merely protecting him from someone at his side supposedly compromised by a "Chinese spy".

Our "regional kings" are a broad coalition: hawks inside the administration like Marco Rubio (who wrote the memo that conveniently leaked - https://t.co/4YahEGer9Q - and that we now know contained false accusations - https://t.co/btiJiiFgW7), Democrats like Elizabeth Warren who've been pushing bill after bill to tighten chip exports, media outlets like the New York Times, which printed the accusations without a shred of evidence, and, last but not least, Anthropic, the AI company at the origin of the export controls in the first place.

This is a bit of an aside but, in case you didn't know, as revealed in Kevin Roose’s new book "The AGI Chronicles" (in chapter 20 in case you want to check), the export controls that limit the sales of Nvidia chips to China were first drafted by Dario Amodei himself and his co-founder Jack Clark in Dario's backyard. They then sent it to Ben Buchanan who had been brought into the Biden administration to advise on tech-related issues: he loved it and the rest is history. Ben Buchanan, incidentally, became an adviser to Anthropic once he left government - nothing to see here...

Back to our "clear the ruler’s side" analogy.

Trump, for all the mockery he gets, showed a better grasp of statecraft here than a Han emperor: he refused to sacrifice his Chao Cuo.

By his own account, he personally convinced Nvidia's board to bring Huang back, 12 days after his ouster. Whatever one thinks of him, he understood what the Han emperor hadn't: the hawks are ultimately after power, and every "adviser" you let them take only makes them stronger.

In this instance, it's all somewhat moot though: the hawks may not have succeeded in taking Huang down but in a curious inversion of the Chao Cuo story, they won on policy instead. 

The rebels of 154 BCE got their minister's head, only to see the emperor rein in the regional kings anyway. The hawks of 2026 failed to get Huang's head, but got almost everything he had fought against: the remote-access loophole is closed, data centers across Southeast Asia now need licenses, and Nvidia itself, while Huang was out, announced it would no longer ship its licensed H200s to China (https://t.co/j8HfReVBQZ) and its latest outlook assumes no data center revenue from China at all (https://t.co/NpAW1r23XS). 

In other words, ironically, while the pretext for the rebellion failed - they failed to "clear the ruler's side" - the rebellion itself seems to have succeeded, so far at least.

Maybe Trump isn't smarter than our Han emperor after all...

This is the topic of my latest article: a painstakingly well-sourced and detailed look at who really tried to push Jensen Huang out, and how a spy accusation nobody has ever substantiated managed to shift US policy on AI.

As I write in the article's conclusion, it's a story in which we all lost. 

We lost, first, on how this was decided. The fate of what had been the world's most valuable company, and of America's policy on the most consequential technology of our age, was shifted by a classified memo written in the shadows, built on an unfounded accusation, illegally leaked, and reported with complete disregard for any journalistic standard.

Due process, shareholder rights, the laws protecting classified information, the presumption of innocence, the basic duty of a newspaper to check what it prints: every formal rule that was supposed to stand in the way simply didn't.

If the thought of the technology that will shape humanity's future being decided like this doesn't send chills down your spine, you... need to read my article, I guess.

And that's before we even get to what was decided, which should worry you even more.

To read the full story, here's the link to my article: https://t.co/akmQ2lZqcX

text:
I will not be buying Anthropic stock. Anthropic is very bad and I wish they did not exist. Here's why.
It is increasingly clear that AI R&D will soon be fully automated (if we do not stop soon). AI companies are not secure against theft of model recipes or weights, so progress they make quickly leaks to our adversaries and proliferates into the world. 
If that happens, it becomes WAY harder to stop the race to superintelligence. Here's one pathway for why: 
In the next two years, I expect there will be rogue/autonomous AIs running their own AI development projects using compute that they hack around the world, including consumer devices. We would not be able to shut such AIs down; we do not have the institutional capacity or technology to do so. There will be rogue swarms of AIs and we won't be able to stop it. Those swarms won't abide by U.S. law or any other law. They might directly harm Americans, American infrastructure, or the economy, and they will certainly cause indirect harm (e.g., humans preemptively shutting off vulnerable services to avoid getting hacked by a rogue swarm). Such AIs might steal money out of your bank account, shut off critical infrastructure as a form of extortion, and otherwise make life bad for us humans. Eventually, if AI gets too smart, I expect it will literally kill all humans in the process of accomplishing its inhuman goals. 
That's just one story. There are plenty of other plausible stories, e.g., rogue states or terrorists using these AIs for rapid autonomous AI development and bioweapons. 
That is the world that Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google are pulling us toward. It is a clear extrapolation from the last few months and years of AI progress and from the stated plans of these companies. 
People have compared rogue AI to a demon. Anthropic is summoning demons. OpenAI is summoning demons. That is not an acceptable thing to do, and I do not consent to you burning humanity's commons like this. Every day you make it harder and harder to have a global ban on superintelligence. Every day you bring us closer to human extinction, to the death of my family and friends. 
These companies are not cool; they are the single biggest threat to American national security in the next two years.

How margin works on @bulktrade, on a real account

Most perp venues margin each position on its own. The requirement is the sum of every leg

BULK margins the account as a whole. Here is a live book from a trader up $280K on BULK:

13 positions, $1.26M across crypto and stocks
 > Short $ZEC $474K
 > Short $BTC $259K
 > Short $HYPE $197K
 > Long $SOL $89K
 > + 9 more, incl. $MU and SK Hynix

Margined leg by leg: $101246
What BULK actually charges: $65220

36% less margin for the same book. $36026 freed

- Why the requirement drops?

BULK risk engine looks at the full book, not each position separately:

> Correlation. Each position s margin is combined using a live correlation matrix between markets, instead of being added up. Opposite positions in related markets offset each other
> Volatility regime. Margin rates rise when BULK regime model sees a more volatile market, and ease when it calms
> Net risk. Rates also reflect how much closing a position would move the book, so bigger, harder to exit positions need more

 - Why it matters?

This $1.2M book needs margin worth 11% of the account. The rest is buffer before liquidation, or room to trade more on the same deposit

While retail celebrates Bitcoin bouncing above 60,500 with US bond desks closed for Thanksgiving, I’m watching an entirely different equation unfold underneath the surface. Thin order books can manufacture impressive green candles without any meaningful improvement in institutional funding conditions. Never confuse price recovery with liquidity recovery.

Now connect what is happening thousands of miles away in the Strait of Hormuz to the selling pressure on your Bitcoin chart. With Gulf tensions reportedly pushing Brent crude towards $96, energy importing nations need more dollars to purchase the exact same quantity of oil. Corporations need more working capital, inflationary pressure intensifies, and the Fed reserve finds itself with even less room to ease monetary conditions.

Essentially, you have rising demand for dollars precisely when the cost of accessing those dollars is already elevated.

Now introduce something almost nobody in crypto discusses.. the institutional collateral hierarchy.

When balance sheets come under pressure, institutions don’t necessarily liquidate assets based on their monetary superiority. They liquidate according to accessibility, collateral requirements and funding obligations. Bitcoin’s greatest technological advantage, its ability to trade 24/7, can ironically become a vulnerability during periods of institutional deleveraging.

The reported 5.39 bn. dollars in US spot Bitcoin ETF outflows this month becomes particularly interesting within this context.

Meanwhile, sovereign buyers accumulating physical gold operate under an entirely different monetary mandate. They aren’t necessarily managing leveraged positions or chasing quarterly returns. They’re reducing their exposure to another nation’s financial liabilities.

Both physical gold and Bitcoin held in self custody carry no issuer default risk. So the fundamental difference isn’t necessarily the asset itself.. it’s WHO owns it, HOW they finance it and WHY they hold it.

This is precisely why I’m interested in tomorrow’s Fed reserve H.4.1 release. Forget the headline balance sheet number. Watch the movement of bank reserves, TGA, repo usage and the composition of the Fed’s assets. That’s where I would look for early evidence of a potential shift in the liquidity regime.

Gold may be absorbing geopolitical uncertainty while Bitcoin absorbs the consequences of institutional deleveraging. Two scarce monetary assets sitting inside two very different financial architectures.

And perhaps the greatest irony here is that Bitcoin, an asset designed to exist independently of the fiat monetary system, still has its marginal price heavily influenced by the availability of fiat liquidity.

That contradiction is what fascinates me.

P.S. If you’re following me for tomorrow’s Bitcoin price, you’re looking in the wrong place. I’m decoding the monetary machinery that determines why capital moves in the first place.

quoted_text:
No, I do not believe that we should “surrender human free will” to AI systems, and it’s absurd to suggest that I do. I have written hundreds of pages of essays and a constant theme in them is the need for AI to be governed by legitimate democratic processes. For millennia (going all the way back to Greek and Roman philosophers), advocates of autocracy have claimed that it leads to better, faster, or more decisive decision-making than the messy process of democracy. Even if this were true (which I doubt!), we should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security. This argument against autocracy applies word for word against governance by AI, and I feel equally strongly that turning over governance to AI is a bad idea.

No one who had carefully read my writing or my interviews could reasonably conclude that I believe anything different. For example in an interview on CBS a couple months ago, I specifically called for AI to be governed democratically. I call for the same in Policy on the AI Exponential, Machines of Loving Grace, and The Adolescence of Technology, and We Must Pace the Frontier. Machines of Loving Grace contains an extended section on using AI to revitalize democracy, and discusses the use of AI as an aid to citizens in their decision-making, "aggregat[ing] opinions and driv[ing] consensus among citizens, resolving conflict, finding common ground, and seeking compromise.” The clear and obvious implication is that humans should remain the ones making political and governance decisions. The Adolescence of Technology has an entire section on fighting against AI-driven tyranny, and I even discuss the danger of AI labs usurping power and come out strongly against it — by implication, this definitely includes an AI lab usurping power and giving it to AI itself!

If I thought any of this was a good idea, I would be advocating for it in public, just as I have not been afraid to advocate for many, many unpopular views over the last few years. But I am not advocating for it, because I think turning over governance to AI is a terrible idea.

Separately, I think there is frequent conflation (including in this article) between the idea of “surrendering human free will” to AI in some grand sense of global governance, and the more prosaic idea that as AI systems advance, they become capable of doing specific tasks in a more automated way. This is not AI “running the world,” but AI driving a car, designing a cancer drug, or writing software end-to-end. Here, my view is mixed. AI doing more complete or larger tasks is economically valuable and can drive important advances in software, medicine, transportation, energy, etc. It is clearly desirable in many cases and will save a lot of lives. But it has downsides as well, and in some areas it may not be worth it.

For example, using AI too autonomously to build the next generation of AI systems (known as recursive self-improvement, or RSI) may cause AI to improve faster than we can control or adjust to it, so we may want limits on this process. As we said publicly in early November, we don’t expect it to be safe for Claude to build successive frontier models fully autonomously, without meaningful human supervision or understanding. Second, in some contexts, using AI in too end-to-end a manner may be a cause of serious job disruption, and it may make sense to slow or even stop some AI deployments to give people more time to adapt. Third, while the use of AI for alignment research is an incredibly valuable tool, it must be done with caution, because we may not be able to trust the work of the AI system. Finally, in many cases, humans would simply prefer to do some activities themselves, so they can stay deeply engaged in what matters to them, even if AI can do those activities better. There are countless other examples and hard cases. I don’t think there are any easy answers here, nor is there (nor should there be) any single decision-maker: some of these decisions will be made by society, some by government, some by AI companies, and some in a decentralized manner by individuals expressing their own preferences as consumers, which may differ from the preferences of others.

I don't think that other AI leaders or AI companies have significantly different views from me on whether specific tasks should be automated. Certainly the products that they offer don’t differ materially in their orientation towards automation of tasks; every company seems to be releasing models more and more capable of task automation (as that’s been the general consequence of scaling up AI training), and every company claims to understand there are risks and downsides of such automation and to offer safeguards. If anything, Anthropic has been the most vocal and the most proactive about acknowledging these downsides and trying to address them. For instance, it’s fairly absurd to cite my statement that fully autonomous weapons might “one day be needed for the defense of democracy” as differing from that of other AI companies, when I was willing to risk Anthropic’s future as a company to refuse to allow our existing AI models to be used for autonomous weapons even in the face of legal sanctions, and no other AI company did the same.

To summarize, as applied to grand questions of how we govern increasingly capable AI, I have been vocal and consistent that AI needs to be governed by a legitimate, democratic process and that “surrendering human free will” to AI systems is a terrible idea. As applied to automation of specific tasks by or for people, my views are more mixed, but I don’t think they differ from those of other AI companies — most other companies seem to be offering similar products and confronting similar tradeoffs without having perfect answers to them. What is happening is that there’s a sort of vibes-based commercial and political positioning that some AI CEOs are engaging in, where they repeat slogans like “human control and agency,” or “AI should be just a tool,” without actually doing anything different in their products or taking seriously the difficult questions that lie behind these slogans.

quoted_text:
The Agentic Scientist: Paper talk now on YouTube!

In this talk, we argue that The Agentic Scientist creates a framework by which off-the-shelf coding agents can be used as research collaborators.

Solely relying on off-the-shelf coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex, these agents tend to behave like strong hyperparameter optimizers when given a research question. While the scores improve, the ideas remain narrow and the reasons for gains are rarely examined.

The Agentic Scientist makes the research loop explicit by using a meta-controller to run parallel instances of agents over a sequence of tasks including task drafting, ideation, planning, sandboxed experiments with baselines and ablations, analysis, and writing. All steps are evaluated against rubrics defined upfront and prior to any experiments.

We showcase the results for an early version of The Agentic Scientist, which helped us study Error Diffusion, a biologically inspired alternative to backpropagation. The work was accepted as an oral at ALIFE 2026. In autonomous runs, the system raised Doc-to-LoRA multi-needle retrieval accuracy from 52% to 98% and designed a learned evolution strategy that improved over its CMA-ES reference on unseen tasks. We ablate the importance of different orchestration layers vs. the strength of base model, finding that reliable autonomy crucially depends on the latter.

Human researchers define the initial question and evidence standards, while agents extend the set of experiments that can be performed.

quoted_text:
As @rutgerbregman & @danwilliamsphil have been arguing - its increasingly clear the people who made crazy sounding predictions about AI are directionally correct. 

But while AI is advancing insanely quickly, politics is only starting to catch up. That's partly because the EA and rationalist communities out of which AI safety grew have been dismissive of mass politics. They counted on elite coordination by enlightened communities to make this go well. They misjudged how power worked. 

Now, with tech bosses warning we are hurtling towards catastrophe, yet doing nothing to stop it, AI safety and mass politics have no choice but to collide. Saturday's @PauseAI_UK demo was a promising start. 

My main take-aways from making this @novaramedia report:
- The people best placed to understand AI's true capability are the most scared of what it can do. This was a protest with the highest proportion of STEM phds I have ever attended. AI is eating up Maths, and the leaders of that field are freaking out. Field medallist Sir Timothy Gowers (@wtgowers) spoke on Saturday. As AI eats up other fields, we can expect other high status professions to freak out. 
- The biggest barrier to people engaging in activism around AI used to be that - to most people - it sounded bonkers. That is no longer the case. On a packed day in central London, I was actively looking for people who thought the 'Pause AI' protestors were mad. Instead, what I found was people who took even the most extreme threats from AI seriously, who had universal contempt for the vision of the future being cooked up in Silicon Valley, and who were relieved to see people taking political action. 
- This was an incredibly orderly march. That has the advantage that it didn't create any negative polarisation among the public. It has the disadvantage that media coverage of AI as a political issue (and potential emergency) remains thin. The AI safety movement will have to decide which of these is more important in the coming weeks and months. 

I am generally an optimist, and I think humanity has time and again shown a phenomenal capacity to solve the problems we both confront and create. The problem with AI is timelines. I am not in a position to judge whether there will be a technical solution to AI risk, but the leaders of the field are clear we should not expect one anytime soon (see: @paulfchristiano's recent @geoffreyhinton lecture). In terms of a political solution, this protest made me mildly more optimistic. But AI is moving at a pace politics (especially mass, democratic politics) struggles to operate on. If anything like RSI is achieved in 2027, we are probably screwed. 

cc. @futurebriefing_ @tombibbys @tegmark @So8res @GarrisonLovely et al

The intrusion was found in the past month during an upgrade after attackers exploited a software vulnerability to reach the control plane, the system’s central management layer that could, in theory, give visibility into aircraft status and logistics flows.

The breach has disrupted operations and paused ongoing migrations of back-office systems.

It potentially exposes sensitive tactical, personnel, and logistics data across one of the military’s largest cloud environments, which also hosts air-defense command-and-control feeds and global munitions tracking.

Cyber Command is assessing the damage.

text:
While I disagree strongly with Donald Trump on a lot of important matters (ICE, Iran, OMG so much else...), I do find I tend to agree w/ his actions on what is almost surely the most consequential issue on our planet now: AI R&D and the path to AGI/ASI....   

I don't know the full story about Jensen Huang, etc., but from the info publicly available, I feel a gov't nudge to bring Jensen back was probably the right thing to do.   The world will be better off with NVidia functioning more effectively.

I don't think GPUs or LLMs are the cosmic path forward to AGI/ASI, but they are obviously proving highly valuable for this interim period, and impairing their progress right now would not be a helpful thing...

Ofc if Jensen had been OK-ing the implantation of Chinese spyware in Nvidia chips the story would be different... but so far as I can tell the "Chinese spy" thing was overblown by media.  Every Chinese exec reports to Chinese intelligence as requested, and everyone knows that; everyone in the industry is an "asset."   US is not quite that way but becoming basically that way -- e.g. we saw (w the Fable saga) Anthropic declined to play nice w US gov't and got spanked and decided to toe the line in ways not being publicly disclosed....  This is almost inevitable as AI moves toward becoming so vastly transformative..

Like TSMC , Nvidia spanning US and China economies is a feature not a bug and helps us move forward together as a global economy and species toward the Singularity rather than getting mired too much in tribalism and nationalism..

Trump's tariffs have been bad for the global economy IMO, but his advocacy for Jensen is among other things a move in favor of globalism which is good...

Spark Savings is the largest cross-chain vault product in DeFi, with deposits peaking at $3 billion earlier this year.

What makes Spark Savings different is a combination of three things:

1. Cross-chain smart contract rails to enforce transparent risk controls.
2. Offchain software that rebalances the vault's positions across approved markets.
3. The Spark Liquidity Layer, which can borrow billions in stablecoins through Sky's allocation system.

Financial platforms we speak with consistently name exit liquidity as a top priority. Spark Savings was designed with withdrawal liquidity as a central requirement.

While a passive lending market relies on interest rates to draw liquidity back, Spark can move the vault's capital out of several markets and swap between stablecoins to meet withdrawals.

Some stats:

Between January and November 2026, the Spark Savings USDT vault on Ethereum had nine days when withdrawals exceeded 25% of deposits. All requests on those days were completed the same day.

On 20 May, the vault processed 741M USDT in withdrawals, equivalent to 60% of its opening assets. The slowest request took four minutes, and the largest single request, for 390M USDT, was filled in one minute.

We think cross-chain vaults are where on-chain savings products are heading, offering the best mix of yield generation and liquidity control.

I am excited to see their adoption into Earn programs to further connect the world with on-chain finance!

#丫丫产品笔记

在别的交易所或券商已经是VIP了，到币安是不是得从头再攒？这个问题我被问过好几次。

11月26日，币安「VIP升舱计划」（VIP Status Match）正式上线。官方的意思其实很直接：你在其他交易所或券商已经拿到的VIP等级，即日起可以转到币安。

我觉得重点不只是「等级能带走」，而是审核通过后，会先按你的情况匹配相应等级，再额外提升一级，前60天先按这个礼遇来。

怎么申请，其实不复杂：

1️⃣ 提交近30天的交易量或资产证明。官方页面上可以填钱包资产、现货/杠杆交易量、合约交易量，任一适用项即可，多项也可以。

2️⃣ VIP团队会在3个工作日内回复你的申请。

3️⃣ 通过后，匹配相应等级，并再升一级，同时会有专属客户经理对接。

举个官方页面上的例子：如果匹配结果是 VIP 2，再升一级后，前60天按 VIP 3 来享受相应礼遇。这是预估示意，最终以审核结果为准。

这60天里，除了等级提升，官方还提到更低费率（自审核通过当日起生效）、专属客户经理，以及受邀出席全球币安VIP聚会等服务。具体能用上哪些，还是看你的等级和官方说明。

有一点想提前提醒大家：这60天是专属礼遇，不是说这一级会一直锁定。礼遇结束后，你的等级会随你在币安的交易表现而定。所以「来币安VIP等级不清零」，指的是你原来的等级可以带过来，不用从零开始。细节以官方公告和条款为准。

新用户和已经在币安的用户都可以申请，不过申请需要审核，也不是所有地区都开放。每个账户的参与规则，也请以官方页面为准。

如果你正好在考虑这件事，可以直接看官方申请页，按自己的情况准备材料就好。

text:
Calm down, Twitter!

I'm writing this from Michael Faraday's old bedroom at 21 Albemarle Street. I'm at a desk pushed up against a window, overlooking the offices of a private equity firm. The workers look just as bored as they did this time last week. Perhaps they haven't heard Riemann was proven, and therefore didn't notice the sky fell in.

An hour ago in the next door room, I walked in on an impromptu talk by @YangHuiHe1. He gave a five minute tear-down of the Riemann proof at @London_Inst.

Yang chose the Rubenstein version (said to be the most legible out there today - Day 6). By now it's one of dozens of retellings of the Alpöge-Claude proof. They're growing in number and shrinking in length every day.

Observations on the Proof:
- Yang showed how this proof orchestrates a dazzling array of techniques (including most of the main breakthroughs in number theory from the past half century), to thread the needle of a particular inequality, with almost no wiggle-room. It very clearly couldn't have been done without summoning whichever instance of Smaug is currently curled up in Dario Amodei's basement
- But neither did Riemann fall to a cab driver thumbing "solve Riemann please" into the prompt window - had that been the case, your fatalism might be justified
- Alpöge is not just any old Princeton PhD. To quote Yang, he's a potentially "Poincaré-grade" figure - Alpöge has repeatedly been touted as a future Fields Medallist. In his mid thirties, he's approaching the height of his powers, and now allowed to pilot state of the art AI. Yang, a storied mathematician in another field, said, "there's no way I nor anyone except a top, top expert could have prompted Claude to produce that result, no way"
- A global race is now on to produce the most succinct, most elegant and most legible proof. Once again, this race is human-led and AI-actuated, just like the proof itself.

On Fatalism:
- I didn't enter a room full of mourners at the London Institute for Mathematical Sciences today (exactly the opposite mood to most of X). They're not weeping for the loss of a former life. Yes, the perimeter of the frontier is flashing out from under their feet. It's destabilising. Their quiet, prayerful lives may be over, and become more like a day on the trading floor.
- But to believe 'all maths gets solved by AI' is crass and a structural impossibility. As Tao said:
"Despite the impression given by press releases and social media, most of the problems at the current frontier of mathematics remain unsolved, even with massive computational expenditure. Indeed, the space of mathematical problems remains infinite; and the difficulty level of such problems is unbounded."
- It echoes what Yang Hui-He told me when I first met him the day of the FrontierMath evals in 2024: “Do you realise how many codimensions we’ve proved for Hodge? One! There are infinitely many to go. I need infinite post docs! I don’t fear being jobless. I fear not knowing in my lifetime."

Uncomputable Outcomes:
- But will AI one day ask all the questions, you ask?
- I think this misunderstands both AI and human at some fundamental level - at least, for now.
- AI reasoning systems are mostly trained against reinforcement learning paradigms that say: keep going, as long as it's very likely profitable profitable. Stop when it's not, or you can't tell.
- By construction, and AI cannot limitlessly decide to expend resources on "uncomputable outcomes" such as the Riemann Hypothesis, whose chances of solution are unknown, and whose economical value is low (unless it's part of a billion dollar marketing budget)
- There's no empirical evidence, to me, that the master commander relationship between an AI model and its human pilot has changed (so far).

The Value of Knowledge:
The chattering gods are telling you "the value of knowledge has gone to zero". Well, the evidence for that is slim.
Mathematicians today are all of us tomorrow.
They're just the first of the species to be pulled first through this infinite accelerator. That this monastic, contemplative group of intellects should have been chosen before the rest of us seems quite unjust and inappropriate.
But they're showing us that AI's massive expansion of possibility doesn't at all imply takeover.
The fact is, the world's greatest maths problem fell to exactly the kind of figure you could have predicted in advance.
Best in class expertise armed Apolgë with the weird incantations required to extract that proof from Claude.
The lesson so far seems to be - keep learning, humans.

author: OfficialSUNio
quoted_text:
𝗨𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗦𝗨𝗡.𝗶𝗼'𝘀 𝗙𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗟𝗶𝗾𝘂𝗶𝗱𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗠𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗹𝘀: 𝗩𝟮, 𝗩𝟯, 𝗩𝟰, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗦𝘂𝗻𝗖𝘂𝗿𝘃𝗲

Liquidity provision is not a one-size-fits-all strategy, and https://t.co/BDR2wKMMx8's four models make that clear.

In DeFi, the liquidity model determines how your capital is deployed, how trading fees are earned, and how actively you need to manage your position.

https://t.co/BDR2wKMMx8 addresses these different needs through four distinct models, each designed for a particular approach to liquidity provision.

Here is what makes each model different, how it works, and who it is best suited for.

1. 𝗦𝘂𝗻𝗦𝘄𝗮𝗽 𝗩𝟮: 𝗙𝘂𝗹𝗹-𝗥𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗲 𝗣𝗮𝘀𝘀𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗟𝗶𝗾𝘂𝗶𝗱𝗶𝘁𝘆

SunSwap V2 uses the traditional constant-product AMM formula, x × y = k, distributing liquidity across the entire price range.

Unlike the earlier V1 model, it also allows any TRC-20 token to pair directly with another without requiring TRX as an intermediary.

Key features:

🔸 Full-range liquidity, from zero to infinity.
🔸 A fixed 0.3% fee on every swap.
🔸 0.25% goes to liquidity providers, while 0.05% is used to buy back and burn SUN.
🔸 Fungible LP tokens represent each provider's share of the pool.
🔸 LP tokens can be redeemed for the underlying assets, while accumulated trading fees contribute to the position's value.

𝗕𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝘀𝘂𝗶𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗳𝗼𝗿: Those who want a straightforward, passive liquidity position without actively managing price ranges.

2. 𝗦𝘂𝗻𝗦𝘄𝗮𝗽 𝗩𝟯: 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗰𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗟𝗶𝗾𝘂𝗶𝗱𝗶𝘁𝘆

V3 introduces concentrated liquidity, allowing providers to allocate capital within specific price ranges instead of spreading it across the entire curve.

This can improve capital efficiency and potentially generate more trading fees from the same amount of capital while the market remains within the selected range.

Key features:

🔸 Providers choose their preferred price ranges.
🔸 Four fee tiers: 0.01%, 0.05%, 0.3%, and 1%.
🔸 Each position is represented by a unique NFT.
🔸 Trading fees must be manually collected.
🔸 If the market moves outside the selected range, the position becomes a single token and stops earning trading fees until it returns to range or is adjusted.

𝗕𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝘀𝘂𝗶𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗳𝗼𝗿: Liquidity providers seeking greater capital efficiency who are comfortable monitoring and adjusting their positions.

3. 𝗦𝘂𝗻𝗦𝘄𝗮𝗽 𝗩𝟰: 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗺𝗺𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗟𝗶𝗾𝘂𝗶𝗱𝗶𝘁𝘆

V4 builds on concentrated liquidity by introducing Hooks, which allow custom smart contracts to execute specific logic during pool operations.

This makes liquidity pools more customizable and opens up possibilities beyond traditional AMM designs.

Key features:

🔸 Hooks enable dynamic fees, custom curves, and on-chain oracle integrations.
🔸 Supports static fee tiers of 0.01%, 0.05%, 0.3%, and 1%.
🔸 Hooks can enable dynamic fees of up to 5%.
🔸 Singleton architecture allows one contract to manage multiple pools, reducing pool creation costs.
🔸 Flash Accounting tracks net balance changes and settles them at the end of a transaction, helping reduce energy costs.
🔸 Restores native TRX support, removing the need to wrap TRX into WTRX for trading.

𝗕𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝘀𝘂𝗶𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗳𝗼𝗿: Advanced liquidity providers and developers interested in custom pool logic, automated strategies, and programmable AMM designs.

4. 𝗦𝘂𝗻𝗖𝘂𝗿𝘃𝗲: 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗦𝘄𝗮𝗽 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘀

SunCurve is designed specifically for stablecoins and pegged assets such as USDT, USDC, USDD, USDJ, and TUSD.

Instead of using the standard constant-product curve, it employs a hybrid StableSwap invariant that provides extremely low slippage around the peg while adjusting its behaviour when prices move further away.

Key features:

🔸 Optimized for stablecoin and pegged-asset swaps.
🔸 Swap fees of 0.01% or 0.04%.
🔸 Fees automatically compound into the liquidity pool.
🔸 Designed to reduce slippage and impermanent-loss exposure for stablecoin liquidity providers.
🔸 Fungible LP tokens represent liquidity positions.

𝗕𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝘀𝘂𝗶𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗳𝗼𝗿: Those interested in stablecoin liquidity, low-slippage trading, and more passive exposure to stablecoin pairs.

𝗖𝗵𝗼𝗼𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗥𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗟𝗶𝗾𝘂𝗶𝗱𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗠𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗹

The four models serve different purposes:

🟡 V2: Passive, full-range liquidity for general token pairs.
⚪ V3: Concentrated liquidity for greater capital efficiency and active management.
🟢 V4: Programmable liquidity for customized pool behaviour and advanced strategies.
🔵 SunCurve: Specialized stablecoin liquidity with low-slippage trading.

None is automatically better than the others. Your choice should depend on the assets involved, your liquidity strategy, and how much time you are willing to spend managing your position.

It is also worth remembering that capital efficiency does not guarantee higher returns. Market movements, trading volume, impermanent loss, and smart contract risks can all affect actual results.

What makes https://t.co/BDR2wKMMx8's approach valuable is the choice it gives liquidity providers. Rather than forcing every participant into one model, it offers different ways to deploy capital according to their needs and strategies.

Explore the liquidity models: https://t.co/FoVNWMiYu0

text:
Google 这次要是还输，真的说不过去了！Gemini Bots 快要来了😎

Gemini 内部代码已经出现多个与 Bots 有关的字段：

BOT_SELECTOR、BOT_BUILDER_YOUR_BOTS、BOT_BUILDER_PREMADE_BY_GOOGLE。

Google 正在开发自己的 Bot 创建系统，用户可能可以创建专属 Bots，也可以直接调用 Google 预制的 Bots。

虽然还没有正式发布，但方向已经非常明确：Gemini 正在从聊天机器人向 AI Agent 平台进化。

最恐怖的是，Google 手里的牌实在太多了：

最强大脑：Neon，负责理解、推理和规划。

AI 员工：Gemini Bots，负责自主执行任务，甚至可能实现多 Bot 协作。

云端基础设施：Google Cloud，负责提供持续运行的算力和执行环境。

应用生态：Gmail、Drive、Calendar、Chrome、Android，直接连接用户的数字生活。

再算一笔账：

ChatGPT Dots：100 美元/月。
Grok Bot：30 美元/月。
Google AI Pro：19.99 美元/月。
如果 Gemini Bots 最终直接纳入 Pro 会员，这价格简直是降维打击！

Google 不需要重新教育用户使用 AI，也不需要从零建立应用生态。十亿级用户已经在使用 Google 的产品，它只需要把 Agent 能力接进去。

Neon 负责思考，Bots 负责执行，Google Cloud 负责 24 小时运行。

你只需要下达一个目标，AI 就能调用邮箱、日历、网盘和各种工具，替你完成一整套工作。

这才是 AI Agent 最终应该长成的样子。

OpenAI 有模型，xAI 有 Grok，但 Google 同时拥有模型、云计算、操作系统、浏览器和办公软件。

如果它再把这些全部打通，竞争对手面对的就不只是一个更强的模型，而是一个完整的 AI 生产力生态。

我已经开始期待 Neon 接上 Gemini Bots 了。

But what now.

text:
Suggestions from someone where gym=life for years.

1. Determine your goal. 

Is it to gain muscle (hypertrophy)? Gain strength (power)? Lose weight? Endurance/Cardiovascular health?

The answer is usually "all of them" but the reality is the way you train (and eat) comes with trade-offs. Set a primary and secondary goal. This will help you with later items.
 
 -------------
2. Choose the # of days per week you're willing to allocate for physical activities.

3 is minimum. You can do 7.

When I was thick in it I did weights for 5 then cardio + active recovery for the other 2.

You do this so that you can properly do [3].

-------------
3. Run a program. 

It gives you structure and reduces the cognitive load while at the gym. 

"Do I gym today?" - Program says yes. You go.
"What exercise should I do?" - Whatever the paper says.

You can be full-on caveman brained and focus on the movements themselves instead of wasting time asking yourself how you feel, or what you did last time at the gym.

If you don't know what a program is you can have an agent create one for you trivially. I've added a prompt in the follow-up comment so that they can build one for you.

Optimally you would track your work and apply progressive overload to it (regardless of what you're training for), but that can come later. Goal right now is to just go with structure.

-------------
4. Track what you eat.

Depending on your activity, you're going to need different foods. 

Cardio needs carbs. 
Weight training needs protein. 
Weight loss needs a calorie deficit. 

Count them and I bet you'd be surprised at where your numbers are vs where they need to be.

--------------
Additionally, you should seek out an activity that you enjoy to supplement whatever you're doing. I truly believe everyone has a physical activity that brings them energy and when you find it the "grind" becomes so much more enjoyable.

I fucking hated "cardio," but what I learned was that I didn't hate the category - I hated running. 

That meant I could look for alternatives like rowing and cycling, and when I ultimately found them I got the same effects without the misery and liklihood that I dropped it entirely. 

That's it. gl bro

【CZ谈预测市场：预测市场是注意力经济，未来空间会很大】

在BNB黑客松上，有观众提问：你关注预测市场了吗？能不能说说你认为预测市场未来的天花板会有多大？

CZ回答：

我认为它未来的空间会很大，只是我不知道会以多快的速度抵达。

我觉得我们现在所有赛道都会持续演化、持续增长：预测市场、永续合约DEX、中心化交易所、稳定币等等。这些赛道都会增长，整个经济体量会变得大很多。

如果你看马斯克的推文，他说SpaceX还有一百万倍的增长空间。如果SpaceX实现这个目标，我们的经济会增长一百万倍，所有事物都会跟着增长。所以我认为这些事情都会发生。

再说预测市场，过去它一直受到压制，因为大家觉得这就是赌博。很多国家，人们会把预测市场和赌博混为一谈。

但现在不一样了，美国正在对一部分预测市场合法化、发放牌照，同时不少项目正在迁移上链。所以我认为这个赛道会迎来大幅增长。对比未来潜力，现在预测市场的规模还很小。

预测市场是强事件驱动的，非常适合做推广。比如选举、世界杯这类大众关注的事件。它相比交易，更偏向注意力经济。

text:
Prediction Markets are only hated by those that never used them.

YouGov conducted a large scale survey on the public perception of prediction markets

when they asked the general public:
- 16% had a positive impression of Kalshi (41.5% negative)
- 17% had a positive impression of Polymarket (46.3% negative)

but when they asked among those that used these platforms:
- 72.6% had a positive opinion of Kalshi (15% negative)
- 46.3% has a positive impression of Polymarket (18% negative)

The contrast are shoking. That's +54 points net impression gap for Polymarket and +82 points for Kalshi !

The differences are mostly driven by large cohorts of negative respondents in the non-user demographic.

You could think it's because the general public is opposed to gambling but not really.

Turns out Sportsbooks have much smaller users vs non-user impression gaps, mostly due to the absence of of non-user detractors:

- DraftKing's gap -> +33 points
- Fanduel's gap -> 30.6 points

I think what is really shows is that the PR/legal campaigns that the sportsbooks lobby is waging against prediction markets is working perfectly on the uninformed public.

It created a large targeted opposition to Prediction Markets on the basis of them being "gambling" while leaving actual gambling platforms unharmed.

Crypto hacks digest, Nov 27

1. Duelbits reportedly saw a suspicious ~$4.3M outflow on Ethereum and BNB Chain (836 ETH, 1.146M USDT, 209 BNB, USDC, SHIB, DAI). The attacker reportedly swapped it into ~1,588 ETH.

4. Binance has lifted its last hack-related withdrawal holds. Per Reuters, citing Chainalysis and Elliptic, over $600M of the stolen funds went through THORChain (possibly counting repeat transfers) and another $342M through CoinJoin. The UK FCA is citing the hack to push DeFi authorization rules.

5. Velocity (Solana perp DEX, formerly Drift) paused on Nov 25 after finding a gap in its insurance fund guardrails that let the fund be drawn on outside its limits. Trading is back and the team says no user funds were lost; signups and deposits are still paused.

6. Address poisoning keeps working: a user lost $51,536 USDT on Ethereum after copying a look-alike address.

text:
Imagine selling luxury fountain pens, reinventing yourself as an anonymous crypto influencer 

and eventually becoming the main suspect in a €185M fraud involving 3,000 investors and a Spanish politician.

That’s the story of Álvaro Romillo, better known in Spain as CryptoSpain.

Álvaro started his first company at just 18 years old, and in 2006 he launched RomilloPens, a luxury fountain pen brand that sold handmade pens for anywhere between €700 and €1,500.

He ran the business alongside his father, Domingo Romillo, until it eventually disappeared around 2015.

But in 2021, Álvaro reappeared on social media under the name “Luis”, wearing a black mask and selling €100 courses teaching people about crypto and how to legally avoid paying taxes.

In 2022, he created CryptoSpain, and in January 2023, he launched his own private investment club called Madeira Invest Club.

The idea was relatively simple.

You paid an annual membership of €2,000, which gave you access to exclusive investment opportunities with guaranteed returns ranging between 20-53%.

Interestingly, just four months after the club launched, Spain’s financial regulator publicly warned that it wasn’t authorized to provide investment services.

Álvaro continued operating for 16 months.

By September 2024, the club had accumulated thousands of investors, but its websites suddenly went offline

According to the Spanish authorities, the operation involved 52 companies, 106 bank accounts and assets in 15 different jurisdictions.

€29M had been transferred to an account in Singapore, another €1.76M in USDT was eventually frozen, and investigators suspect that a 61-meter yacht worth €23M was sold to a Bulgarian company for just €100K to avoid seizure.

After the collapse, Álvaro admitted to having given €100K in cash to Alvise Pérez, whose political party had received 800,000 votes in the 2024 European elections.

(Alvise acknowledged receiving the money but denied illegal campaign financing)

On November 6, 2025, Álvaro was arrested over concerns that he might flee the country.

The UCO, Spain’s Civil Guard investigative unit, estimated the figure could be as high as €260M.

Today, Álvaro remains in pretrial detention, denies committing fraud and faces a potential prison sentence of up to 26 years.

26 OF 27 RENT-STABILIZED NYC BUILDINGS JUST WENT TO AUCTION.

ZERO BIDS.

Nearly 900 apartments in East Harlem, mostly rent-stabilized, hit a foreclosure auction this month.

27 buildings on the block. 26 got not a single bid. Each one went back to the bank for $500.

The only sale was a three-story walk-up. About $826,000.

These buildings carry roughly $250 million in debt and more than 2,300 open housing violations.

Former owner Emerald Equities let them rot. A court-appointed receiver runs them now. Nobody has lined up the money to fix them.

So why won’t anyone buy? Do the math.

In June, Mayor Mamdani’s Rent Guidelines Board voted 7-1 to FREEZE rents on every one- and two-year stabilized lease.

That same board’s own index found the cost of running these buildings jumped 5.3% this year.

Taxes go up. Insurance goes up. Heat, water, labor and repairs go up. The rent doesn’t.

Tenants who won a rent strike last year launched a “buyer beware” campaign to scare off investors.

One tenant leader warned would-be buyers: “We’re going to be on their necks.”

Message received.

The city backed a $110 million offer from its preferred buyer. The lender turned it down. On auction day, the private market didn’t even show up.
The landlords’ trade group summed it up in six words: 

“Nobody wants to own these buildings.”

The tenants are the ones stuck. They were promised a nonprofit savior. Instead they’re left with a bank, a receiver, and 2,300 violations nobody can afford to fix.

Freeze the rent, not the bills, and nobody wants the keys.

Welcome to Mamdani’s NYC.
#NYC #Mamdani

text:
First, it was @Bramble_fi. Now, it's @Chance_.

@Starknet has been going hard on wallet infrastructure, and this one might be the most useful yet.

Imagine writing a long-ass prompt only for your agent to give a different output than what was expected.

The prompt was never the problem, your agent just needed stricter terms to follow your rules. Chance enforces them, and the best part is that you can plug it in right now.
___________

AI agents are getting creative at trading, and paying for things onchain. But they hallucinate A LOT. One wrong decimal, and a "sell" reads as a "buy", or maybe a lookalike wallet address is sent tokens, and your money is gone before you notice.

Enter Chance.

It sits between what you asked for and what your agent actually sends onchain. The team calls it a "verification harness", which simply means a checkpoint every transaction has to pass through.

Here's how it works.

1. Propose
Your agent builds the transaction and writes a note on what it's trying to do - every agent does this. Because it repeated your exact task with the steps it'd take, doesn't mean it should be trusted.

2. Verify
The exact transaction is test-run first, to see what it would really do to your balances. Your trading limits like; max amt per trade, daily cap, allowed tokens, allowed recipients, etc, are checked first. Then a separate AI model, called the "judge", compares the result with your prompt or the rules you fed it with, and gives one of three answers:

✓ ALLOW: it matches, so it goes ahead
✗ BLOCK: it broke a limit or your intent, so nothing moves
? ESCALATE: something can't be confirmed, so it waits for you to approve it

3. Settle
Your funds sit in an escrow wallet on Starknet, a wallet that only releases money when its conditions are met. Your funds leave only on an ALLOW, and every check comes with a signed receipt.

Two details made me respect this design.

First, the AI never gets the final say over your limits or funds. If a trade is above your cap, it is blocked before it gets run by the judge.

Second, it works with privacy. It supports STRK20 - Starknet's private token standard that hides the sender, the receiver and the amount. Every private transfer is still checked against your rules, and you get a receipt proving it was authorized, without revealing the parties involved.

Plugging it in is simple. It connects to the agent you already use through MCP, a standard way to link AI agents to outside tools, with no code on your side.

Agents are already using it. Here are the numbers so far, shared by Starknet on 25 Nov:
→ 150K+ agent transactions verified
→ $275M+ in value checked

It already checks orders on @Polymarket, @Kalshi, @HyperliquidX, @trylimitless, @MyriadMarkets, @predictdotfun & @opinionlabsxyz, and @cbventures listed it in their agentic trading stack on 18th November.

As agentic finace is becoming impossible to ignore, this product makes sure your agent stays in line with your needs, matching exactly what you actually said with your output.

It works only on STRC20 transactions.

text:
去中心化AI网络一直绕不开一个核心痛点：用户的提示词和数据发给了一个素未谋面的算力节点，凭什么信任它不作恶、不偷工减料？

最近看了一下@AntSeed 的机制设计，他们用代币质押加NFT凭证，做了一套挺有意思的博弈闭环，顺便把“免费用 AI”和“锁仓流动性”这两个问题一起解了

1️⃣鼓励用户用真金白银给节点“背书”

在Antseed上，任何人都可以跑节点AI算力。为了筛选出靠谱的服务商，系统给每个节点设了一个0到100的信任评分，而用户质押给该节点的ANTS数量，占了这个评分的最大权重

我个人觉得这就像去淘宝买东西的时候先去看看店铺交了多少的保证金：节点背后的质押量越大，作恶的成本就越高，系统在分配请求时也就更倾向于把单子派给它

2️⃣用户质押即“白嫖”算力，还能吃每周补贴

对普通用户来说，单纯为了帮节点刷信用显然缺乏动力，Antseed 给出的直接激励是免费AI额度：

目前网络里有超过30家服务商推出了质押优惠，用户把ANTS锁给哪家节点，哪家就给用户提供免费的AI调用额度。锁得越多、时间越长，能用的免费额度就越高（注意一下质押的具体相关规则各家都是自己定的）

除此之外，质押者每周还能拿到浮动的ANTS质押激励。等于一边拿着代币生息，一边把日常用大模型的开销给省了

🙋如何把质押变成可交易的lANTS NFT保证流动性

通过把用户的质押份额直接封装成一枚lANTS NFT（相当于一张带锁定期的链上存单）解决这个问题：

一是支持无损转让： 如果用户中途急用钱想退出，不用去硬扛解押销毁的琐事，直接把这枚lANTS NFT挂到社区交易市场卖掉就行。买家接手你的剩余锁定期，整个过程代币零销毁

再就是支持灵活调度：就算不卖，用户也可以把NFT拆分成两份，或者直接把质押关系无损转移到另一家服务商名下，原有的数量和剩余时间都不会变

➡️用户怎么参与AntSeed？

1、平时在Antseed上正常使用AI服务就能攒到ANTS，拿到币后可以去社区独立开发运营的市场（antseedmarkets）做质押

2、或者也可以直接在二级市场买入lANTS NFT即可，然后就可以直接享受现成的免费AI额度和周奖励

🤔之前的锁仓：单纯锁仓拿收益，锁仓了就失去了流动性，而且没有丝毫赋能

现在的锁仓：可以锁仓置换免费使用，而且还可以二级交易，不丢失流动性

AntSeed就是其中的代表项目之一，将“节点信用筛选 + 算力消费补贴 + 质押空投激励 + 锁仓凭证NFT化”拧在一起的设计，比单纯画饼讲AI算力故事要务实不少，挺有意思的

text:
纽约市长佐赫兰·曼达尼（Zohran Mamdani）一句话，想把延续了整整 100 年的梅西感恩节游行推迟到周六。

理由很简单：天气不好。结果全网骂声还没落地，远道而来的伊利诺伊大学行进乐队直接用脚投票——管你推不推迟，全员扛着铜管乐器和大鼓杀进时代广场，硬生生把一场官方叫停的空城，演成了全美最燃的街头感恩节庆典。

外行看热闹，觉得这是“热血大学生硬刚官僚市长”的爽文剧情；但只要你懂大型城市活动的商业账本和工程逻辑，就会发现这事背后藏着一个极其荒诞的现实悖论：市政厅以为自己只是在日历上把活动挪了两天，实际上却一脚踹翻了横跨航空、酒店、电视转播和百年零售业的精密齿轮。

1. 百年历史里，能让梅西游行停摆的只有“二战”
先把历史账本翻出来，你就知道为什么纽约人这次气炸了。

梅西感恩节游行从 1924 年办到现在，整整一个世纪，唯一停办过的年份是 1942 到 1944 年——那是因为二战爆发，氦气和橡胶全被美军征用造军工物资了。除此之外，刮风下雨、零下严寒，游行从来没挪过窝。

懂纽约警局（NYPD）安全规范的人都知道，游行其实早就有一套极其成熟的“恶劣天气工程预案”：

1997 年“戴帽子的猫”巨型气球被大风吹撞路灯致人重伤后，纽约立下了死规矩：只要持续风速超过每小时 23 英里，或阵风超过 34 英里，巨型气球就必须禁飞或降高。

重点在于：禁飞的是气球，不是整场游行。 花车照常开、乐队照常走、电视照常播。

曼达尼这次直接推动把整场游行推迟到周六，等于绕过了磨合几十年的分级风控机制，直接拉了总电闸。在城市治理里，这叫典型的“绝对免责式官僚避险”——只要我把活动延期，万一出了事锅就甩不到我头上，至于由此产生的连锁灾难，不在市政厅的 KPI 里。

2. 伊利诺伊大学乐队冲进时代广场，不只是热血，是算清了“沉没成本”
很多人夸伊利诺伊大学行进乐队（Marching Illini）有骨气，其实背后是一笔极其残酷的现实账。

一支顶级大学行进乐队来纽约参加梅西游行，动辄两三百号人加上成吨的乐器设备，机票、曼哈顿酒店、大巴车队全部是提前半年到一年锁死的不可退改订单，背后是学生家长和校友会辛辛苦苦筹了一整年的经费。

市长轻飘飘一句“改到周六”，对这些外州乐队意味着什么？

酒店多住两晚，感恩节黑五档期的曼哈顿房价直接翻倍，谁来买单？

返程航班集体改签，两三百张票的差价和空位去哪找？

他们根本等不到周六。 既然大老远来了，官方舞台没了，干脆直接把时代广场当舞台。这一波操作不仅保住了全队一年的心血，还顺手在全美社交媒体上拿下了比官方游行还炸裂的自然流量——顺带把市政厅的“天气危险论”啪啪打脸。

3. 挪动两天，撞碎的是“黑五前夜”的十亿级商业引信
梅西感恩节游行从来不只是给小孩看气球的公益活动，它是美国零售业与传媒业一年中最值钱的超级引擎之一：

对梅西百货（Macy's）而言：感恩节上午的全国直播，是紧接着第二天“黑色星期五”全美购物狂欢的最高转化率免费广告。游行推迟到周六，黑五都打完折了，这场营销大戏直接变成了“马后炮”。

对转播方（NBC 等）而言：感恩节上午是非 NFL 赛事之外全美收视率最顶级的黄金广告位，品牌方花天价买的贴片广告全按周四档期排死。临时挪到周六，不仅和大学橄榄球黄金档撞车，更是对广告主合同的毁灭性打击。

这场风波最讽刺的地方就在于此：

一边是手握公权力、试图用“安全至上”改写百年城市传统的纽约市长；另一边是拒绝为官僚决定买单、直接用铜管乐声接管时代广场的大学乐队。

如果让你站在纽约市民的角度做一次冷酷站队：面对恶劣天气预警，你觉得曼达尼推动延期是顶着骂名、把公共安全放在第一位的务实担当；还是完全不顾商业规律与外地游客死活的“一刀切”懒政，活该被伊利诺伊大学乐队在时代广场当众抢尽风头？

text:
Looking at the unfiltered long-term full sample from 1950 to 2025, Thanksgiving carries a strong upside win rate. 

Over the past 76 years, the S&P 500 has posted a 70% to 76% win rate on the Wednesday before Thanksgiving, on Black Friday, and across Thanksgiving week as a whole, yet the average single-day gain is only +0.28% to +0.33%, with the full week averaging just +0.71%.

When pre-Thanksgiving VIX is above 20, the S&P 500 has historically followed a four-stage sequence: pre-holiday restraint, a coin flip during Black Friday's half-day session, a sharp Monday washout and reversal, and a strong Tuesday through Friday recovery.

 With VIX above 20, the Black Friday seasonal rally myth immediately degrades into a coin flip, with a 50% win rate across the full sample and just 42.9% since 2007. 

Volatility and risk concentrate on Monday once institutional desks return, with an average daily range 2.6 times that of Black Friday and 6 of the last 7 modern instances reversing Friday's move. 

This comes down to institutional desks returning after the 68.5-hour weekend break right into November month-end rebalancing. 

Once Monday's washout clears positioning, early December inflows and retreating volatility typically drive a high-win-rate recovery from Tuesday through Friday, going 7 for 7 in the modern sample with an average gain of +3.71%, while equities pull back in a risk-off move ahead of the FOMC. 

Overall, the day before Thanksgiving and Friday premarket carry high odds of moving higher, though if premarket runs too far, it tends to pull back and mean-revert after the open. 

Friday's close remains uncertain, while next Monday will likely bring heavy volatility and a high probability of a pullback. 

Once Monday pulls back and sells off, the following sessions should continue to bounce and recover on short covering right up until the FOMC.

Historically, trading days where the SPX closed up more than 5% (73 times across its full history since 1928) have almost all been concentrated in major financial crises, geopolitical or macro black swans, or violent short squeezes during primary bear market downtrends, and have never occurred during low-volatility, steady bull market uptrends. 

Across all 24 occurrences of single-day gains ≥ 5% in modern US equities since 1950, the following day (T+1) has typically seen profit-taking and mean-reverting pullbacks. 

The index closed lower the next day 16 times (66.7%) and higher only 8 times (33.3%), with a mean next-day return of -0.81% (median -0.55%) across all 24 samples.

text:
Here's a quick explainer for anyone who isn't deep into this yet.

Every useful proof of work chain has two parts, and it helps to understand the essence when you keep them apart:

→ mining: the work that counts towards the block reward, nothing more, nothing less
→ useful work: the work someone actually uses

They obviously don't have to be the same, because mining can be partly useful and partly not. Plenty of chains out there call themselves useful work chains while only a small part of their mining does anything for real users.

The best case is that the two overlap completely, so every bit of work counts for both.

If they don't, you spend time and energy on one without getting the other. Push that far enough and you end up with a badly executed proof of useful work chain ... and when it's really bad, arguably just proof of work.

This brings bigger problems when the useful work is inference. Large compute providers aren't going to give up capacity to mine on the side, because why would they take on the overhead? And even if they did, miners would go for the cheapest work that counts, which pushes the difficulty up and shrinks the reward for anyone doing real useful work.

On @Tensorcash the useful work is inference, and it's the same work as the mining - the model writing an answer is what mines.
author: 100XInsight
quoted_text:
For those that don't understand… yes, this means you get two outputs from one unit of electricity, and that the mining is actually useful work.

Why? Because on @Tensorcash, every 256 tokens the model writes are hashed together with the latest block, and that hash is the shot at the block. Writing the answer is the mining.

Some chains claim the same, but they reward big matrix multiplications. That only fits reading the prompt, roughly 10% of the GPU's time. Writing the answer, the other ~90%, goes token by token and doesn't mine.

author: puffer_unifi
quoted_text:
💭 What If Ethereum L1 and L2 Could Compose in Real Time?

One of Ethereum’s greatest strengths is composability: the ability for smart contracts to interact within a single transaction.

But as more applications launched on L2s, they became separated from Ethereum’s mainnet and from each other.

Today, smart contracts on L1 and L2 cannot typically interact within the same transaction. Instead, they rely on bridges and asynchronous messaging, introducing delays, additional steps, and complexity.

@Puffer_UniFi is designed to overcome this limitation through based sequencing and synchronous composability.

By coordinating execution with Ethereum L1, Puffer UniFi enables smart contracts on L1 and L2 to interact atomically within the same transaction.

For developers, this opens the door to applications that combine L2 scalability with Ethereum’s existing protocols. For users, it means fewer cross-chain steps and more seamless interactions.

Scaling Ethereum shouldn’t mean breaking the connections between its applications. 🐡

it was only centuries later that we found that marrying your cousin also lowers IQ on average and  increases the risk of genetic diseases.

anyway, they keep doing it in these countries because clan-based social structures are still in place and because they never found jesus.

1/ 这波为什么跌

全球市场连在一起，很难归因到一件事

AI 公司陆续上市，SpaceX 1 万多亿美元，Anthropic 1.3 到 1.4 万亿，后面还有 OpenAI

区块链也一样，它已经不是最热的话题，但真正的建设现在才开始

4/ 四年周期是群体心理

四年一个高点、一个低点，到现在相当准
