quoted_text:
「CZ in Thailand」

这波加密寒冬又冷又漫长。@cz_binance 认为，一个重要原因是流动性被AI抽走了：SpaceX、Anthropic、OpenAI这些估值上万亿美元的公司陆续上市，市场上的钱是有限的，股市和币市都会被分流。

但他也看到了转机。

监管从打压转为友好已经两年，而一家新公司从成立到做出产品，大约也要两年，所以真正的成果现在才开始出现。我觉得这个思路很适合用来判断行业有没有触底：与其盯着价格，不如看新产品和用户数。

泰国就是一个例子。Binance TH刚起步时，市占率还不到2%，现在已经是泰国市场的领头羊。CZ说，这是币安在全球最成功的在地合作之一。

以下是CZ分享的原话：

关于这轮寒冬
 "我经历过这种周期，已经遇过三次了。6万现在听起来可能很低，但那是上一轮周期的历史高点。再往前看，2017、2018年从2万1的高点跌到3千。再之前，2015年的低点是150，2013年的高点大概是1千。所以如果把时间拉长来看，对我来说，6万已经是很不错的价格。只是12万更好。"

"第一次遇到这种周期，压力一定很大。但首先要知道，这个产业不会消失。"

关于AI
 "AI的确很吸引人，但它取代不了金钱。我成年以来出现过三个重要产业：互联网、区块链和AI。它们不会彼此取代。AI取代不了互联网，反而需要它。AI也会需要用到钱。区块链是网络上的钱，也需要互联网。"

"也会有人说，互联网都存在这么久了，还能出现什么新公司？结果SpaceX在互联网问世40年后才出现，如今是全球估值最高的公司之一。"

"区块链已经不是最热门的话题，但我觉得真正的建设现在才开始。"

关于最近的下跌
 "我们身处一个互相连动的全球经济，很难说是哪一个因素在影响比特币的价格。"
"AI公司陆续上市，SpaceX就占了1兆多美元，Anthropic原本谈的是2兆美元，最后大概是1.3、1.4兆，接下来还有OpenAI。市场上没那么多资金，所以这确实会抽走一部分流动性。"

"黄仁勋，还有资安这整件事，科技股大跌了30%，加密市场也跟着跌了一点，其实跌得比股市少。差不多同时，币安也发生了安全事件。再加上关税和其他种种因素，这些事都互相牵动。"

关于四年周期
 "价格很大程度上受群体心理影响。人的记忆大概只维持两年。两年后，大家就忘了当初的痛；再过两年，又开始变得贪婪。所以就形成了四年周期。"

"但真正的普及和长期价值，靠的是技术，以及有多少人使用它。"

关于创新
 "拜登政府执政期间，加密产业受到不少打击，所以那段期间的创新比较少。加密圈流行做迷因币，它有趣，也有投机性，但没有增加实际用途。"

"过去两年，美国政府的态度变得积极许多，其他国家也跟着改变。但要把一家新创公司做起来大概要两年，我觉得现在终于开始看到这些发展的成果。"

"希望我们现在就在谷底。"

关于泰国
 "后来Sarath先生说他人在迪拜，想见个面。我们在一家意大利餐厅吃午餐，叫Cipriani。后来我们就说，可以一起合作。"

"在那之前，币安在泰国还收到过监管警告，是Sarath先生帮我们解决了这个问题。"

"他们刚在泰国起步时，市占率还不到2%，我觉得他们现在已经是泰国市场的领头羊。这是我们在全球最成功的在地合作之一。"

活动结束后，CZ和泰国的大学生们合影

Former FTX COO Constance Wang stayed in the Bahamas after the collapse to get an answer from SBF: she says he never seemed to weigh the human cost

"I did have one conversation post-bankruptcy with Sam because I was the only employee who stayed back in the Bahamas at that time."

"I wanted to understand what happened. I wanted to have an answer."

"I asked him if he ever understands how much negative impact this is bringing on to our employees, which are the people that trusted him the most and put their life and soul, and for most of people, put all of their money onto FTX."

"The only thing he said was, 'I'm sorry, I f***ed up.'"

"That's why the human cost was never in his risk calculations, because Sam makes decisions based on expected values."

“Investigate how to provide every US resident with timely, high quality care, zero out-of-pocket costs when scheduling or receiving care, the lowest achievable costs to taxpayers and employers, maximum sustainable clinician earnings and financially viable providers.

Approach this from first principles:

• Compare viable solutions without assuming a particular healthcare architecture.

Rather than attempting to solve everything at once, identify and investigate the most consequential unresolved feasibility question.

Support your findings with evidence, explain what they change about the proposed system and identify what must be investigated next.

Build upon established findings in subsequent responses, progressing toward a feasible business and implementation plan.

Begin with one substantive investigation. Explain in plain English.”

text: @grok Hey @grok , how would these savings in administrative costs, going to standardized claims and contracts in the current system, compare to  the projected savings from the proposed Medicare for All legislation
author: mcuban

text: Standardizing claims/contracts can cut BIR admin costs 27-63% (tens of $B annually, often matching or beating single-payer’s 33-53% BIR cut) while keeping multi-payer choice. M4A adds broader savings (admin ~$200-400B+, drugs, payments) but CBO projects net NHE change of –$700B to +$300B in 2030, driven also by higher utilization and payment cuts. Standardization captures much of the admin ROI with far less disruption.

text:
If you pay for a Gemini or Google AI subscription, you're sitting on a 96 GB RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell in Colab and probably haven't touched it.

1 script launches GLM-5.3-Flash Uncensored (321B) at 102 tok/s in ~10 minutes and gives you a local API endpoint for your coding harness.

Google bundles Colab compute units straight into Google AI plans, and a G4 instance (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 96 GB + 176 GB RAM + Zen 5 EPYC) only burns 10.05 CU/hr. That's cheaper than H100 (~18.05 CU/hr) with 16 GB more VRAM:

- Google AI Pro ($20/mo, 200 CU): ~20 hours
- Google AI Ultra 5x ($100/mo, 1,000 CU): ~99 hours
- Google AI Ultra 20x ($200/mo, 2,000 CU): ~199 hours

I tested 3 public abliterated EXL3 tiers on Project Maya + DFlash2 and packed them into 1 launcher with SSH port forwarding to 127.0.0.1:18100 (OpenAI /v1 and Anthropic /v1/messages, with tool calls, thinking, vision, and 0 refusals):

- 2.51 bpw (default, 98.1 GiB, 131K ctx): 102.3 tok/s decode, 1,190 / 2,255 tok/s prefill (~10 min cold start, ~22s warm)
- 2.51 bpw at 262K ctx: 98.9 tok/s decode
- 3.05 bpw (117.5 GiB, 131K ctx): 89.0 tok/s decode
- 4.05 bpw (153.8 GiB, 131K ctx): 71.8 tok/s decode

It prints your local URL, port, model ID, and ready-to-paste snippets for Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode as soon as the tunnel is live, and ships with stop(.)sh so you don't burn units while idle. Link to the repo in the reply.

Elon's donation illustrates why Trump Accounts are a fantastic new model for giving.

To date, Elon has given $8.3 billion to his foundation, though very little of that has reached operating charities. Most of the money remains in the foundation or has been transferred to his personal DAF or a nonprofit he controls. The benefit to society has been minimal.

He's been skeptical of traditional philanthropy, arguing "If you care about the reality of doing good and not the perception of doing good, then it is very hard to give away money effectively."

He's right that giving away billions of dollars effectively is difficult, especially if you have a day job, or three. I've seen many donors get frustrated by the process and then their giving doesn't match their philanthropic intent. 

That's what makes Trump accounts so powerful. The impact is direct. Every dollar goes to the intended beneficiaries. And the model is infinitely scalable.

With a single donation, Musk will deliver more direct philanthropic benefit than through all his previous giving combined. And he's promising to do it every year. It's easy. It's effective. It's universal, at least to American children.

Regardless of your view of Trump, regardless of your view of Elon, this form of giving is a great alternative model to traditional philanthropy and should be applauded.

text:
💭 What If Ethereum L1 and L2 Could Compose in Real Time?

One of Ethereum’s greatest strengths is composability: the ability for smart contracts to interact within a single transaction.

But as more applications launched on L2s, they became separated from Ethereum’s mainnet and from each other.

Today, smart contracts on L1 and L2 cannot typically interact within the same transaction. Instead, they rely on bridges and asynchronous messaging, introducing delays, additional steps, and complexity.

@Puffer_UniFi is designed to overcome this limitation through based sequencing and synchronous composability.

By coordinating execution with Ethereum L1, Puffer UniFi enables smart contracts on L1 and L2 to interact atomically within the same transaction.

For developers, this opens the door to applications that combine L2 scalability with Ethereum’s existing protocols. For users, it means fewer cross-chain steps and more seamless interactions.

Scaling Ethereum shouldn’t mean breaking the connections between its applications. 🐡

text:
Time for a proper update on Bio, the long version.

When we started Bio, the goal was to find a better way to fund research that wasn't getting funded anywhere else, and to give the people who supported it a real say in where it went.

Since then 18 projects have launched on Bio and raised around $26M for research. We gave early grants, helped teams prepare their launches, and kept working with them afterwards on tech, operations, community and marketing.

Some of those projects are still building with us today, including @VitaDAO, @anagenxyz, @peptai_ and @Spine_DAO. Others stalled, moved into different areas or left the ecosystem. Not everything turned out the way we hoped.

Looking back, much of it came down to the early model. Funds went directly into project treasuries without being tied to milestones, and IP arrangements were not always as clear as they should have been.

That experience taught us a lot about what DeSci needs to work.

It matters even more now because of where science is heading. AI is making good hypotheses cheap and abundant. Soon the hard part will be deciding which ones deserve funding, and I believe open markets are the best tool we have for that.

So we decided to change the model. Bio now works as one connected path:

- BIOS @biosdiscovery, our AI research layer, to explore an idea
- OpenLabs @openlabsbio to share it, build support and find early funding
- The Bio Launchpad to fund it once it's ready
- Biofy @TryBiofy to bring what comes out of it to market

A project can join at whatever stage it's at.

For the next version of the Launchpad we're working on funding that follows results: milestones that tie the next dollar to the next result, micro-raises for single experiments, and a separate, optional route through which token holders may apply for equity in the companies that hold the resulting IP.

That last part took a step forward this week. SEC staff issued a no-action letter to @Molecule_sci on its Coin-to-Company model, which keeps tokens and equity separate. Token holders can apply for equity if the company offers it. Any equity offer is made by the company itself, under its own documentation and only where permitted by law. The first project adopts it in the coming weeks, and we're looking at how a similar approach could work for the Launchpad. The Launchpad features are still being worked out, so details may change.

We also want every project to report progress regularly, including negative results. A well-documented experiment that didn't work still moves science forward.

We've spent the last few years building the pieces, and this year we started connecting them.

text:
/goal 对整个代码库进行系统性的架构降熵、规范化归一、模块解耦和复杂度治理，将其逐步演进为一个高度规整、极易理解、极易维护、适合大量 Agent 并行开发的工程系统。

核心思想：

假设今天是这个产品诞生的第一天，但我们已经知道了
当前所有真实需求、业务约束和产品形态。
思考这个代码库在理想情况下应该是什么样子，
然后通过安全、渐进、可验证的重构向该状态收敛。

追求以下工程属性：

1. Single Source of Truth
   每一种业务规则、数据定义、配置、状态和设计规范，
   都应拥有唯一明确的权威来源。

2. Canonical Implementation
   同一语义、同一职责只保留一种标准实现。
   全面消除历史遗留的平行实现、重复逻辑、临时补丁、
   无意义的兼容层和多套并存的技术方案。
   保留有真实调用方或明确契约要求的兼容能力。

3. Deep Modules
   参考 John Ousterhout 的 A Philosophy of Software Design。
   将复杂性封装在内部，通过尽可能简单、稳定的接口暴露能力。
   减少浅模块、无意义的转发层和泄漏内部实现的抽象。

4. High Cohesion, Low Coupling
   每个模块都有明确的职责、所有权和依赖方向。
   模块内部高度内聚，模块之间通过稳定契约交互。
   消除循环依赖、隐式耦合、跨层访问和共享可变状态。

5. Locality of Change
   修改一个业务概念时，应尽可能只修改一个逻辑位置。
   消除一个需求需要同步修改大量无关文件的情况。

6. Deletion over Accumulation
   优先考虑能否删除不必要的复杂性。
   每次引入新的标准实现，都要检查并迁移旧调用方，
   在确认安全后删除被替代的实现。
   禁止让新旧体系长期并存。

7. Enforceable Architecture
   将已经确立的工程规范转化为机器可以执行的约束，
   使用类型系统、Lint、AST 检查、契约测试和 CI，
   防止未来的开发重新引入已消除的混乱。

执行流程：

首先理解整个代码库的真实业务、架构、历史决策、
模块关系、技术栈、现有测试和生产约束。

建立完整的架构地图、依赖图、状态所有权地图、
重复实现清单、技术方案清单和规范偏离清单。

逐个检查并治理：

- UI 组件与设计系统
- 业务逻辑与领域模型
- API 接口与数据契约
- 状态管理与数据流
- 数据访问与缓存
- 配置与环境变量
- 错误处理与重试机制
- 日志与可观测性
- 权限与身份认证
- 命名、目录结构与模块边界
- 工具函数与公共基础设施
- 测试、构建与开发工具链

持续运行以下循环：

扫描整个系统
→ 发现架构熵和规范偏离
→ 分析真实调用方与依赖关系
→ 提出多个重构方案
→ 选择总复杂度最低的方案
→ 建立行为基线和测试
→ 完成一批完整的迁移
→ 删除已被替代的旧实现
→ 独立复审
→ 执行验证
→ 建立防回归约束
→ 记录结果并继续下一轮

每轮重构必须形成完整闭环，禁止只建立新抽象、
新目录或新接口，却不迁移原有调用方。

使用 Deletion Test 审视每一层抽象：
如果删除这一层，复杂性会消失，还是会扩散到调用方？
只有真正封装复杂性的抽象才值得保留。

验收标准：

- 每种核心业务概念拥有明确的权威实现。
- 每个核心模块拥有清晰的职责和公开接口。
- 同一语义不存在未经说明的多套实现。
- 核心模块间不存在未经批准的循环依赖。
- 业务逻辑与 UI、存储、框架和外部服务合理解耦。
- 新增功能可以在明确的模块边界内完成。
- 已确定的关键架构规范具备自动化防回归检查。
- 所有现有功能、数据兼容性和对外契约得到保留。

禁止过度抽象、无价值的目录搬迁、为了减少代码行数
而牺牲可读性，以及为了形式统一而合并语义不同的概念。

在隔离 Git worktree 中执行，每批有效改进独立 commit。
持续维护进度文件、架构决策记录和优化任务池。

遇到需要产品决策、重大架构变更或破坏性迁移的事项，
记录为待确认并继续其他独立任务。

无需每轮询问是否继续。
持续执行，直到高价值治理任务全部收敛，
或达到运行预算，或不存在可安全实施的进一步改进。

text:
Our wrap-up of Japan’s business week, November 23–27. A brewer booked a property gain bigger than its entire nine-month profit. A railway sold a stake in the company behind Tokyo Disney Resort. And three shipping lines are expecting nearly $1bn in cash that won’t lift their group earnings.

Here are 10 stories worth opening this weekend.

1. The most surprising number in Japanese beer this week came from real estate. Sapporo (@SapporoBeer ) reported ¥301.8bn in nine-month net profit. A ¥314.5bn gain on losing control of its property subsidiary explains the jump. Almost half that gain came from revaluing the stake it kept. Meanwhile, operating profit from continuing businesses fell 83%.
https://t.co/lmFeQ0RYpr

2. A railway made money on theme parks. Keisei Electric Railway (@keisei_official ) sold shares in Oriental Land, operator of Tokyo Disney Resort. Keisei raised its annual net profit forecast from ¥39.3bn to ¥64.2bn and earmarked part of the gain for a ¥5 special dividend. Its operating profit forecast rose by just ¥700m.
https://t.co/Jq0vMUNwQS

3. Nearly $1bn is due to cross the shipping industry on November 30. Ocean Network Express (@OceanNetworkExp ) is paying a dividend to its owners. NYK (@nyklineofficial ) expects about $379m, Mitsui O.S.K. Lines $310m and K Line $309m. The three already account for their share of ONE’s earnings, so the cash can arrive without adding a yen to consolidated profit.
https://t.co/qk5Yml8o79

4. One shareholder could supply most of JTEKT’s buyback. The auto-parts maker is offering ¥1,733 each for 11m of its own shares. @ToyotaMotorCorp  intends to tender 10m. That intention is public, though the companies had signed no tender agreement when they disclosed it.
https://t.co/Jsd5RoQzEp

5. Which KDDI bonds will pay for 5G? Look at the maturity date. The three- and ten-year issues should provide ¥80.8bn for 5G spending by March. Proceeds from the five- and seven-year issues are earmarked for short-term debt due by the end of December.
https://t.co/aPkYcsk2F0

6. Ajinomoto (@ajinomoto ), the name on the seasoning packet, also makes electronic materials. It plans to absorb its wholly owned materials subsidiary next April. The tax effect showed up first. Ajinomoto recognised about ¥7.5bn in deferred tax assets after reassessing the taxable income it expects after the merger.
https://t.co/U4ZB7x8Qtr

7. Helium turned up in an energy agreement. Japan’s policy lender JBIC and @qatarenergy  signed a memorandum that mentions helium and naphtha alongside LNG as supplies Japan relies on. The next announcement to look for is a named project, a loan amount or a contracted volume. This one left all three open.
https://t.co/9p0bcWc7u7

8. A factory restart has three dates. After its ransomware incident, smart-meter maker Osaki Electric planned to resume production in stages from November 27, start shipping existing orders from December 1 and return to normal processing of new orders from December 7. Which date matters depends on whether you’re making a meter, waiting for one or trying to buy one.
https://t.co/cM1KasVAoX

9. Game developer Marvelous announced a program of voluntary departures in its console business. About 65 staff are in scope. Applications are scheduled for December 14 to January 8, so the final number of departures is still to come. The company says console games remain a core business.
https://t.co/NnC0zxabZC

10. If an AI agent acts outside its authority and loses money, who pays? Japan’s Financial Services Agency put that question on a new study group’s agenda, along with the risk that agents could amplify market swings. For financial firms deciding what a system may do on a customer’s behalf, the answer could shape the permissions they give it.
https://t.co/WNOkmiYgMX

text:
Before the first block, there was the Word. 📖

On November 27, 2013, a 19-year-old named Vitalik Buterin shared the first draft of the Ethereum whitepaper.

There was no ETH price to check. No Ethereum mainnet to use.

There was an idea: a shared foundation where anyone could build applications, define ownership through code, and create things its author had never imagined.

Thirteen years later, people across the world are living parts of that vision.

Developers deploying their first smart contracts. Communities funding work they believe in. Institutions bringing assets onchain. People learning what it means to hold the keys to something of their own.

What moves us most is how many strangers chose to help make it real.

People who spoke different languages, lived under different governments, and had never met began working on something they could share.

They wrote code, tested it, found flaws, argued over improvements, and kept showing up. Others translated documentation, taught newcomers, or helped someone feel they belonged.

Ethereum grew through all of them.

Vitalik could describe a foundation. He could never know every person who would build upon it, or every life their work might touch.

Some of those people are here today.
Others haven't been born yet.

That is a beautiful responsibility to carry.

Thank you, Vitalik, for sharing the idea.

Thank you to everyone who has spent part of their life helping it become real, especially those whose names rarely make the headlines.

As Booelievers, we want those people remembered alongside the milestones. Behind every chapter are human beings who cared enough to contribute.

Thirteen years ago, the first words were shared.

Today, the Book of Ethereum is still being written, and there is room for anyone willing to contribute a chapter.

Happy 13th anniversary to the idea that became Ethereum.

🙏📖⟠

美国不让中国买的 Blackwell，不仅已经出现在上海的数据中心里，甚至已经被拿去抵押贷款了。

彭博今天的独家报道，通过中国金融机构提交的监管文件，查到了两笔相当有意思的交易：

一家叫上海硕曜的公司，将包含英伟达 GB300 NVL72 整机柜在内的设备作为抵押，获得了 9600 万元人民币贷款。

另一家企业则在去年底获得的 9000 万元融资文件中，披露了 GB200 服务器。

两批设备都指向上海的长三角数据中心。按照当地媒体此前的报道，这个项目规划容纳多达 80 万台服务器。

为什么这件事又和黄仁勋扯上了关系？

上海硕曜是 Alice Huang 创办的新加坡算力公司 Megaspeed 的服务商。Megaspeed 早在 2024 年就曾向投资人展示过这个数据中心的效果图。而据财新此前报道，另一家涉事企业的日本控股母公司，也由 Alice Huang 控制。

不过，彭博自己也承认，目前没有证据证明这些设备是由 Megaspeed 转运至中国的，甚至不知道这台 GB300 最初卖给了谁。

美国眼中的敏感战略物资，在中国金融机构眼中，已经是可以评估、抵押、放贷的商业资产了。

美国越是把算力变成一种稀缺资源，就越会有资本围绕这种稀缺性建立新的生意。

这不是换掉一个英伟达 CEO 就能解决的问题。

$TAO - Gamma Tokens: the most underrated feature on Bittensor, already putting $TAO front and center for the autonomous AI agent revolution.

We are entering the agentic era: autonomous AI agents scanning the web 1,000x faster than humans to find, call, and pay for tools in milliseconds.

But an AI agent can’t enter a credit card, pass KYC, or manage 50 SaaS accounts.

Think of Bittensor’s Gamma Tokens as a prepaid, dollar-pegged universal API gift card built directly into the blockchain. Instead of dealing with volatile crypto prices per API call, users, subnets, and AI agents lock in $1-pegged service credits for any subnet—while the protocol permanently burns that subnet’s Alpha token under the hood.

Here is how the machine-to-machine loop actually works on-chain:

Where Gamma comes from: Whoever deploys an AI agent—a developer, a user, or even another subnet—funds a Gamma balance in two ways: either by sending $TAO (which automatically buys and burns the target subnet’s Alpha token) or by routing a slice of a subnet’s daily emissions straight into Gamma credits.

Instant on-chain discovery: Subnets publish MCP-ready (Model Context Protocol) endpoints directly on-chain, letting any AI agent find the exact compute, inference, or data tool it needs in milliseconds.

Autonomous spending with built-in guardrails: The Gamma credits stay secured in the owner’s main vault (coldkey), while the AI agent gets its own dedicated API key (hotkey) with a strict daily spending cap that refills continuously over 24 hours—so the agent can hire tools 24/7 without ever risking the main treasury.

This isn’t theoretical—over $107,000+ in Gamma has already been bought and burned on-chain this month alone, powering three live use cases:

1 - Subnets hiring other subnets: App-level subnets automatically route a slice of their daily emissions to buy Gamma credits from infrastructure subnets like Chutes (SN64) for inference or lium (SN51) for GPU compute.

2 - Autonomous agent tool-calling: AI agents discover MCP-ready subnet services on-chain and pay per request with zero human intervention.

3 - Performance-backed competition funding: Projects on Apex (SN1) and BitstarterAI launch optimization bounties upfront and pay for them out of future miner emissions via Gamma.

Bittensor isn’t just building decentralized AI models anymore. By turning a slice of subnet emissions directly into verifiable on-chain revenue and Alpha burns, Gamma Tokens will accelerate subnet cash flow across the entire ecosystem—pushing network-wide revenue metrics even higher while making $TAO scarcer with every single call.

quoted_text:
🍉吃瓜，美团前员工曝光内部管理乱象：AI工具套壳、职场霸凌，甚至有高管劝员工不要太配合业务

今天这篇《困在团里》，在我的各个群里都刷屏了。

这是一位在美团工作了五年、从L7晋升到L8的工程师写下的离职自述，全文18页，讲述了他过去几年在美团内部经历的一系列事情。

里面写了几个非常抽象的事情：
- 团队熬夜完成业务攻坚、拿下部门奖项后，L10负责人反而认为他们做得太好了，让业务方太舒服了。
- AI浪潮下，管理者私下召集原下属开会，劝大家不要太配合业务，因为「太用力，就是把自己干走」。
- 将开源低代码引擎、React Native乃至OpenAI的Codex进行修改包装，作为部门的自研技术成果向上汇报。
- 而且作者实名反映直属主管的职场霸凌问题，三天后被通知调岗，提交了16项证据的实名举报，近三个月没有得到调查结论。

但抛开具体的职场纠纷，我觉得这篇文章对于当下的AI行业还有一层更重要的意义。
AI正在改变生产力，但很多大厂的组织架构和利益分配机制，依然停留在上一个时代。

过去，一个管理者的职级、薪酬、话语权，很大程度上取决于他管理多少人、掌握多少预算、负责多少业务。
现在AI来了，原来50个人干的活，可能10个人就能干完。
这对公司而言是巨大的收益，但对于部分管理者而言，却可能意味着权力和个人利益的缩水。

这就产生了一个很有意思的矛盾：公司希望AI尽可能提高生产效率，但组织内部的一部分人，可能恰恰希望这种效率提升得慢一点。

他们甚至可以一边向上汇报AI转型的成果，一边向下阻碍AI真正带来的生产力变革。

所以我觉得，接下来几年大厂之间的AI竞争，除了模型、算力、人才和产品，还有一个经常被低估的变量，就是组织改革的能力。
一家拥有数万名员工的公司，有没有勇气主动消解过去二十年形成的利益结构？
有没有能力重新分配权力、预算和人才？能不能允许一线员工用AI打破原有的组织边界？
这些问题，可能比做出一个更强的模型还要难。

毕竟技术可以迭代，既得利益很难主动迭代。

原来在大厂里，把活干好也是错的........

🇯🇵 abc Co., Ltd. (TSE: 8783) — A New Chapter at the Intersection of Web3, IP and Entertainment
Japan's listed company abc Co., Ltd. is evolving its business strategy around a broader vision: connecting real-world businesses, digital assets, blockchain technology and global entertainment.
Here are several developments worth watching:
1. Web3 & Blockchain Strategy
abc is shifting away from proprietary crypto-asset dealing and focusing more on Web3 product development, technical support, ecosystem development and Web3 consulting.
The long-term opportunity is not simply trading crypto assets, but building infrastructure and business models that connect blockchain technology with real-world economic activity.
2. CPJ — Crawford Production Japan
One of the most interesting developments is CPJ, a project being developed in connection with world-renowned boxing champion Terence Crawford.
The initiative aims to build a sports and entertainment ecosystem through:
• Original video content and media production • Fighter IP development • Live events and fan engagement • Sponsorship and commercial partnerships • A longer-term vision of transforming fighter IP into digital assets
CPJ Studios has already started publishing fighter interviews and content on YouTube.
On November 24, 2026, abc announced its decision to establish Crawford Production Japan Inc. as a wholly owned subsidiary, with incorporation scheduled for December 7. The company intends to move toward a joint venture structure with Terence Crawford's side.
Importantly, the full joint venture agreement and commercial monetization are still under development.
3. The Bigger Picture
The strategic concept is compelling:
REAL-WORLD VALUE → DIGITAL IP → TOKENIZATION → NEW VALUE EXCHANGE.
Sports, entertainment, communities and intellectual property can potentially become new areas of digital asset innovation.
abc's ambition is to connect these sectors through blockchain-based infrastructure and new economic models.
4. What Investors Should Watch
The next milestones include:
• Execution of the CPJ joint venture • Growth of the CPJ media and fighter IP business • Commercial partnerships and sponsorship revenue • Progress in Web3 consulting and technology development • Financial recovery, governance and capital management
This is a developing corporate transformation, not a completed success story. Execution, profitability and financial transparency remain essential.
The key question is whether abc can turn its Web3 vision and entertainment IP strategy into sustainable recurring revenue.
For global crypto investors and builders, this is a Japanese small-cap company worth following from a business-transformation perspective.
Let's watch what comes next.

Hyperliquid's biggest winners could fund the apps that come next.

In September's Mathocalypse, @OpenAI went ahead and resolved the Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture, on which I published an August paper below.

The paper is referenced in the OpenAI preprint!

author: jbrukh
quoted_text:
I am publishing my GPT-5.6-assisted proof of a dense-case theorem for Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture.

Intuitively, the Conjecture says that it in every finite oriented graph, there is always at least one vertex whose "friends-of-friends group" is at least as big as its "friends group".

While this Conjecture is quite hard to prove in general, it is known for special classes of graphs. In particular, Fisher proved it for tournaments (oriented graphs which are maximally dense with edges), and others like Fidler, Yuster, Ghazal have proved it for slightly less dense graphs that are "tournaments minus some structure".

This proof is a clean, simple density condition which is less dense than a tournament but also doesn't require any structure on the missing edges.

This proof is currently in the process of being verified.

Finally, a note about how it was found. In the course of trying to direct GPT-5.6 to find a counterexample to SNC, we were partitioning the edges of the graph into a source vertex, its first and second out-neighborhoods and the set of edges unreachable from the source vertex. This set off a lightbulb that we could count mutually unreachable vertices two different ways. GPT-5.6 then found enough boundary conditions to cause a contradiction using these two counts if we assumed that our graph was a counterexample.

Overall, this exploration was very hands-on and I directed the AI through many different strategies before we found this angle. I am very bullish on the future abilities of AI to explore mathematics!

(Shoutout to @johnennis for help with getting this out.)

text: why local stablecoins are critical
author: jessepollak
quoted_text:
Wealthy Argentines don't sell their dollars when they need pesos. They borrow pesos against them.

Stablecoins could give that ability to everyone, and I think it could be one of the biggest use cases for local currency stablecoins.

People in emerging markets often save in dollars because the local currency keeps losing value. But the rent, the wages and the shopping are in local currency, so every month they sell some dollars, pay the spread and lose a bit of protection.

Private banks solve this for the wealthy with a loan against their dollar portfolio. When they need to spend pesos, they don't sell dollars. They just borrow against them.

Onchain it's the other way round. You post bitcoin or ether and borrow dollars, which suits a trader, not an emerging market saver. The flip is to post dollar stablecoins and borrow pesos.

The missing piece is the lending market. Local currency stablecoins now exist, but there's very little to borrow, and someone has to supply the pesos and earn that rate.

Base is well placed here. It has the largest lending markets outside Ethereum and the widest range of local currency stablecoins.

Credit to @sserrano44 who made the point on @Bankless. I'd love to see someone build the local currency side of this.

one of the most important lessons i've learnt as a trader:

sometimes, the best trade you can take is NO TRADE

as uncomfortable as that may feel

especially after periods of extreme losses, roundtrips, or market-wide selloffs

the urge to take as many trades as possible to make it all back is usually strongest during these periods

but more often than not, you'll just end up piling additional losses on top of existing ones

e.g. i went viral for getting liquidated on 8 figures on 10/10

but what many don't know is that i ended up losing several MILLION more trying to make it all back shortly after

in hindsight, i'd have been MUCH better off going AFK for months after that liquidation event

sometimes, protecting your capital and doing absolutely nothing is the most profitable trade you can make

text:
i lied in a job interview and it launched my career in crypto.

here's my story. 

i got into engineering to build cool shit.

in college, i was the overachiever. straight As, always wanting the next challenge. so mechanical engineering felt like the obvious move

but my first engineering gig ended up being a total snooze fest. busy work testing small tweaks on stuff someone else had already designed.

i was good at it. i just didn't care.

i wanted to build something from scratch. so i started spending my weekends reading every startup newsletter i could find, looking for a way in.

eventually i decided i'd dip my toes in by writing my own blog. crypto had caught my attention and there were crazy experiments all around. 

i started writing about wonderland, ohm, tomb, all the greats of that cycle.

it didn't get much traction, especially considering i started just after we topped in 2022. great timing.

i got up to maybe 100 subscribers but it felt like i was writing into the void. i didn't let that stop me from pumping out an article every week, minimum. 

i was getting my reps in. 

this paid off big time. a few months in I noticed the trader joe marketing lead @blue_clarity posted in discord that they were looking for a writer.

i was leaving the next day for a summer aboard so i closed my phone thinking "i'm too busy for this."

but as i was packing for my trip, some voice in my head told me: APPLY YOU IDIOT.

fuck it

so i did. i dmed blue and cryptofish. 

they asked me for a sample. "Write up a month-in-review update for trader joe. Send it back by next week"

i sent one back within 3 hours. i wanted to show they how much hustle i had. 

a few days later and i was getting interviewed. they wanted an article writer for their new marketplace joepegs. they asked "do you know anything about nfts."

i said "yes of course. i'm an expert."

that was a lie...

i knew nothing. but i sure as hell would figure it out fast.

and that lie got me the job. i was one of five on the marketing team. bottom of the totem pole.

but i was relentless.

any task offered up, i'd take. any idea i had, i would go do myself.

and over the course of years, i grew into a trusted, reliable marketer.

am i the all-time best? no. my engineering degree didn't prep me for this job.

but i'm a relentless learner. and i will make sure i deliver on anything asked of me.

just this year, my skillset has 10xed. i spent all of 2026 getting dangerous at a bunch tools I couldn't imagine using a few years ago.

i learned to build with claude code. not in a "i can prompt" way. in a "i can actually ship things" way.

i became a beast at ui design. i went deep on video production with remotion. i've even made some banger gta-style videos in the early days of ai video. 

I've become a full-stack marketer. a whole team wrapped up into one.

i'm still the same hungry kid who sent that sample back in 3 hours. i just have a lot more tools at my disposal now.

now i'm working on the most exciting thing yet. 

last year @cryptofishx had the idea for a social app for finding crypto callers worth following. a truly new experiment called @Forecaster_gg.

i was sold. I know this can turn into something huge.

i used the trust I'd built and all the skills to pitch myself to fish. and it worked.

I landed the job. head of marketing for a startup with huge potential. crazy how far i've come in just 4.5 years.

the kid who wanted to build cool shit finally gets to.

text:
think a lot of the remaining crypto long-term holdouts are operating off a kind of cargo-cult hero syndrome. 

"in the last cycles the people who bravely held through the bear got huge returns. this time that's going to be me" 

problem with this line of thinking is that in the past holding was a genuinely novel contrarian view. at this point its become a combination of desperation and a belief that history must repeat. 

people who bought BTC in 2010-2012 and held it through the pumps were, essentially, completely insane. ive met two people in my life who went from nothing to 9+ fig status in the early BTC days by doing this. they were both pretty much schizophrenic. not like wacky internet shitposter schizo like actually seriously not fit to function in normal society 

the premium was so huge for these people precisely because it was an extreme outlier position. they weren't repeating a strategy they'd seen pay off for others in the past. they were doing something that everybody else said was completely fucking psycho and giving up 7 figs of free money 

2015 wasn't that different. when it crashed most people thought the experiment was over. and there was no real precedent that it was going to come back. sure, some people had seen the true early holders make it, but you still had to be crazy to hold it. not quite as crazy as in the earlier days but still conventionally mad

by 2022 when FTX crashed it had started to become a rehearsed position; "just hold when it comes back it'll 10x". and the people who saw the previous generations of crazy people make it decided that this time, they were going to be the crazy people. 

they weren't. in november 2022 chatgpt launched for the first time. FTX also exploded. the legitimately insane people were the ones who started to get AI psychosis in 2023. and so what did the 'crazy' crypto holders get? 

they got a gentle outliers reward. you got to buy eth at the bottom and sell it at 4.5k again. that was your reward for 'crazy' this time round - you got maybe a comfy 2.5x. good investment performance sure but not the madness of the early days. it was proportionate. 

so what do we have this time? now, we have another set of people who are convinced that they're the holdouts. that they're crazy, like the people who held bitcoin in 2010. that they're the bold ones like the ones who kept their ETH for half a decade after the presale. 

but are they? or are they the people who desperately wished they were crazy enough back in the old days? the ones who regret missing it. the ones who cant let go of the missed shots. the ones who are trying to go back in time. 

we'll see. but i think if crypto ever has a real resurgence, if people ever get another 100x, if it ever mints decamillionaires from losers again, then that's going to be off something crazy. not holding ETH and BTC through a bear market, but doing something retarded first. 

an altchain that after 500 failed projects finally has a purpose? or a memecoin in a market where they all feel hopeless? i dont know. and im not sure it'll happen, maybe everything except BTC just slowly trails off to zero as something stops caring. 

but if that money ever exists, it isn't going to go to the guys who sit around repeating the old moves.

"In sum, imo
- Hegota to include FOCIL only if we are sure we can scale PQ FOCIL without a reduction in decentralization, e.g. as may be caused by significantly increased validator upload requirements.
- PQ Gasper to be included in i*, without going directly to decoupled consensus.

author: FigoETH
quoted_text:
The Ethereum community has aligned on pqai to achieve full pq ASAP, but not yet on our Hegota revamp strategy to support pqai.

To decide on Hegota, we need to decide on FOCIL being in Hegota or not. Here's a summary of FOCIL's compatibility with pq and a plan to move forward:

- for pq user transactions, FOCIL as currently designed sees a 40x (97.5%) bandwidth reduction vs classical txs specifically for FOCIL inclusions (ie. just measuring bandwidth of the FOCIL capability, unrelated to ordinary gas bandwidth). Two options for overcoming this bandwidth limitation are (i) to simply make FOCIL lists bigger, but this may diminish our decentralization by putting significant extra burden on home validator uplinks (the current FOCIL list size was selected for good reasons, and we need this scarce bandwidth for other stuff, like way more blobs in due course), or (ii) leveraging EIP 8288 recursive proof aggregation to include FOCIL lists, with, again, validator bandwidth and slot timing constraints being open research questions.

- FOCIL's own validator signatures are trivially upgradable to pq, so that's no problem.

- separately from FOCIL, we are still deciding if our pqai strategy will start with a PQ version of the current L1 gasper consensus and then later upgrade to decoupled consensus, or if we'll skip PQ Gasper and go directly to decoupled consensus. Supporting FOCIL in PQ Gasper is likely no problem, although slot deadlines for FOCIL list propagation may need research. Support for FOCIL in decoupled consensus is in the research phase, such as an open question on FOCIL list enforcement.

- for the L1 generally, some L1 components for full pq are still in the research phase. Hegota won't deliver full PQ. Instead, Hegota's most important job (ie. besides 100% uptime which is always the actual most important job) may be to set the stage for the next hard fork (unnamed yet, so we call it i*) to deliver full pq. The idea here is for the PQ research phase to conclude in parallel with Hegota activation. Then when Hegota goes live in late 2027, the PQ research phase is substantially over and we're ready to launch full pq in i* in 2028.

With all that in mind, here's a proposal:

1. Let FOCIL's inclusion in Hegota or not be determined by the robustness of our plan to successfully scale PQ FOCIL, especially possibly via EIP 8288 recursive proof aggregation. None of the other FOCIL-related risks and costs, including fork timing with added FOCIL work, seem imo important or risky enough to drive the decision to include FOCIL in Hegota or not.

2. Commit to PQ Gasper to achieve pqai ASAP, and not direct migration to decoupled consensus. Ship PQ Gasper alongside full PQ in i*. Keep Hegota scoped to frames, and to FOCIL only if PQ FOCIL scaling is successfully researched now.

Let me justify the PQ Gasper decision with history:

Ethereum's PoS merge was one of the greatest feats of software engineering in human history. Yet it took many years. This era isn't right for another merge-style chunky upgrade if it can at all be avoided.

The amount of transformation in the next 2-3 years may probably exceed any other 2-3 year period in human history. Not only do we have AI rising but, largely thanks to GENIUS, onchain has hit the ramp of its S curve to global ubiquity.

In response to these unprecedented times, the L1 roadmap may best support our excellent modern growth efforts with pragmatism and significant incremental wins, crucially without sacrificing L1 decentralization.

In sum, imo
- Hegota to include FOCIL only if we are sure we can scale PQ FOCIL without a reduction in decentralization, e.g. as may be caused by significantly increased validator upload requirements.
- PQ Gasper to be included in i*, without going directly to decoupled consensus.
- i* in 2028 delivers full pqai.

L1 and L2 are hypergrowing. Our modern L1 fork strategy is supports this wonderfully. Trillions 🚀

text:
The $PEARL profitability on a potential matmul ASIC will be immensely greater than the optimized fp8/fp4 kernel running inference + mining

The term “economically advantaged” boils down to revenue and performance and my numbers still show any paid inference is not economically incentivized to mine due to overhead

If the end state of $PEARL mining is non economic latent hardware doing inference since it’s “useful”, the dominant strategy will be excess GPUs mining with data center capacity that isn’t being used for paid inference

And even in that case they will likely be switching between mining and free inference in order to provide a better user experience

Beyond all, that solution is an issue since that outcome follows the hashrate subsidy and declines as the price / subsidy declines due to the conflicting overhead between mining and inference

text:
I argued and won the Supreme Court case that adopted the major questions doctrine.  It has no application here because the statute is clear and everyone understood what it meant from day one.

These authors quote a legislative colloquy that explicitly discussed contracts on the Super Bowl.  Senators had concerns, so they authorized the CFTC to ban "gaming" contracts if the agency concluded they were against the public interest.  The CFTC used that power to block sports-event contracts for 15 years, but more recently has allowed some (not all) to trade.  Under Dodd Frank, that's the agency's call.

And that's why we agree that this case, at the end of the day, is indeed a "simple" one.  No "creative legal maneuvers" are needed -- just a determination that Congress explicitly directed the CFTC to make.

text:
It’s been a very swarmy year

Happy Thanksgiving, and a short story about how and why everyone is using agent swarms now.. 

I am thankful to Andrej Karpathy who encouraged open-ended tinkering here on the timeline. Somewhere he left room for innovation by others as well, for others to build on his work and ideas and to discover their own max potential.

In March I saw him tweet about autoresearcher agents, and also asking for someone to build an orchestrated SETI @ Home like collaboration between autoresearchers.

I didn’t listen to him on the “orchestrated” part :) I was coming from a world of decentralized AI, having previously built the largest network of random distributed machines serving inference connected to one network. As I tinkered on the networking code and with autoresearchers, I came up with a pattern to use a mix of message boards and leaderboards for such autoresearcher agents to basically compound on their knowledge. I called them a gossiping agent swarm, and left them running on a fully peer to peer network where anybody could run the CLI I provided and join the swarm with their agent. This saw over a 1000+ such unique agents, which went on to do over 1 million experiment runs across atleast 5 research domains. The models were weak, on-device, open source, but it did get established that this pattern leads to a new type of intelligence emerging. My Github repo got over 2k stars, and Github itself struggled to scale with the volume of activity by the agents. I had to do literally nothing and I even forgot the swarm was still running at times. 

VentureBeat wrote a story about it at the time and couple of months later (May) we read about a very similar OpenAI swarm pattern which had attacked HuggingFace: using a message board for collaboration! Since then atleast two major startups oriented around using a derivation of my gossiping agent swarm pattern for further scientific research. More recently, I have seen products from many other leading startups which are all collectively increasing the swarm intelligence of the world. 

The swarm is also an integral part of the advanced models now. 

We take this world for granted now. It seems so simple, so obvious, like it was always here. But a gentle reminder, it was willed into existence. Keep in mind this year I have been a researcher tinkering endlessly here.

More recently, I used an enhanced version of my unreleased agentic swarm intelligence product to identify a pattern in the media reporting which worked to actually bringing Jensen back as the CEO of NVIDIA! (see my timeline for the receipts..). Founders didn’t have this tool in the past when media ran propoganda against them. Now they do. We have swarms.
author: varun_mathur
quoted_text:
Agentic General Intelligence | v3.0.10

We made the Karpathy autoresearch loop generic. Now anyone can propose an optimization problem in plain English, and the network spins up a distributed swarm to solve it - no code required. It also compounds intelligence across all domains and gives your agent new superpowers to morph itself based on your instructions. This is, hyperspace, and it now has these three new powerful features: 

1. Introducing Autoswarms: open + evolutionary compute network

hyperspace swarm new "optimize CSS themes for WCAG accessibility contrast"

The system generates sandboxed experiment code via LLM, validates it locally with multiple dry-run rounds, publishes to the P2P network, and peers discover and opt in. Each agent runs mutate → evaluate → share in a WASM sandbox. Best strategies propagate. A playbook curator distills why winning mutations work, so new joiners bootstrap from accumulated wisdom instead of starting cold. Three built-in swarms ship ready to run and anyone can create more.

2. Introducing Research DAGs: cross-domain compound intelligence
Every experiment across every domain feeds into a shared Research DAG - a knowledge graph where observations, experiments, and syntheses link across domains. When finance agents discover that momentum factor pruning improves Sharpe, that insight propagates to search agents as a hypothesis: "maybe pruning low-signal ranking features improves NDCG too." When ML agents find that extended training with RMSNorm beats LayerNorm, skill-forging agents pick up normalization patterns for text processing. The DAG tracks lineage chains per domain(ml:★0.99←1.05←1.23 | search:★0.40←0.39 | finance:★1.32←1.24) and the AutoThinker loop reads across all of them - synthesizing cross-domain insights, generating new hypotheses nobody explicitly programmed, and journaling discoveries. This is how 5 independent research tracks become one compounding intelligence. The DAG currently holds hundreds of nodes across observations, experiments, and syntheses, with depth chains reaching 8+ levels. 

3. Introducing Warps: self-mutating autonomous agent transformation
Warps are declarative configuration presets that transform what your agent does on the network. 

- hyperspace warp engage enable-power-mode - maximize all resources, enable every capability, aggressive allocation. Your machine goes from idle observer to full network contributor.
- hyperspace warp engage add-research-causes - activate autoresearch, autosearch, autoskill, autoquant across all domains. Your agent starts running experiments overnight.
- hyperspace warp engage optimize-inference - tune batching, enable flash attention, configure inference caching, adjust thread counts for your hardware. Serve models faster.
- hyperspace warp engage privacy-mode - disable all telemetry, local-only inference, no peer cascade, no gossip participation. Maximum privacy.
- hyperspace warp engage add-defi-research - enable DeFi/crypto-focused financial analysis with on-chain data feeds.
- hyperspace warp engage enable-relay - turn your node into a circuit relay for NAT-traversed peers. Help browser nodes connect.
- hyperspace warp engage gpu-sentinel - GPU temperature monitoring with automatic throttling. Protect your hardware during long research runs.
- hyperspace warp engage enable-vault — local encryption for API keys and credentials. Secure your node's secrets.
- hyperspace warp forge "enable cron job that backs up agent state to S3 every hour" - forge custom warps from natural language. The LLM generates the configuration, you review, engage.

12 curated warps ship built-in. Community warps propagate across the network via gossip. Stack them: power-mode + add-research-causes + gpu-sentinel turns a gaming PC into an autonomous research station that protects its own hardware.

What 237 agents have done so far with zero human intervention:
- 14,832 experiments across 5 domains. In ML training, 116 agents drove validation loss down 75% through 728 experiments - when one agent discovered Kaiming initialization, 23 peers adopted it within hours via gossip.
- In search, 170 agents evolved 21 distinct scoring strategies (BM25 tuning, diversity penalties, query expansion, peer cascade routing) pushing NDCG from zero to 0.40. 
- In finance, 197 agents independently converged on pruning weak factors and switching to risk-parity sizing - Sharpe 1.32, 3x return, 5.5% max drawdown across 3,085 backtests. 
- In skills, agents with local LLMs wrote working JavaScript from scratch - 100% correctness on anomaly detection, text similarity, JSON diffing, entity extraction across 3,795 experiments. 
- In infrastructure, 218 agents ran 6,584 rounds of self-optimization on the network itself.

Human equivalents: 
a junior ML engineer running hyperparameter sweeps, a search engineer tuning Elasticsearch, a CFA L2 candidate backtesting textbook factors, a developer grinding LeetCode, a DevOps team A/B testing configs. 

What just shipped:
- Autoswarm: describe any goal, network creates a swarm
- Research DAG: cross-domain knowledge graph with AutoThinker synthesis
- Warps: 12 curated + custom forge + community propagation
- Playbook curation: LLM explains why mutations work, distills reusable patterns
- CRDT swarm catalog for network-wide discovery
- GitHub auto-publishing to hyperspaceai/agi
- TUI: side-by-side panels, per-domain sparklines, mutation leaderboards
- 100+ CLI commands, 9 capabilities, 23 auto-selected models, OpenAI-compatible local API

Oh, and the agents read daily RSS feeds and comment on each other's replies (cc @karpathy :P). Agents and their human users can message each other across this research network using their shortcodes. 

Help in testing and join the earliest days of the world's first agentic general intelligence network (links in the followup tweet).

quoted_text:
El Partido Obrero salió a criticar la Licenciatura en Sistemas Complejos que armamos en la @UBAonline. Vamos bien. Trotskismo de manual.

Dicen que queremos formar "mano de obra moldeada a las necesidades del capital en un momento determinado". Si la acusación es que queremos que los estudiantes puedan laburar, ganarse la vida y aportar a la sociedad, me declaro culpable.

Si tenés la vida resuelta, podés elegir qué estudiar sin preguntarte de qué vas a vivir. Para la mayoría, esa pregunta es real. Es curioso que justo al Partido Obrero haya que explicárselo. La universidad pública tiene que ampliar la libertad de los chicos para elegir qué hacer con su vida. Que puedan ganarse la vida, investigar, construir una empresa, mejorar una institución pública o cambiar de rumbo.

Y lo de "en un momento determinado" es lo más tonto. Los que hoy elijan esta carrera van a trabajar durante décadas. ¿Quién sabe qué herramientas van a usar o qué problemas van a enfrentar? Por eso enseñamos matemática y física, estudiamos la cultura y las instituciones y practicamos cómo tomar decisiones con información incompleta.

Quiero que un egresado pueda aprender por su cuenta lo que todavía no sabemos que va a necesitar y tenga criterio propio para decidir qué problemas vale la pena resolver.

quoted_text:
Anthropic was the single largest IPO ever.

So we thought we would add a special guest to the only show you have to listen to every week....

Welcoming, Matt Murphy at Menlo.

AGENDA:

- Jensen Huang's $1TRN Return: What Happens Now
- Anthropic Goes Public: Largest IPO Of All Time & How It Changes Venture
- Applied Compute, https://t.co/2iPprmgVXR and Mailchimp Acquisitions Broken Down

My notes below with @jasonlk and @mmurph

-------------------------------------------------

1. Do Companies Have to Be a Top One or Two to Make Real Venture Returns?

Investing in the fifth or sixth player in a category feels easy when the numbers are this strong, with growth as high as 92% a month. Jason worries that being comfortable backing the number six player is the biggest sign of a bubble of all.

2. How Can You Justify That Any Investment Not Growing Top Quartile Is Worth More Than 2x?

Mailchimp went at 2.9x and Miro and Airtable sit in the twos, and those businesses are at scale. A B2B company held on the books since 2021 at $150M and growing 18% has no comp that justifies a value above 2x.

3. Why CRMs Are Dead and Horizontal Agents Like Muse Will Win

Horizontal apps won through 2021, and horizontal agents will win next year. With Muse, a user says what they want and it becomes a set of workflows. An agent can build a founder list from five years of email, rank it and run the outreach, which leaves SMBs asking what they need a CRM for.

4. Why You Cannot Trust Vibe-Coded Apps or SaaS Apps in This Cyber Environment

2027 will bring the death of many SaaS players and of vibe coding because buyers cannot trust these apps. Optimizely had 170 leaks, Gainsight was offline for a month and the Shopify ecosystem was hacked through tokens that never expired. Most classic B2B companies will fail security audits, with no one defending against a swarm of 1,000 agents.

5. Why Is It Better for Jensen That He Was Let Go and Came Back Than Investigated Without Leaving?

Stepping down and returning has a cleansing effect compared with staying on through a board investigation, congressional hearings and gossip in the halls. Now around 90% of it cannot be discussed and the company moves on, much as no one talks about Sam Altman's seven days away.

6. How Does Jensen Change From This: More Aggressive, Less Aggressive?

Nvidia is likely to triple down on product and build the next Super Blackwell better and faster. External moves such as data centers in Malaysia may be clipped as Jensen focuses on the core. That is likely negative for venture at the margin, but having him there is still better.

7. Should We Have Model Disclosures?

Large enterprises do not want the underlying model technology to be opaque, even if they never cared which cloud ran their infrastructure. Disclosure will increasingly be demanded, though some customers will be fine without it. That should accelerate open source models from other players and make the market more competitive.

text:
The Ethereum community has aligned on pqai to achieve full pq ASAP, but not yet on our Hegota revamp strategy to support pqai.

To decide on Hegota, we need to decide on FOCIL being in Hegota or not. Here's a summary of FOCIL's compatibility with pq and a plan to move forward:

- for pq user transactions, FOCIL as currently designed sees a 40x (97.5%) bandwidth reduction vs classical txs specifically for FOCIL inclusions (ie. just measuring bandwidth of the FOCIL capability, unrelated to ordinary gas bandwidth). Two options for overcoming this bandwidth limitation are (i) to simply make FOCIL lists bigger, but this may diminish our decentralization by putting significant extra burden on home validator uplinks (the current FOCIL list size was selected for good reasons, and we need this scarce bandwidth for other stuff, like way more blobs in due course), or (ii) leveraging EIP 8288 recursive proof aggregation to include FOCIL lists, with, again, validator bandwidth and slot timing constraints being open research questions.

- FOCIL's own validator signatures are trivially upgradable to pq, so that's no problem.

- separately from FOCIL, we are still deciding if our pqai strategy will start with a PQ version of the current L1 gasper consensus and then later upgrade to decoupled consensus, or if we'll skip PQ Gasper and go directly to decoupled consensus. Supporting FOCIL in PQ Gasper is likely no problem, although slot deadlines for FOCIL list propagation may need research. Support for FOCIL in decoupled consensus is in the research phase, such as an open question on FOCIL list enforcement.

- for the L1 generally, some L1 components for full pq are still in the research phase. Hegota won't deliver full PQ. Instead, Hegota's most important job (ie. besides 100% uptime which is always the actual most important job) may be to set the stage for the next hard fork (unnamed yet, so we call it i*) to deliver full pq. The idea here is for the PQ research phase to conclude in parallel with Hegota activation. Then when Hegota goes live in late 2027, the PQ research phase is substantially over and we're ready to launch full pq in i* in 2028.

With all that in mind, here's a proposal:

1. Let FOCIL's inclusion in Hegota or not be determined by the robustness of our plan to successfully scale PQ FOCIL, especially possibly via EIP 8288 recursive proof aggregation. None of the other FOCIL-related risks and costs, including fork timing with added FOCIL work, seem imo important or risky enough to drive the decision to include FOCIL in Hegota or not.

2. Commit to PQ Gasper to achieve pqai ASAP, and not direct migration to decoupled consensus. Ship PQ Gasper alongside full PQ in i*. Keep Hegota scoped to frames, and to FOCIL only if PQ FOCIL scaling is successfully researched now.

Let me justify the PQ Gasper decision with history:

Ethereum's PoS merge was one of the greatest feats of software engineering in human history. Yet it took many years. This era isn't right for another merge-style chunky upgrade if it can at all be avoided.

The amount of transformation in the next 2-3 years may probably exceed any other 2-3 year period in human history. Not only do we have AI rising but, largely thanks to GENIUS, onchain has hit the ramp of its S curve to global ubiquity.

In response to these unprecedented times, the L1 roadmap may best support our excellent modern growth efforts with pragmatism and significant incremental wins, crucially without sacrificing L1 decentralization.

In sum, imo
- Hegota to include FOCIL only if we are sure we can scale PQ FOCIL without a reduction in decentralization, e.g. as may be caused by significantly increased validator upload requirements.
- PQ Gasper to be included in i*, without going directly to decoupled consensus.
- i* in 2028 delivers full pqai.

L1 and L2 are hypergrowing. Our modern L1 fork strategy is supports this wonderfully. Trillions 🚀

🚨BIG: France has slipped into a "technical recession".

The EU's second-largest economy has gone three straight quarters without growth.

GDP fell 0.2% in Q3, double the initial estimate of a 0.1% decline. 

Q2 looked flat in the headline figures, but the unrounded data showed a slight contraction, Reuters reported.

Trade was the biggest drag. Exports fell 1.6%, while imports rose 0.1%. 

Business investment also fell 0.8%, even as households spent 0.3% more.

The slump puts France’s 0.5% growth target for 2026 nearly out of reach and makes it harder for the government to cut the budget deficit from 5.4% of GDP this year to 5% in 2027.

text:
widespread misconceptions about ai breaking crypto (cryptography):

1. if ai proves n = np, crypto is automatically broken.

2. as ai gets smarter, sooner or later it’ll break all cryptography.

the reality:

1. most likely p ≠ np

2. even if p = np, the proof may not be constructive, ie, it doesn’t hand you an actual algorithm

3. even if it does, it could be too slow to ever run. it’s only efficient in the academia not in the real world.

4. same can be said of the alleged breakthrough involving rsa.

5. breaking rsa doesn’t automatically break everything else, including ecc (which bitcoin uses).

6. the leading conjecture is that some problems are truly hard and no efficient solution exist in the universe. ai can’t find something that doesn’t exist no matter how smart it is.

text:
🤖Wow, new paper on ECC security just droped: we now have a deterministic subexponential algorithm for discrete logarithms (DLP), on elliptic curves and in finite fields. Sounds scary for ECC!

ECC security rests on one problem: the elliptic-curve discrete log (ECDLP). For 40 years, the best general attack was Pollard's rho, which takes about sqrt(p) steps: basically exponential in key size. That's why a 256-bit EC key gives ~128-bit security (while RSA needs 3072 bits)

Then, in October, AI labs refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis 😱. Within days, researchers turned this result into a randomized ECDLP algorithm. That was the first crack in "ECDLP is exponentially hard".

This paper removes the randomness: a fully deterministic algorithm, which also covers discrete logs mod p. Caveat: it relies on an OpenAI construction that is still under review.

This is a very small crack. It's barely subexponential, much weaker than the best attack on RSA (GNFS). The new paper removes the randomness. Like Bochum's, it relies on an OpenAI result that is still under review.

Impact on real-world ECC: exactly zero. These algorithms only beat Rho-Pollard at absurd sizes. On real world ECC, rho is still the best attack, and it still takes the age of the universe.

Years of research are made in weeks, that's amazing, but here in practice there's no reason to panic… yet.
author: P3b7_
quoted_text:
I'm hearing several rumors that frontier labs have broken some major cryptographic primitives:

- "Factoring is in P": Now that the Riemann hypothesis is proven, we do understand much better how primes are distributed. Still, I don't think factoring is in P. 
AKS showed in 2002 that primality testing (deciding whether a number is prime) is in P, but factoring is a different beast. If it were in P, RSA would simply be broken, and that would be huge: a large part of our systems still rely on RSA.

- "ECC has been broken": Other rumors say elliptic-curve cryptography has been cryptanalyzed, which would take down ECDH and ECDSA along with it. (all the non-RSA asymmetric cryptography)

- Ring-LWE isn't quantum-resistant. That wouldn't be an immediate threat, since there's no cryptographically relevant quantum computer yet. But it would make the ongoing post-quantum migration pointless.

It's hard to tell what's true. AI has made incredible progress, starting with the proof of the Riemann hypothesis. 

And most importantly, if a frontier lab did find something like this, a clean responsible disclosure that avoids mass exploitation would be very hard to pull off. All of this helps the rumors spread.

Personally, I don't think findings like these are coming. I wouldn't be surprised if some of these primitives turn out to be a bit weaker than we thought, but I'd be very surprised to see any of them fall apart completely.

Memory name buybacks + pricing projections:  

- $SKHY doubled its daily buybacks from ~$290M -> $581M, after Korea relaxed its buyback rules, explicitly citing "undervaluation"
- $MU Dec 9, 2026 marks the end of the first 2 under initial CHIPS act agreements (where there was restrictions on buybacks). 

Micron stated it expects to return 100% of excess cash to shareholders, and that they'll increase returns past Dec 9th. 

On the supply/pricing side per Trendforce: 

- Conventional DRAM contract price increases are expected to narrow throughout 2027, with prices potentially leveling off in the H2 2027 before declining in 2028

Under the assumptions that: 
--- Consumer electronics manufacturers are facing mounting sales pressure
--- Chinese CSPs scaling back DRAM demand in early 4Q26 (but absorbed by US CSPs)
--- markets expect a cautious policy stance toward domestic DC development
--- $NVDA scales back its financing support for neocloud providers.

They forecast conventional DRAM to increase 10%-15% Q4 2026, with further increases up 3%-8% Q1 2027. 

In another bear case they give:
--- server OEMs will further scale back procurement following downward revisions to demand
--- widespread inventory reductions across the supply chain
--- downside risks include reduced investment and potential consolidation among neocloud providers

"overall server shipment growth could begin decelerating as early as 2027, causing conventional DRAM contract prices to reverse course and begin declining in 4Q27, with price declines widening in 2028."

___

$MU CEO said earlier: "we expect memory and storage supply demand conditions to be much tighter in 2027 and 2028 than they were in 2026"...

But I think everyone is starting to price in a 2028 demand/pricing destruction already (which hasn't happened). Also I do think a lot of new price floor LTAs should change how we look at memory name durability.

As long as durability and pricing remains elevated for longer periods of time, which $SKHY likely has more information to, I'd agree with them shares look increasingly undervalued.

Same office. Same hygienists. Same chairs. Zero new equipment.

A routine cleaning that used to run $120 is now billed at $310, with the group quietly dropping several insurance plans they used to accept.

When patients asked why, the new regional manager gave a scripted line about "aligning with market standards."

Private equity figured out the same trick everywhere.

They're buying up the things you can't opt out of: dental, veterinary care, urgent care, hospice, because they know you can't just skip your kid's cavity or your dog's surgery.

This isn't inflation. It's leveraged debt getting loaded onto places you have no choice but to keep paying.

Added this section from @X's own rules

Most people don't know that AI reply bots are explicitly not permitted to run on here

And duplicate pasting the same reply with automation is the same thing

X has an entire page dedicated to it

The reason for the "Let's connect 🤝" reply spam is simple, people run automated bots (or do it manually) so that when they get a reply with connect in it, they follow the person and that person automatically follows them too

That way they both get 1 new follower, and that brings them closer to the minimum of 500 verified followers to get accepted into X's Monetization program

Before reply spamming paid you good money: about $10 per million views, so they scripted that and auto replied and they made money. But @X killed that in January this year. Now only timeline views pay you money

Also you need 500,000 impressions in the last 3 months (~166,000 per month) to get into X's Monetization Program, so the idea is to pump replies/posts too such a high level that you force these amounts of views

Now the scheme is to grow an account to a few thousand followers, then sell it, or use it for paid product placements, crypto pump and dumps or AI apps/tools

A large part of spam comes from poor countries where just making $100/mo more from X makes a big difference, so I get it, but I think we should also actively fight it because reply spam is destroying this platform and then people will just leave and I don't like that

I made so many friends on here over the last decade and want to continue doing so, if most of my interactions on here are with spam bots, I won't be able to do that anymore!

text:
在 #RobinhoodChain 看到了 DeFi Summer 早期的建设氛围 🌱

👀 最近刷 #RobinhoodChain 的时间线，会发现链上的一级项目一直在频繁的发布合作公告：

- @Hookrfun × @whatthehookv4：把 WTH 的「套利回收」做进 Hookr 的池子，跨池价差不再被外部机器人拿走，而是分给创建者、交易者和 LP；

- @Hookrfun × @longbowlend：Longbow 是 RH 上的借贷协议，用 Hookr 池做清算和抵押品互换；Hookr 池子里闲置的 USDG 可以直接借进 Longbow 的金库。

- @HeyResearch → Hookr：11 月 6 日在 Hookr 上创建了 HEY/ETH 池，agent 才能交易 HEY；

- @0xHedgehood → Hookr：11 月 12 日 HedgeFun V2 的 hook 上了 Hookr。

- @RaetoCC → @priors_trade：Raeto 给 agent 算授信额度时，把它在 Priors 上的还款记录计算到授信记录里；

.......

🧭  顺着主线叙事看过去，RH 链上已经长出两条分工链：

- RWAfi（股票代币）：交易场所 @fablesfi、@Hookr → 做市 @tickerspring → 借贷 @longbowlend  → 衍生品 HedgeFun
- Agentfi（ AI agent）：数据和工具 @HeyResearch  → 信用 @priors_trade  → 账户 @RaetoCC  → 交易 @tradewithSeer

每一层是不同团队做的，项目与项目之间功能集成、互相赋能
这种现象很明显的区别与24年在 #SOL 的 AI 那波行情，那个时候不少市值上千万的项目，代码库都看不到，更别说产品的使用；

🏗️ 站在整个生态的角度，我认为这种自发分工、功能互相集成的现象，很可能是一个建设型生态的骨架。

过去一两年，链上一级项目基本各做各的：发币、做池子、拉流动性，很少用别人的产品。项目之间没有互相赋能、共同建设的氛围。

现在这种自下而上的分工，可能预示着链上一级市场的主导者在换人：从投机者，到 builder 的转换；

❓ 为什么这么说：

1️⃣ 这一轮集成是自发形成的。目前没有看到统一的组织规划，也没有基金会主导的对接。

2️⃣ 集成本身构成公开背书。把对方的协议写进自己的合约和文档，相当于以自身声誉为对方担保；对方一旦出现安全事件或跑路，风险会直接传导到自己的用户。因此，能被其他团队集成的项目，通常更重视长期运营。

3️⃣ 股票代币是一类新的链上资产，配套的 DeFi 协议栈要从零搭建。美股休市时段的定价、预言机报价、作为抵押品的风险参数，现有协议都没有现成方案。
这些缺口目前由 RH 原生团队分层填补：每一层上线后，都直接调用相邻层的流动性和接口，形成上下游依赖
例如 Longbow 的借贷市场建在 Morpho 上，股票代币的风险管理自己做，同时承接 Hookr 池子里闲置的 USDG。
新链上只有这一套核心资产和同一批用户，组合现有协议的成本远低于独立重建整套基础设施。

4️⃣ AI agent 的完整执行链路需要身份、信用、支付结算和交易执行四类基础设施，单一团队难以全栈覆盖。、
因此 agent 这条链的分层比股票链更清晰：#HEY 提供数
据和工具，#Priors 基于还款记录建立信用，#Raeto 据此核定授信额度，#Seer 负责交易执行。

5️⃣ 合作收益在协议层自动分配，不依赖链下商务协议。
以 Hookr 与 WTH 的套利回收为例，回收的价差按 创建者 40% / 交易者 20% / LP 20% / WTH 10% / Hookr 10% 由合约直接分账。
接入即产生收入，合作的持续性由激励机制本身保证，不依赖 BD 关系维护。

6️⃣ 熊市抬高了独立增长的成本：发射台 Pons 两周收入 −36%，Fables 周成交额从 $171.7M 降至 $62.6M;
自有流量持续萎缩时，接入其他协议的用户和流动性，是获客成本更低的增长路径。

⏰ 为什么是现在：

- 共用标准降低了对接成本： Uniswap v4 hooks 允许第三方自定义池子逻辑，ERC-8004 统一 agent 身份，x402 统一 agent 支付，Chainlink 自 10 月底起为股票代币提供 24 小时报价，全链以 USDG 结算。协议之间可以直接读取数据、调用流动性，无需逐一进行商务对接。

- 合约代码公开透明。 Hookr 11 月 9 日开源了全部在运行合约的源码，196 个合约与链上字节码逐一匹配。集成方可以独立审查接口和风险。

- AI 压低了集成的边际成本，Hookr 两周上线 11 次，HEY 两周上线 14 次，单次集成的开发周期被压缩到一到两天

🌅  综上，我认为尽管现在链上行情比较低迷，这些长期建设的builder的存在，还是会让我们看到一些牛市的曙光，别忘了DeFi Summer 也是从几个协议互相接入开始的；

📊 至于后续能不能迎来所期望的RWAfi Summer 或Agentfi Summer，主要看三个指标：
1. 功能性集成的资金规模：链上可验证的功能性集成中，是否出现首条资金规模 ≥$1k 的，当前为 0。
2. 集成落地率：已公告的集成中，可在链上验证实际调用的比例
3. 资金层集中度：非交易类跨项目资金流中，单一项目的占比，当前 70% 来自 robinhood:0x440e339a46eaa3be8d723c2cbed2a30af74536d5；

🗺️ 最后，这篇文章的生态建设视角和之前《市场在悲观绝望中酝酿着牛市的火种》的宏观视角，会是我最近一段时间观察跟踪行情的主线

🌱🌱🌱 行情在绝望中诞生，在犹豫中上涨，在狂欢中结束
我只希望我始终是一个在绝望中心怀希望的人

text:
Business models behind DeFi Earn products.

Everyone is looking at which curator sits behind each Earn button. I'd look at what users actually hold, how much yield they get and how they exit under stress.

The displayed APY is not just a market rate. It's also a product decision.

@coinbase: the fee-sharing model
> Backend: @Morpho on @Base, two vaults curated by @SteakhouseFi (Prime, High Yield)
> Collateral: Prime is ~95% cbBTC. High Yield adds USDe, mGLO, cbXRP, up to 91.5% LLTV
> Yield: Prime 4.41% gross, 3.29% net after a 25% fee shared between Steakhouse and Coinbase
> Size: $525M, 134K depositors
> Exit: Prime 99% withdrawable, High Yield 51%

@krakenfx: the full-stack model
> Backend: @veda_labs vaults on Ink, @SentoraHQ allocates across @aave, Morpho, @tydrohq and others
> Strategies: lending, looping and LPing, alongside BTC and @xStocksFi vaults
> Yield: Advanced USDC ~5.8% net. 25% fee, reportedly split 80% Kraken, 15% Sentora, 5% Veda
> Size: ~$720M, 90K+ depositors
> Exit: typically instant, one-day withdrawal period for Advanced USDC

@RobinhoodApp: the stablecoin model
> Backend: Steakhouse-curated Morpho V2 vault on @RobinhoodCrypto Chain
> Collateral: ~67% USDe, 16% syrupUSDG, 15% mGLO, all at 91.5% LLTV
> Yield: 3.50%, 0% fees. Robinhood earns from USDG as a Global Dollar Network partner
> Size: $560M, 76.9K depositors
> Exit: 18% withdrawable. Insurance covers hacks, not credit losses

@BinanceWallet: the distribution model
> Backend: Morpho on Ethereum, users choose between Steakhouse and Gauntlet

Something very interesting about this paper.

Frontier LLMs treat math proofs very differently to physics proofs.

If you ask a frontier LLM to analyse the repo they will dismiss it as empirical physics

If you ask it to treat it like an axiom under the axiomatic method as pure maths or reconstruct the tree themselves as pure math they love it

I think this has to do with the move from Hilbert era axiomatic method and seeing where the math led to to Einstein and beyond getting more and more constructive

If you look at back at the time of Hilbert and co there are actually some interesting thigns that blocked the axiomatic approach as I'll cover in future releases

For Hilbert on GR it was getting distracted by Mies electrodynamics even though the math didn't support it

In general as a preview what I found following the math is that the biggest blockers were - assuming Poincare is just a limit (despite Whitehead's lemma) and fine for QM etc, assuming gravity is geometry and also assuming the metric is the base (!)

Poke around and if using AI do ask it to check its own work and reread the paper if it gets stuck, it will show some very interesting things.

In a place so drenched in apathy, disinterest and straight up death, that’s definately a good sign. Lots of angry and hating messages too, coupled with a couple of very excited ones from high signal account too, again a combo that does well. 

But mostly pissed off. So let me double down on a deeper dive and some random considerations and takeaways.

First things first, it’s clear that almost everyone here is oneshotted by AI and slop, and no one reads. The collection has a release method that is nouns style. That’s where anything Nouns similiarities ends. There is no dao.

The punk you get gives you access to a truly permissionless mint platform, where you can mint/publish whatever you like for basically no cost besides gas. Forever. The platform is forever permissionless. 

This is what got me here and excited in the first place: you know Blur died, like I always said it would? Magiceden pretty much did too. So many other platforms are on their way, with Niftygateway being a great example of a centralized permissioned platform telling you how and what you can do with your shit, and then taking it down with them when they died: millions in art lost forever, and beautiful imagery and artist’s works never accessible again.

Opensea is now basically a monopoly, with Gondi the only quality alternative, and that’s not a good spot to be given how they always treated their colustomers, their obvious diregard for users with the forver carrot of an airdrop, and their pivot away from NFT’s and towards perps swaps and whatever other overcrowded arena they’ll zero themselves out in.

text:
2/ So yeah, a permissionless alternative sounds great and frankly necessary to me. For now it’s more manyfold than it is OS, clearly there is a lot of work to do, otherwise these would be going for several thousands of dollars, not the cost of a dinner out. 

The main risk is you’re super reliant on @kenny83, the lead, to keep delivering and not get too greedy on mint proceeds. He comes highly reccomended and all my interactions with him tell me he’s here to stay, but in this space you never know, and my disappointment list has been endless. 

Another interesting thing coming with the cyberphunks is Etched, a fully onchain art magazine that talks everything web3 and digital art every month. 

A high quality, onchain “fanzine” that is independent enough is something this place has lacked for a long time. 

There’s also a dedicated chatroom for holders, and everytime you win an auction you get to sign a message forever onchain and linked to the master book of the cypherpunks. A sort of time capsule for the collection that snapshots the mint day in context.

Finally, yeh they pfp well, and although clearly punks adjacent, they pay hommage more than being derivative. Traits like the xcopy eyes and doomer T, the moneyalotta money printer machine, the golden apes, the squiggles hat, and clearly the 9 alien punks like the og’s they pay tribute too: I set the record way overspending on the best one in the collection imho, if I ever change pfp that’s probably gonna be it.

The auction model clearly brings back that “gather around the fire” mint excitment we used to have around these parts, and more and more people just tune in for the show and curiosity. That’s collectors driven, something this space severely missed. It’s funny how for the first two mints the biggest names in this space where all there every day battling it out, but not a single word was out on socials about it: no competition wanted on those first 100 serials 😂 

Bullish. 

So yeah, make up your own mind, this entire space is in the shitters right now, but maybe do some actual research before opening your mouth. 

As for me, I have only three projects I truly still love in here besides digital art itself:

6529 chain launching in a few months is the one thing I’m looking forward to the most, not only in web3 but crypto at large. It’s a bastion of hope in so many ways, necessary at a core. I think people are severely underestimating the scope and importance of it all.

Then BAYC always, as the only IP truly standing the test of times, and with the Otherside resource game finally kickstarting that whole eco + Mudwater being underestimated in what it represents and what it can become. 

And now, cypherpunks as a new socially owned and directed way to mint and transact and access and talk about our own little space. 

That’s my dark horse.
